short_description.id: Dalam cerita rakyat Kanada, Igopogo adalah makhluk legendaris yang konon tinggal di Lake Simcoe, Ontario; namanya disebut didasarkan pada Ogopogo dari Lake Okanagan.
short_description.en: In Canadian folklore, the Igopogo is a legendary creature said to live in Lake Simcoe, Ontario; its name is ostensibly based on the Ogopogo of Lake Okanagan.

long_description.id: Dalam cerita rakyat Kanada, Igopogo adalah makhluk legendaris yang konon tinggal di Lake Simcoe, Ontario. Namanya disebut didasarkan pada Ogopogo dari Lake Okanagan, British Columbia, dan juga pada judul buku I Go Pogo tahun 1952. Julukannya antara lain Beaverton Bessie, dari kota Beaverton, dan Kempenfelt Kelly, dari teluk yang menjorok dari danau ke kota Barrie.
long_description.en: In Canadian folklore the Igopogo is a legendary creature said to live in Lake Simcoe, Ontario. Its name is said to derive from the Ogopogo of Lake Okanagan in British Columbia and from the title of the 1952 book I Go Pogo. Its nicknames include Beaverton Bessie, after the town of Beaverton, and Kempenfelt Kelly, after the bay that reaches from the lake into the city of Barrie.

long_description.id: Penampakan pertama yang dikreditkan terjadi pada 1823: David Soules, seorang pemukim awal, dilaporkan melihat makhluk panjang yang meninggalkan riak di air dan jejak di lumpur saat menggembala domba. Sumber lain menyebut penampakan penting pada 1952 dan 1963, pembacaan sonar atas hewan besar pada 1983, dan rekaman video pada 1991 tentang hewan mirip anjing laut.
long_description.en: The first sighting credited to the creature came in 1823, when David Soules, an early settler, reportedly saw, while herding sheep, a long creature that left a wake on the water and a track in the mud. Another source lists important sightings in 1952 and 1963, a sonar reading of a large animal in 1983, and a 1991 videotape of a seal-like animal.

long_description.id: Gambaran tentang Igopogo berbeda-beda. George M. Eberhart menggambarkannya sebagai hewan abu-abu mirip anjing laut sepanjang 12–70 kaki (3,7–21,3 m), berwajah seperti anjing atau kuda, bermata menonjol, bermulut menganga, bersirip punggung, dan berekor seperti ikan. Menurut John Robert Colombo, tidak ada dua deskripsi Kempenfelt Kelly yang sama.
long_description.en: Accounts of the Igopogo differ. George M. Eberhart pictures it as a gray, seal-like animal between 12 and 70 feet (3.7–21.3 m) long, with a face like a dog or a horse, prominent eyes, a gaping mouth, dorsal fins and a fishlike tail. According to John Robert Colombo, no two descriptions of Kempenfelt Kelly coincide.

long_description.id: Sebagian penulis menduga bahwa penampakan itu sebenarnya hewan seperti anjing laut atau berang-berang. Penulis sebuah artikel berita menyatakan banyak laporan dapat dijelaskan sebagai berang-berang yang berenang berjajar, dan pencarian mereka berakhir tanpa bukti yang baik. Pembacaan sonar tahun 1983 juga dibantah sebagian orang yang menyebutnya gerombolan ikan.
long_description.en: Some writers suggest the sightings were really seals or otters. The author of a news article says many reports could be explained as otters swimming in a line, and that their search ended without good evidence. The 1983 sonar reading has also been disputed by some who say it was a school of fish.

short_description.id: Ikatere ("ikan cepat") adalah dewa ikan dalam mitologi Māori dan Polinesia, bapa semua makhluk laut, yang memilih membawa anak-anaknya ke laut saat badai Tāwhirimātea.
short_description.en: Ikatere ("fast fish") is a fish god in Māori and Polynesian mythology, father of all sea creatures, who chose to take his children to the sea during Tāwhirimātea's storms.

long_description.id: Dalam mitologi Māori dan Polinesia, Ikatere (juga ditulis Ika-tere, "ikan cepat") adalah dewa ikan, bapa semua makhluk laut, termasuk putri duyung. Ia putra Punga, cucu Tangaroa, dan saudara Tū-te-wehiwehi. Dalam salah satu catatan awal, Tangaroa memperanakkan Punga dan Punga memperanakkan Ika-tere, bapa ikan, serta Tu-te-wehiwehi, bapa reptil.
long_description.en: Ikatere (also written Ika-tere, "fast fish") is a fish god of Māori and Polynesian mythology and the father of all sea creatures, mermaids included. He is the son of Punga, grandson of Tangaroa and brother of Tū-te-wehiwehi. One early record has Tangaroa begetting Punga and Punga begetting Ika-tere, father of fish, and Tu-te-wehiwehi, father of reptiles.

long_description.id: Ketika Tāwhirimātea (dewa badai) berperang melawan saudara-saudaranya karena pemisahan Rangi dan Papa, Ikatere dan Tū-te-wehiwehi harus lari demi bertahan hidup. Keduanya berselisih apakah harus tinggal di laut atau pergi ke darat: Ikatere memilih membawa anak-anaknya, ikan, ke laut, sedangkan Tū-te-wehiwehi membawa anak-anaknya, reptil, ke darat.
long_description.en: When Tāwhirimātea (god of storms) went to war with his brothers over the separation of Rangi and Papa, Ikatere and Tū-te-wehiwehi had to flee to survive. They argued about whether to remain in the sea or head for the land: Ikatere kept his children, the fish, in the sea, while Tū-te-wehiwehi took his children, the reptiles, ashore.

long_description.id: Dalam versi itu, kedua ras itu segera berpisah, ikan lari ke laut dan reptil mencari selamat di hutan dan semak. Ika-tere memperingatkan Tu-te-wehiwehi bahwa sisik mereka akan dihanguskan di atas seikat pakis kering sebelum dimasak, dan Tu-te-wehiwehi menjawab bahwa ras yang mencari selamat di laut kelak diletakkan di atas makanan nabati untuk memberi cita rasa. Pepatah "Tāua ki uta, tāua ki te wai" ("Kita di darat, kita di laut") merujuk pada pilihan mereka.
long_description.en: In that version the two races parted at once, the fish fleeing to the sea and the reptiles seeking safety in the forests and scrubs. Ika-tere warned Tu-te-wehiwehi that their scales would be singed off over a wisp of dry fern before being cooked, and Tu-te-wehiwehi answered that the race seeking safety in the sea would be laid on top of vegetable food to give it a relish. A Māori saying, "Tāua ki uta, tāua ki te wai", alludes to their choices.

short_description.id: Jarita adalah burung betina Sarngika yang kisahnya terdapat dalam Mahabharata. Ia membesarkan empat putra Mandapala dan melindungi mereka ketika hutan Khandava terbakar.
short_description.en: Jarita is a female Sarngika bird whose story appears in the Mahabharata. She raised Mandapala's four sons and protected them when the Khandava forest burned.

long_description.id: Jarita adalah burung betina Sarngika yang kisahnya terdapat dalam Mahabharata. Dalam teks itu, seorang Resi berwujud burung Sarngaka berhubungan dengannya, dan dari Jarita lahir empat putra yang semuanya pelafal Weda. Mandapala mengambil bentuk burung jantan dan memiliki empat anak dengannya, lalu meninggalkannya; ia pergi kepada istri lain bernama Lapita ketika anak-anaknya masih berada dalam telur.
long_description.en: Jarita is a female Sarngika bird whose story appears in the Mahabharata. In the text a Rishi in the form of a Sarngaka bird had connection with her, and she bore four sons who were all reciters of the Vedas. Mandapala took the form of a male bird and had four sons with her, then abandoned her; he went to another wife called Lapita while his sons were still in their eggs.

long_description.id: Jarita membesarkan anak-anaknya sendiri, sambil menjalani cara hidup yang wajar bagi jenisnya. Ketika Mandapala melihat Agni datang untuk membakar hutan Khandava, ia memuji Agni dan memohon agar anak-anaknya dibiarkan hidup. Itulah sebabnya, menurut teks itu, Agni tidak berkobar untuk membinasakan anak-anak Mandapala saat melahap hutan itu. Menurut satu sumber, anak-anaknya akhirnya diselamatkan melalui pengaruh Mandapala atas dewa api.
long_description.en: Jarita brought up her children herself, following the pursuits proper to her own species. When Mandapala saw Agni coming to burn the forest of Khandava he praised Agni and asked him to spare his children. For that reason, according to the text, Agni did not blaze forth to destroy Mandapala's children while consuming the forest. In the end, according to one account, Mandapala's influence over the fire god rescued her young.

long_description.id: Ketika api berkobar di hutan Khandava, Jarita yang tak berdaya menangis karena tahu anak-anaknya terlalu kecil untuk melarikan diri; ia mengatakan akan menutupi mereka dengan sayapnya dan mati bersama mereka, dan mengusulkan lubang tikus di dekat pohon sebagai tempat berlindung. Ia mengenang kata-kata ayah mereka tentang keempat putranya: Jaritari, Sarisrikka, Stamvamitra, dan Drona.
long_description.en: When the fire blazed in the forest of Khandava the helpless Jarita wept because she knew her children were too young to escape; she said she would cover them with her wings and die with them, and proposed a mouse's hole near the tree as shelter. She recalls their father's words about the four sons: Jaritari, Sarisrikka, Stamvamitra and Drona.

short_description.id: Jinmenju ("pohon berwajah manusia") adalah yōkai dan yaoguai dalam cerita rakyat Jepang dan Tiongkok berupa pohon dengan bunga menyerupai kepala manusia.
short_description.en: Jinmenju ("human-faced tree") is a yōkai and yaoguai of Japanese and Chinese folklore, a tree whose flowers resemble human heads.

long_description.id: Jinmenju, juga disebut Ninmenju, adalah sejenis yōkai dan yaoguai dalam cerita rakyat Jepang dan Tiongkok. Ia umumnya digambarkan sebagai pohon yang berbunga menyerupai kepala manusia, dan antara lain muncul dalam Konjaku Hyakki Shūi karya Toriyama Sekien dari zaman Edo. Teks penjelasnya menyebut bahwa di lembah pegunungan bunganya seperti kepala manusia, tanpa kata hanya tersenyum terus sampai kelopaknya gugur.
long_description.en: Jinmenju, also called Ninmenju, belongs to the yōkai and yaoguai of Japanese and Chinese folklore. It is usually shown as a tree whose blossoms look like human heads, and it appears prominently in the Edo-period Konjaku Hyakki Shūi by Toriyama Sekien. Its explanatory text says that in mountain valleys the flowers are like human heads, and without a word they just keep smiling until their petals fall.

long_description.id: Sumber lain yang menyebutnya mencakup Wakan Sansai Zue dan kutipan dari Sancai Tuhui Tiongkok, yang menggambarkan pohon serupa dari negeri bernama Dashiguo. Menurut Sancai Tuhui, bila pohon itu ditanyai, bunganya tertawa tetapi tidak memahami bahasa manusia, dan bila terlalu banyak tertawa bunganya layu dan jatuh. Rōō Sawa, kumpulan kisah ganjil dari Aizu, juga mengutip Sancai Tuhui tentang pohon ini.
long_description.en: Other sources that name it include the Wakan Sansai Zue and a passage drawn from the Chinese Sancai Tuhui, which tells of a comparable tree in a country named Dashiguo. According to the Sancai Tuhui, if the tree is questioned its flowers laugh but do not understand human language, and if they laugh too much they wither and fall. The Rōō Sawa, an Aizu anthology of strange tales, likewise cites the Sancai Tuhui on this tree.

long_description.id: Sebuah kamus Jepang mendefinisikan jinmenju sebagai pohon berbuah sebesar buah ume yang konon berbiji seperti wajah manusia. Wikipedia bahasa Jepang menyebutnya sebagai pohon dalam tradisi Tiongkok dan menjelaskan bahwa gambar dalam Konjaku Hyakki Shūi menggambarkan pohon dari negeri Daishikoku yang dikutip Wakan Sansai Zue dari Sancai Tuhui.
long_description.en: A Japanese dictionary defines the jinmenju as a fruit-bearing tree whose fruit, about the size of an ume plum, is said to have a pit like a human face. Japanese Wikipedia calls it a tree of Chinese tradition and explains that the picture in the Konjaku Hyakki Shūi depicts a tree from the land of Daishikoku that the Wakan Sansai Zue quotes from the Sancai Tuhui.

short_description.id: Kallana adalah sebutan masyarakat Kaani untuk gajah kerdil yang mereka klaim hidup di hutan Western Ghats, Kerala; keberadaannya sebagai jenis tersendiri belum dipastikan secara ilmiah.
short_description.en: Kallana is the Kaani name for a dwarf elephant they claim lives in the forests of the Western Ghats in Kerala; its existence as a distinct variety has not been scientifically ascertained.

long_description.id: Kallana adalah dugaan spesies gajah kerdil yang konon ditemukan di India Selatan. Suku Kaani di hutan hujan Western Ghats (Kerala, India) mengklaim ada dua jenis gajah di kawasan hutan Peppara: gajah India biasa dan jenis kerdil yang mereka sebut kallana. Nama itu berasal dari kata kallu, batu atau bongkahan batu, dan aana, gajah, karena gajah yang lebih kecil lebih sering terlihat di dataran tinggi yang berbatu.
long_description.en: Kallana is a suspected dwarf elephant said to occur in South India. Kaani tribal people living in the rainforests of the Western Ghats (Kerala, India) say that the Peppara forest range holds two kinds of elephant: the ordinary Indian one and a dwarf type they call kallana. The name joins kallu, meaning stones or boulders, with aana, meaning elephant, since the smaller animal is met more often on higher, rocky ground.

long_description.id: Pada 17 Maret 2010, Mallan Kani memandu fotografer Benny Ajantha ke seekor kallana dan ia memotretnya; hal itu dimuat di harian Malayala Manorama, tetapi seekor harus ditangkap dan diuji untuk memastikan apakah itu spesies terpisah.
long_description.en: On 17 March 2010 Mallan Kani led the photographer Benny Ajantha to a kallana and he photographed it; the Malayalam daily Malayala Manorama carried the report, but an animal would have to be caught and tested to tell whether it is a separate species.

long_description.id: Keberadaan jenis gajah kerdil di India belum dipastikan secara ilmiah. Sebagian ahli menilai semua penampakan berupa hewan tunggal, yang bisa menandakan kelainan genetik, bukan spesies terpisah. Pada 2013 seekor individu kerdil Elephas maximus teramati di Taman Nasional Udawalawe, Sri Lanka selatan, dan terdokumentasi secara ilmiah; sebuah catatan ilmiah menyebutnya catatan pertama gajah Asia dewasa liar dengan dwarfisme tidak proporsional, jantan setinggi sedikit lebih dari lima kaki dengan tubuh atas normal tetapi kaki sangat pendek.
long_description.en: The existence of a pygmy elephant type in India has not yet been scientifically confirmed. Some experts observe that every sighting involved a lone animal, which might point to a genetic abnormality instead of a separate species. In 2013 a dwarf Elephas maximus was seen and scientifically documented in Udawalawe National Park in southern Sri Lanka; one scientific note calls it the first record of a free-ranging adult wild Asian elephant with disproportionate dwarfism, a male just over five feet tall with a normal upper body but very short legs.

short_description.id: Kasha adalah yōkai Jepang yang dikisahkan mencuri jenazah.
short_description.en: Kasha is a Japanese yōkai said to steal corpses.

long_description.id: Kasha adalah yōkai Jepang yang dikisahkan mencuri jenazah. Penggambaran sekarang kerap menyerupai kucing, sedangkan bentuk awal lebih mirip iblis. Makna awal kasha ialah kendaraan api yang membawa pendosa ke neraka Buddhis.
long_description.en: Kasha is a Japanese yōkai said to steal corpses. Modern depictions are often cat-like while earlier forms were demon-like. The earlier kasha was a fiery vehicle carrying sinners to Buddhist hell.

long_description.id: Pada masa awal modern, kasha juga dipahami sebagai penjaga neraka atau dewa petir. Perpaduan dengan kisah nekomata yang mencuri mayat mendorong wujud kucingnya. Kemunculan kasha kerap dikaitkan dengan awan gelap dan guntur.
long_description.en: Early modern depictions also associated it with hell wardens or the thunder god. Conflation with corpse-stealing nekomata tales helped produce its cat form. Kasha is often associated with dark clouds and thunder.

long_description.id: Dalam penuturan lain, kasha adalah sejenis bake-neko: kucing besar berkaki dua yang sering disertai api neraka atau kilat dan suka muncul saat hujan atau badai, paling sering pada malam hari. Ia sering hidup di antara manusia dengan menyamar sebagai kucing biasa, lalu menampakkan wujud aslinya saat pemakaman untuk merebut jenazah dari peti. Menurut sumber ini, kasha dahulu kucing rumah biasa yang, setelah bertambah usia dan memiliki kekuatan gaib, berubah menjadi bake-neko, neko-mata, lalu kasha.
long_description.en: In another account the kasha is a type of bake-neko: a large bipedal cat often accompanied by hellish flames or lightning, fond of appearing in rain or storms, most often at night. It often lives among humans disguised as an ordinary cat and reveals its true form at funerals to snatch corpses from coffins. According to this source, kasha were once ordinary house cats that, as they aged and gained magical powers, turned into bake-neko, then neko-mata, then kasha.

long_description.id: Kasha kadang dipekerjakan sebagai utusan atau pelayan neraka untuk membawa jenazah orang jahat, dan pada kesempatan lain mencuri jenazah untuk dijadikan boneka atau dimakan. Beberapa daerah punya cara menangkalnya: di Yamagata para pendeta mengadakan upacara pemakaman palsu dengan peti berisi batu, dan di Okayama mereka memainkan myōhachi, sejenis simbal, untuk mengusirnya.
long_description.en: Kasha are occasionally employed as messengers or servants of hell to carry off the corpses of wicked people, and at other times steal corpses to animate as puppets or to eat. Some regions have ways to ward them off: in Yamagata priests hold a fake funeral with a casket full of rocks, and in Okayama they play the myōhachi, a type of cymbal, to keep them away.

note.en: Conflation with corpse-stealing nekomata tales is said to have produced the cat form of the kasha; another source places the neko-mata as a stage before the kasha.

statement.en: Kasha were once ordinary house cats; as cats age and their tails lengthen they develop magical powers, some becoming bake-neko, more powerful ones neko-mata, and beyond that some becoming kasha.

statement.en: The name kasha means "fire cart" and sometimes causes confusion with other yōkai, although kasha do not use vehicles of any kind.

short_description.id: Kayış, atau Kayış Baldır dan Kayış Bacak, adalah makhluk jahat berkaki seperti tali kulit dalam kepercayaan rakyat, yang menipu orang agar menggendongnya lalu menjadikan mereka budak; ceritanya dipakai untuk menakuti anak-anak.
short_description.en: Kayış, also called Kayış Baldır or Kayış Bacak, is a malevolent being with leather-strap legs in folk belief that tricks people into carrying it and then enslaves them; its story was used to frighten children.

long_description.id: Kayış adalah makhluk jahat yang dikenal juga dengan nama Kayış Baldır atau Kayış Bacak. Artikel pertama menyebutnya gulyabani (sejenis hantu pemakan manusia) yang kakinya terbuat dari tali kulit, sedangkan kamus kedua menamainya jin bengkok. Dalam bahasa Turki Anatolia, kata kayış berarti sabuk atau kulit.
long_description.en: Kayış is a malevolent being also known as Kayış Baldır or Kayış Bacak. The first article calls it a gulyabani, a kind of ghoul, whose legs are made of leather strap, while the second source names it the crooked jinn. In Anatolian Turkish, the word kayış means belt or leather.

long_description.id: Ia tampak seperti orang tua tanpa tangan dan kaki yang tidak sanggup berjalan sendiri. Menurut kepercayaan setempat, ia duduk di tepi sungai dengan wajah memelas dan meminta orang yang lewat menggendongnya menyeberang. Begitu naik ke punggung seseorang, dari perutnya keluar dua kaki panjang atau lengan mirip ular yang melilit tubuh orang itu.
long_description.en: It looks like an old man with neither hands nor feet who cannot walk unaided. In local belief it sits by a river looking pitiful and begs passers-by to carry it across. Once on a person's back, two long legs or snake-like arms emerge from its belly and coil around the victim's body.

long_description.id: Setelah itu ia melilitkan kakinya ke pinggang korban dan tidak melepaskannya sampai perjalanan selesai, lalu menjadikan orang itu budak yang harus menuruti perintahnya. Kamus kedua menambahkan bahwa ia mengganggu perempuan yang baru melahirkan dengan duduk erat di bahu mereka. Ada pula cerita bahwa tubuhnya bisa memanjang sampai kepalanya menyentuh awan.
long_description.en: It then winds its legs around the victim's waist and will not let go until the trip is over, turning the person into a slave who must obey its orders. The second source adds that it troubles women who have recently given birth by sitting tightly on their shoulders. Other tales say its body can stretch until its head reaches the clouds.

long_description.id: Kayış muncul setelah azan magrib dan, menurut kamus kedua, berkeliaran sampai fajar. Menurut satu tafsiran, kisahnya diceritakan agar anak-anak tidak keluar rumah ketika petang gelap dan tidak berbuat nakal.
long_description.en: Kayış comes out after the evening call to prayer and, according to the second source, roams until dawn. One interpretation holds that its tale was told to keep children indoors after dark and out of mischief.

cultural_context.id: Menurut satu tafsiran, kisah Kayış dipakai untuk mencegah anak-anak keluar rumah dan berbuat nakal saat hari mulai gelap.
cultural_context.en: According to one interpretation, the tale of Kayış served to stop children from going out and misbehaving as darkness fell.

claims.quote: Kayış, Çocukları korkutmak için uydurulmuş kötücül varlıktır. Kayış Baldır veya Kayış Bacak da denilen, ayakları kayıştan gulyabanidir.

statement.id: Kayış adalah makhluk jahat (kötücül varlık) yang direka untuk menakut-nakuti anak-anak (çocukları korkutmak); disebut juga Kayış Baldır atau Kayış Bacak, ia gulyabani yang kakinya dari tali kulit (kayış).
statement.en: Kayış is a malevolent being (kötücül varlık) invented to frighten children (çocukları korkutmak); also called Kayış Baldır or Kayış Bacak, it is a gulyabani (ghoul) whose legs are made of leather strap (kayış).

claims.quote: O, kendi ayakları üzerinde durup yürüyemez. Bunun için de yoldan giden insanları aldatıp, onun boynuna biner.

statement.id: Ia tidak dapat berdiri dan berjalan di atas kakinya sendiri (yürüyemez); karena itu ia menipu orang yang lewat di jalan lalu menunggangi lehernya (boynuna biner).
statement.en: It cannot stand and walk on its own feet (yürüyemez); so it deceives people going along the road and rides on their neck (boynuna biner).

claims.quote: Sonra kayış ayaklarını onun beline dolayıp, yolu bitinceye kadar onu bırakmaz.

statement.id: Lalu ia melilitkan kaki talinya ke pinggang orang itu (beline dolayıp) dan tidak melepaskannya sampai perjalanannya selesai (yolu bitinceye kadar).
statement.en: Then it wraps its strap legs around the person's waist (beline dolayıp) and does not let go until the journey ends (yolu bitinceye kadar).

claims.quote: Elsiz ve ayaksız bir ihtiyar görünümünde olan bu varlık, ırmak kenarında oturup, gariban bir görünüş sergileyerek

statement.id: Makhluk yang tampak seperti orang tua tanpa tangan dan kaki (elsiz ve ayaksız bir ihtiyar) ini duduk di tepi sungai (ırmak kenarında) dengan penampilan memelas (gariban).
statement.en: This being, looking like an old man without hands or feet (elsiz ve ayaksız bir ihtiyar), sits by the river bank (ırmak kenarında) putting on a pitiful appearance (gariban).

claims.quote: Elleriyle de sıkı sıkıya sarılıp, "Ne dersem, onu yapacaksın" diyerek, o insanı kölesi yapar.

statement.id: Dengan tangannya ia memeluk erat (sıkı sıkıya sarılıp) dan, sambil berkata bahwa orang itu harus melakukan apa pun yang ia katakan, menjadikan orang itu budaknya (kölesi yapar).
statement.en: Clinging tightly with its hands (sıkı sıkıya sarılıp) and saying the person will do whatever it says, it makes that person its slave (kölesi yapar).

claims.quote: Söylentilere göre 'Kayış Baldır' uzadıkça uzanan, başı bulutlara değen korkunç bir canlıdır. O, akşam ezanından sonra ortaya çıkar.

statement.id: Menurut cerita, Kayış Baldır makhluk mengerikan yang terus memanjang hingga kepalanya menyentuh awan (başı bulutlara değen), dan ia muncul setelah azan magrib (akşam ezanından sonra).
statement.en: According to rumours, Kayış Baldır is a terrible creature that keeps stretching until its head touches the clouds (başı bulutlara değen), and it appears after the evening call to prayer (akşam ezanından sonra).

claims.quote: Bir yoruma göre, böyle bir hikâye anlatılarak, çocukların akşam karanlığında evden çıkmalarının ve yaramazlık yapmalarının önüne geçilmek isteniyormuş.

statement.id: Menurut satu tafsiran, cerita semacam itu diceritakan untuk mencegah anak-anak (çocukların) keluar rumah saat gelap petang dan berbuat nakal (yaramazlık).
statement.en: According to one interpretation, such a story was told to stop children (çocukların) from leaving the house in the evening darkness and misbehaving (yaramazlık).

claims.quote: KAYIŞ: Çarpık Cin. ... Hava karardıktan sonra genellikle akşam ezanının ardından ortaya çıkarak tan vaktine kadar dolaşır. Eğri bacaklı, korkunç görünüşlü bir yaratıktır.

statement.id: Kamus kedua menyebut Kayış jin bengkok (Çarpık Cin) yang muncul setelah hari gelap, biasanya sesudah azan magrib (akşam ezanının ardından), dan berkeliaran sampai fajar (tan vaktine kadar); ia makhluk berkaki bengkok (eğri bacaklı) dan berpenampilan mengerikan.
statement.en: The second source calls Kayış the crooked jinn (Çarpık Cin), which appears after dark, usually after the evening call to prayer (akşam ezanının ardından), and roams until dawn (tan vaktine kadar); it is a crooked-legged (eğri bacaklı), terrifying-looking creature.

claims.quote: Lohusalara musallat olarak, omuzlarına ayakları önden sarkacak şekilde sımsıkı oturur. Sonra da yakaladığı kadından gezinmesini ister.

statement.id: Ia mengganggu perempuan yang baru melahirkan (lohusalara musallat), duduk erat di bahu mereka dengan kaki menjuntai ke depan, lalu menyuruh perempuan yang ditangkapnya berjalan-jalan (gezinmesini ister).
statement.en: It haunts women who have recently given birth (lohusalara musallat), sitting tightly on their shoulders with its legs dangling in front, and then demands that the woman it has caught walk it around (gezinmesini ister).

claims.quote: Ancak insanın sırtına binince karnından üç arşın uzunluğunda iki bacak veyâ yılana benzer kollar çıkıp kişinin bedenine dolanır.

statement.id: Namun begitu naik ke punggung orang, dari perutnya keluar dua kaki sepanjang tiga arşın (üç arşın) atau lengan menyerupai ular (yılana benzer kollar) yang melilit tubuh orang itu.
statement.en: But once it climbs onto a person's back, two legs three arşın long (üç arşın) or snake-like arms (yılana benzer kollar) come out of its belly and wrap around the person's body.

claims.quote: Anlam: (Kay). Anadolu Türkçe'sinde Kayış sözcüğü kemer, deri demektir.

statement.id: Dalam bahasa Turki Anatolia (Anadolu Türkçe), kata Kayış berarti sabuk, kulit (kemer, deri).
statement.en: In Anatolian Turkish (Anadolu Türkçe) the word Kayış means belt, leather (kemer, deri).

Kedua sumber tidak menyebut negara secara eksplisit; hanya bahasa Turki Anatolia yang disebut dalam bagian asal kata.
Tautan luar di artikel pertama (McDonald; Nerin Köse) adalah salinan arsip makalah yang tidak dibuka; dipakai kamus Türk Söylence Sözlüğü sebagai sumber kedua.

short_description.id: Khyah adalah makhluk humanoid dalam cerita rakyat Newar, digambarkan pendek, gemuk, berbulu, dan mirip kera.
short_description.en: Khyah are humanoid creatures of Newar folklore, portrayed as short, fat, hairy and apelike.

long_description.id: Khyah adalah makhluk humanoid dalam cerita rakyat Newar, digambarkan pendek, gemuk, berbulu, dan mirip kera. Ia muncul dalam cerita anak yang populer di masyarakat Newar. Khyah yang bersahabat membawa kebaikan, sedangkan yang jahat membawa masalah; Khyah putih dipercaya membawa keberuntungan dan yang hitam dapat menimbulkan masalah. Bertemu Khyah dapat membuat orang sakit, dan Khyah dikatakan menggelitik korbannya hingga mati.
long_description.en: Khyah are humanoid creatures of Newar folklore, portrayed as short, fat, hairy and apelike. Children's tales that are popular among the Newars feature them. Friendly ones are said to bring goodness to a home and bad ones trouble; white Khyah are believed to bring luck, black ones problems. Encountering a Khyah can make one ill, and Khyahs are said to tickle their victims to death.

long_description.id: Dalam kebudayaan Newar mereka mendampingi Lakshmi dan menjaga kantong uang dalam penggambarannya. Khyah rumah tinggal di loteng dan ruang penyimpanan gelap dan dikatakan takut pada lampu listrik; seorang penulis juga menyebut mereka selalu tinggal di tempat gelap karena takut cahaya. Khyah dan Kawancha muncul dalam drama tari suci dan menjadi penjaga kuil.
long_description.en: In Newar culture they attend Lakshmi and guard bags of coins in depictions. Household Khyahs dwell in attics and dark storerooms and are said to fear electric lighting; one author adds that they stay in darkness because light frightens them. Khyah and Kawancha appear in sacred dance dramas and as temple guardians.

long_description.id: Tari Khyah Pyakhan pada festival Yenya menampilkan aktor berkostum Khyah. Dalam trup tari topeng Newar, khyāh digambarkan sebagai makhluk berbulu mirip kera dengan tudung hitam dan jubah wol hitam yang membuatnya tampak seperti beruang, dengan lidah merah menjulur; ia berakrobat, berguling-guling di lantai, dan sesekali membuat gerakan jorok kepada gadis di antara penonton. Dalam trup para dewa, khyāh menyertai bersama kerangka, raksasa, dan betāh, melompat dan berguling di lantai. Khyah juga muncul dalam ritual Gufa bagi gadis sebelum haid pertama, sebagai boneka Bahra Khyah di ruang gelap.
long_description.en: Khyah Pyakhan dances at the Yenya festival feature actors in Khyah costumes. In Newar masked-dance troupes the khyāh is an ape-like hairy creature in a black cowl and black woollen pelisse that make him look like a bear, with a red tongue hanging from his mouth; he does acrobatics, rolls over the floor, and occasionally makes scatological gestures at young ladies in the audience. In a troupe of gods, khyāh accompany them with skeletons, demons and betāh, jumping and rolling on the floor. Khyah also appears in the Gufa ritual for girls before menstruation, as a Bahra Khyah doll in a dark room.

long_description.id: Menurut legenda Newar dalam sebuah esai, dewa-dewa tua melahirkan Khyah: seorang anak lahir dari dewa-dewa tua, mereka berebut memegangnya, kulitnya terlepas, dan dari dagingnya muncul Khyah sementara Kavam muncul sebagai kerangka. Untuk mengendalikan kekuatan si kembar itu, para dewa membuat alat musik Dhimay, yang mengiringi para penari Khyah dalam Khyah Pyakhan.
long_description.en: According to a Newari legend told in an essay, the old Gods gave birth to the Khyahs: a child was born to the old gods, they tussled to hold it, its skin detached, and from the flesh came Khyah while Kavam emerged as the skeleton. To control the power of the twins, the Gods created the instrument Dhimay, which accompanies the Khyah dancers in Khyah Pyakhan.

sources.author: Gérard Toffin

claims.quote: Khyāh (Newar: 𑐏𑑂𑐫𑐵𑑅; alternative spellings Khyā or Khyāk) is a mythical humanoid creature in Newari folklore. It is depicted as a fat, hairy and short ape-like creature.

statement.id: Khyah adalah makhluk humanoid dalam cerita rakyat Newar, digambarkan pendek, gemuk, berbulu, dan mirip kera.
statement.en: Khyah are humanoid creatures of Newar folklore, portrayed as short, fat, hairy and apelike.

claims.quote: Khyahs appear in children's stories popular in Newar society. A friendly Khyah fills the home with goodness while bad ones bring trouble. A white Khyah is believed to bring good luck while a black one can create problems. Encountering a Khyah can make one ill. Khyahs are said to tickle their victims to death.

statement.id: Khyah yang bersahabat membawa kebaikan, sedangkan yang jahat membawa masalah.
statement.en: Friendly khyah bring goodness, while bad ones bring trouble.

claims.quote: In Newar culture, Khyahs attend to Lakshmi, the goddess of wealth, and pictures of the deity show them guarding overflowing bags of coins. Household Khyahs usually dwell in the attic and dark storerooms. They are said to fear electric lighting.

statement.id: Dalam kebudayaan Newar mereka mendampingi Lakshmi dan menjaga kantong uang dalam penggambarannya.
statement.en: In Newar culture they attend Lakshmi and guard bags of coins in depictions.

claims.quote: Household Khyahs usually dwell in the attic and dark storerooms. They are said to fear electric lighting.

statement.id: Khyah rumah tinggal di loteng dan ruang penyimpanan gelap.
statement.en: Household khyah dwell in attics and dark storerooms.

claims.quote: The antithesis of the Khyah is the Kawanchā, a skeleton. Khyahs and Kawanchas appear as supporting characters in sacred dance dramas of the Newars. Images of Khyahs and Kawanchas are also placed at temples as guardians of the shrine.

statement.id: Khyah dan Kawancha muncul dalam drama tari suci dan menjadi penjaga kuil.
statement.en: Khyah and Kawancha appear in sacred dance dramas and as temple guardians.

claims.quote: During the Yenya festival in Kathmandu, dance performances are held at market squares and the Durbar Square where actors dressed in Khyah costumes give dance performances. The dances, known as Khyāh Pyākhan (ख्याः प्याखं), consist of antics and tumbling.

statement.id: Tari Khyah Pyakhan pada festival Yenya menampilkan aktor berkostum Khyah.
statement.en: Khyah Pyakhan dances at the Yenya festival feature actors in khyah costumes.

claims.quote: Each troupe also features one or two skeletons kavã ... Their associate, the jostler khyāh, an ape-like hairy creature wears a black cowl over his head; he is dressed in a black woollen pelisse, that gives him the appearance of a bear, with a red tongue dangling from his mouth.

statement.id: Dalam trup tari topeng Newar, khyāh digambarkan sebagai makhluk berbulu mirip kera yang mengenakan tudung hitam dan jubah wol hitam sehingga tampak seperti beruang, dengan lidah merah menjulur dari mulutnya.
statement.en: In Newar masked-dance troupes the khyāh, an ape-like hairy creature, wears a black cowl and a black woollen pelisse that gives him the appearance of a bear, with a red tongue dangling from his mouth.

claims.quote: the jostler khyāh, an ape-like hairy creature ... Both perform a series of acrobatics on stage. They tumble and roll over the floor. Occasionally, they rush around making scatological gestures at young ladies in the audience.

statement.id: Khyāh dalam pertunjukan itu berakrobat di panggung, berguling-guling di lantai, dan sesekali berlari sambil membuat gerakan jorok kepada gadis-gadis di antara penonton.
statement.en: The khyāh in the performance does acrobatics on stage, tumbles and rolls over the floor, and occasionally rushes around making scatological gestures at young ladies in the audience.

claims.quote: These gods and goddesses are accompanied by skeletons (kawã), demons (rākshas), betāh and khyāh who jump and roll around on the floor (gwara-gwara tulegu)

statement.id: Dalam trup tari topeng para dewa dan dewi Newar, khyāh ikut menyertai bersama kerangka, raksasa, dan betāh, melompat dan berguling-guling di lantai (gwara-gwara tulegu).
statement.en: In a Newar masked-dance troupe of gods and goddesses, khyāh accompany them with skeletons, demons and betāh, jumping and rolling around on the floor (gwara-gwara tulegu).

claims.quote: According to Newari legend, the old Gods gave birth to the terrible Khyahs. It is said that a child was born to the old gods, and a tussle began between them to hold the baby. The struggle led to the detachment of the skin, and the child only remained with flesh and bones. Out of the flesh came Khyah, and Kavam emerged as the skeleton.

statement.id: Menurut legenda Newar, dewa-dewa tua melahirkan Khyah; dalam kisah itu, seorang anak lahir dari dewa-dewa tua, mereka berebut memegangnya, kulitnya terlepas, lalu dari dagingnya muncul Khyah dan Kavam muncul sebagai kerangka.
statement.en: According to Newari legend the old Gods gave birth to the Khyahs: a child was born to the old gods, they tussled to hold it, its skin detached, and from the flesh came Khyah while Kavam emerged as the skeleton.

claims.quote: To control the power of the twins, the Gods created the Newari instrument called Dhimay from a tree trunk. During Khyah Pyakhan, the traditional Newari dance, dancers dressed as Khyah, dance to the beat of a Dhimay.

statement.id: Untuk mengendalikan kekuatan si kembar itu, para dewa membuat alat musik Newar bernama Dhimay dari batang pohon; dalam Khyah Pyakhan, penari berkostum Khyah menari mengikuti tabuhan Dhimay.
statement.en: To control the power of the twins, the Gods created the Newari instrument called Dhimay from a tree trunk; in Khyah Pyakhan, dancers dressed as Khyah dance to the beat of a Dhimay.

claims.quote: Khyahs often make significant appearances in the Newari Gufa tradition, a ritual meant for young girls before the beginning of their menstruation. During this ritual, girls remain inside a dark room with a small doll that represents Bahra Khyah.

statement.id: Khyah sering muncul dalam tradisi Gufa Newar, ritual bagi gadis sebelum haid pertama, di mana para gadis berada di ruang gelap bersama boneka kecil yang mewakili Bahra Khyah.
statement.en: Khyahs often appear in the Newari Gufa tradition, a ritual for young girls before menstruation, in which the girls stay in a dark room with a small doll representing Bahra Khyah.

claims.quote: Khyahs always dwell in the dark as they are afraid of the light. There are two types of Khyahs; white and black. The white ones are the good ones

statement.id: Menurut penulis ini, Khyah selalu tinggal di tempat gelap karena takut cahaya, dan ada dua jenis Khyah, putih dan hitam; yang putih adalah yang baik.
statement.en: According to this author, Khyahs always dwell in the dark as they are afraid of the light, and there are two types, white and black; the white ones are the good ones.

short_description.id: Kichkandi adalah roh perempuan dalam cerita rakyat Nepal yang melekat pada bagian tubuhnya yang belum dikremasi.
short_description.en: Kichkandi is a woman's spirit in Nepalese folklore attached to an uncremated part of her body.

long_description.id: Kichkandi (juga kichkanya) adalah roh perempuan dalam cerita rakyat Nepal yang melekat pada bagian tubuhnya yang belum dikremasi, biasanya tulang. Perempuan ini semasa hidup diperlakukan tidak adil atau meninggal saat melahirkan atau hamil. Sebuah artikel jurnal menyebutnya hantu perempuan muda yang cantik yang meninggal dalam keadaan tidak wajar, seperti bunuh diri, saat melahirkan, atau dibunuh.
long_description.en: Kichkandi (also kichkanya) is a woman's spirit in Nepalese folklore attached to an uncremated part of her dead body, usually a bone. Such women were treated unfairly while alive or died during childbirth or pregnancy. A journal article calls her a young, beautiful female ghost who died in unnatural circumstances such as suicide, childbirth or murder.

long_description.id: Cerita menempatkannya di lokasi kematian yang tidak wajar. Ia dikatakan berambut panjang hitam, berkulit pucat dan kurus, dan berpakaian pengantin merah; kakinya menghadap ke belakang. Ia memikat pelancong laki-laki sendirian dan menyerap daya hidupnya, dan menurut artikel jurnal itu laki-laki yang bersentuhan dengannya akan jatuh sakit atau mati.
long_description.en: Tales place her at the site of an untimely death. She is said to have long black hair, a pale and bony complexion and a red bridal dress, and her feet face backward. She lures a solitary male traveller and saps his life force, and according to the journal article any man who came into contact with her would fall ill or die.

long_description.id: Menurut seorang informan penelitian, kichkini berjalan sendirian pada malam hari di sekitar desa kecil serta di tepi sungai dan tempat kremasi. Informan lain menyebut perhiasan seperti gelang kaki dibawa laki-laki sebagai perlindungan, bahwa kichkini tidak dapat menyeberangi air, dan bahwa tulang yang diikat benang harus dibakar untuk menyingkirkannya. Informan berbeda pendapat tentang motifnya: balas dendam atau mungkin hanya mencari cinta. Penulis artikel menafsirkan kichkini sebagai wakil ancaman yang dirasakan dari seksualitas perempuan terhadap struktur patrilineal.
long_description.en: According to a research informant, kichkini walk alone at night around small villages and alongside rivers and cremation grounds. Other informants mention jewelry such as anklets carried by men as protection, that kichkini cannot cross water, and that the bone with the string tied around it must be burned to get rid of her. Informants differ on her motive: revenge, or perhaps just looking for love. The article's author suggests kichkini may represent the perceived threat of female sexuality to patrilineal structures.

short_description.id: Kijimuna adalah roh kayu kecil dalam mitologi Okinawa yang digambarkan seperti anak berambut merah liar dan dikatakan tinggal di pohon, terutama beringin.
short_description.en: The kijimuna are small wood spirits of Okinawan mythology, described as child-like with wild red hair and said to live in trees, above all the banyan.

long_description.id: Kijimuna adalah makhluk mitologi yang dikatakan mendiami pulau Okinawa, dan menurut mitologi Okinawa merupakan roh kayu kecil. Mereka dikatakan tinggal di pohon, yang paling umum adalah gajumaru atau beringin. Mereka digambarkan menyerupai anak berusia tiga atau empat tahun dengan rambut merah liar, dengan kulit kemerahan menurut satu sumber.
long_description.en: The kijimuna are mythological creatures said to inhabit the island of Okinawa, and in Okinawan mythology are small wood spirits. They are said to live in trees, the most common being the gajumaru or banyan. They are described as resembling a child of three or four with wild red hair, and, according to one source, red-tinted skin.

long_description.id: Kijimunā sering membantu nelayan menangkap ikan sebagai imbalan makanan matang, dan sangat menyukai mata ikan. Mereka dikenal jahil dan salah satu tipuan terkenalnya adalah berbaring di dada seseorang sehingga orang itu tak bisa bergerak atau bernapas. Mereka membenci ayam, periuk masak, orang yang buang angin, dan terutama gurita.
long_description.en: Kijimunā often help fishermen catch fish in return for a cooked meal, and are especially fond of fish eyes. They are known to be mischievous, and one of their best-known tricks is to lie on a person's chest so that they cannot move or breathe. They loathe chickens, cooking pots, people passing gas and, above all, the octopus.

long_description.id: Menebang pohon beringin tempat mereka tinggal membangkitkan kemarahan mereka; kijimunā yang disakiti dikenal membunuh ternak, merusak perahu, atau menjebak orang di pohon berongga. Banyak kisah rakyat Okinawa bermula dengan kijimuna berteman dengan manusia lalu berakhir dengan hubungan yang memburuk; dalam satu kisah teman manusia itu membakar pohonnya sehingga kijimuna lari ke pegunungan.
long_description.en: Cutting down the banyan tree where they live earns their wrath; wronged kijimunā are known to kill livestock, sabotage boats, or trap people in hollow trees. Many Okinawan folk tales begin with a kijimuna befriending a human and end with the relationship going bad; in one story the human friend burns down the tree, so the kijimuna flees to the mountains.

claims.quote: are mythological creatures said to inhabit the island of Okinawa.

statement.id: Kijimuna adalah makhluk mitologi yang dikatakan mendiami pulau Okinawa.
statement.en: The kijimuna are mythological creatures said to inhabit the island of Okinawa.

claims.quote: They are described as resembling around a three or four-year-old child with wild red hair.

statement.id: Mereka digambarkan menyerupai anak berusia sekitar tiga atau empat tahun dengan rambut merah liar.
statement.en: They are described as resembling a child of around three or four years old with wild red hair.

claims.quote: The kijimuna are small wood spirits according to Okinawan mythology.

statement.id: Menurut mitologi Okinawa, kijimuna adalah roh kayu kecil.
statement.en: According to Okinawan mythology, the kijimuna are small wood spirits.

claims.quote: The kijimuna are said to live in trees, but the most common one is the 'gajumaru' or banyan tree.

statement.id: Kijimuna dikatakan tinggal di pohon, dan yang paling umum adalah gajumaru atau beringin.
statement.en: The kijimuna are said to live in trees, the most common being the gajumaru or banyan tree.

claims.quote: Habitat: banyan trees on the islands of Okinawa

statement.id: Habitat kijimunā disebut pohon beringin di pulau-pulau Okinawa.
statement.en: The kijimunā's habitat is given as banyan trees on the islands of Okinawa.

claims.quote: Physically, kijimunā are about the same height as a child, with wild and thick bright red hair, and red tinted skin.

statement.id: Secara fisik kijimunā setinggi anak-anak, dengan rambut merah terang yang liar dan tebal serta kulit kemerahan.
statement.en: Physically, kijimunā are about as tall as a child, with wild, thick, bright red hair and red-tinted skin.

claims.quote: They are especially fond of fish eyes, even preferring the left eye over the right.

statement.id: Mereka sangat menyukai mata ikan, bahkan lebih memilih mata kiri daripada kanan.
statement.en: They are especially fond of fish eyes, even preferring the left eye over the right.

claims.quote: They loathe chickens and cooking pots. They are extremely put off by people passing gas. However, the thing they hate above all else is the octopus.

statement.id: Mereka membenci ayam dan periuk masak, sangat terganggu oleh orang yang buang angin, dan yang paling mereka benci adalah gurita.
statement.en: They loathe chickens and cooking pots, are extremely put off by people passing gas, and hate the octopus above all else.

claims.quote: Kijimunā often help fishermen catch fish, or aid humans in other ways in return for a cooked meal.

statement.id: Kijimunā sering membantu nelayan menangkap ikan, atau menolong manusia dengan cara lain sebagai imbalan makanan matang.
statement.en: Kijimunā often help fishermen catch fish, or aid humans in other ways, in return for a cooked meal.

claims.quote: Cutting down the banyan tree in which they live is a sure way to earn their wrath. Kijimunā thus wronged have been known to murder livestock, sabotage boats so they sink while their owners are far out at sea, or magically trap people in hollow trees from which they cannot escape.

statement.id: Menebang pohon beringin tempat mereka tinggal pasti membangkitkan kemarahan mereka; kijimunā yang disakiti dikenal membunuh ternak, merusak perahu agar tenggelam saat pemiliknya jauh di laut, atau menjebak orang di pohon berongga secara gaib.
statement.en: Cutting down the banyan tree in which they live surely earns their wrath; wronged kijimunā are known to kill livestock, sabotage boats so they sink while owners are far out at sea, or magically trap people in hollow trees.

claims.quote: The Kijimuna are known to be very mischievous, playing pranks and tricking humans. One of their best-known tricks is to lie upon a person's chest, making them unable to move or breathe.

statement.id: Kijimuna dikenal sangat jahil, gemar bercanda dan mengelabui manusia; salah satu tipuan terkenalnya adalah berbaring di dada seseorang sehingga orang itu tak bisa bergerak atau bernapas.
statement.en: The Kijimuna are known to be very mischievous, playing pranks and tricking humans; one of their best-known tricks is to lie upon a person's chest, leaving them unable to move or breathe.

claims.quote: One story tells of a kijimuna's friend burning down his tree, so the kijimuna fled to the mountains.

statement.id: Satu kisah menceritakan teman seorang kijimuna yang membakar pohonnya sehingga kijimuna itu lari ke pegunungan.
statement.en: One story tells of a kijimuna's friend burning down his tree, so that the kijimuna fled to the mountains.

claims.quote: 沖縄諸島地域の伝承にある妖怪。樹木（しばしばガジュマルの木）の精霊とされる。「キジムン」などとも。
claims.locator: Entri キジムナー (デジタル大辞泉プラス)

statement.id: Kamus Jepang menyebut kijimuna sebagai yōkai dalam tradisi wilayah kepulauan Okinawa, dianggap roh pohon (sering pohon gajumaru), juga disebut "Kijimun".
statement.en: A Japanese dictionary calls the kijimuna a yōkai in the lore of the Okinawa Islands, regarded as a spirit of trees (often the gajumaru), also called "Kijimun".

claims.quote: Alternate names: sēma, bunagaya

statement.id: Nama lain kijimunā adalah sēma dan bunagaya.
statement.en: Alternate names of the kijimunā are sēma and bunagaya.

claims.quote: The kijimuna are a common subject in Okinawan folk tales. Many of their stories begin with the kijimuna becoming a human's friend and then ending with the relationship going bad.

statement.id: Kijimuna adalah tokoh umum dalam cerita rakyat Okinawa; banyak kisahnya bermula dengan kijimuna berteman dengan manusia lalu berakhir dengan hubungan yang memburuk.
statement.en: The kijimuna are a common subject in Okinawan folk tales; many stories begin with the kijimuna befriending a human and end with the relationship going bad.

short_description.id: Kijo adalah oni perempuan dalam legenda Jepang, umumnya perempuan yang berubah menjadi oni akibat karma dan dendam.
short_description.en: Kijo is a female oni in Japanese legends, usually a woman transformed into an oni by karma and resentment.

long_description.id: Kijo (鬼女, harfiah 'perempuan iblis') adalah oni perempuan dalam legenda Jepang. Kamus mendefinisikannya sebagai oni berwujud perempuan, dan kata ini juga dipakai untuk perempuan yang hatinya sekejam oni. Biasanya dianggap perempuan yang berubah menjadi oni akibat karma dan dendam.
long_description.en: A kijo (鬼女, literally 'demon woman') is an oni woman from Japanese legends. Dictionaries define it as an oni in the form of a woman, and the word is also used for a woman whose heart is as cruel as an oni. They are usually thought to be women whom karma and resentment have transformed into oni.

long_description.id: Menurut yokai.com, kijo mirip perempuan manusia tetapi sangat buruk rupa, dan sebagian bermata merah atau kuning, berkulit biru, bertanduk, atau berkuku panjang. Mereka terutama perempuan yang berubah akibat cemburu hebat, kejahatan, atau dendam, lalu menyingkir ke gua gunung, rumah terbengkalai, atau jalan pegunungan. Sumber yang sama menyebut mereka lebih kuat daripada kebanyakan manusia, ahli sihir, dan mampu mengutuk, meracik racun, serta merajut ilusi.
long_description.en: According to yokai.com, kijo resemble human women but are hideously ugly, and some have red or yellow eyes, blue skin, horns, or long claws. They are chiefly women transformed by intense jealousy, wicked crimes, or a grudge, who retreat to mountain caves, abandoned houses, or mountain roads. The same source says they are stronger than most humans, excel in magic, and can bestow curses, brew poisons, and weave illusions.

long_description.id: Kijo sering muncul dalam legenda, dongeng, dan seni pertunjukan Jepang; yang terkenal antara lain Momiji dari Togakushi dan Suzuka Gozen dari Pegunungan Suzuka. Onibaba dari Adachigahara juga dianggap kijo. Tosa Obake Zōshi menceritakan seorang kijo yang memakan janin dari perempuan hamil, dan Nihon Kokugo Daijiten mengutip lakon Noh bahwa Yamanba adalah kijo yang tinggal di gunung.
long_description.en: Kijo often appear in Japanese legends, folktales, and performing arts; famous ones include Momiji of Togakushi and Suzuka Gozen of the Suzuka Mountains. The onibaba of Adachigahara is also considered a kijo. The Tosa Obake Zōshi tells of a kijo that ate a fetus from a pregnant woman, and the Nihon Kokugo Daijiten cites a Noh play saying Yamanba is a kijo who lives in the mountains.

long_description.id: Menurut yokai.com, nama kijo hanya gabungan kanji oni dan perempuan, tetapi tidak ada dasar untuk menganggap kijo padanan perempuan oni; keduanya mungkin makhluk terpisah. Ensiklopedia lama Heibonsha mencatat bahwa perempuan tua dikatakan menjadi kijo.
long_description.en: According to yokai.com, the name kijo is just the kanji for oni and woman combined, but nothing supports treating kijo as the female counterparts of oni; the two may be separate creatures. The older Heibonsha encyclopedia notes that an old woman is said to become a kijo.

literal_meaning.en: "demon woman" (the kanji for oni and woman)

claims.quote: A kijo (鬼女, lit. demon woman) is an oni woman from Japanese legends.

statement.id: Kijo adalah oni perempuan dalam legenda Jepang.
statement.en: Kijo is a female oni in Japanese legends.

claims.quote: They are normally considered to be women who have turned into oni as a result of karma and resentment, with the younger ones being called "kijo" while the ones that look like old ladies are called onibaba (鬼婆, "demon hag").

statement.id: Kijo umumnya dianggap perempuan yang berubah menjadi oni karena karma dan dendam; yang lebih muda disebut kijo, sedangkan yang berpenampilan nenek-nenek disebut onibaba.
statement.en: Kijo are normally considered women who turned into oni through karma and resentment; the younger ones are called kijo, while those that look like old ladies are called onibaba.

claims.quote: They often appear in Japanese legends, folktales, fairy tales, and performing arts, and famous among them are Momiji (from The Legend of Momiji and Momijigari) from togakushi, Shinano Province (now the town of Kinasa, Nagano, Nagano Prefecture) and Suzuka Gozen from the Suzuka Mountains.

statement.id: Tokoh - tokoh seperti itu muncul dalam cerita rakyat dan pertunjukan panggung.
statement.en: Such figures appear in folklore and stage performances.

claims.quote: The onibaba of Adachigahara (Kurozuka) had "baba" in her name, but she is also considered a kijo.

statement.id: Onibaba Adachigahara juga dapat digolongkan sebagai kijo.
statement.en: The onibaba of Adachigahara can also be classed as a kijo.

claims.quote: き‐じょ〔‐ヂヨ〕【鬼女】 １ 女の姿をしている鬼。 ２ 心が鬼のようにむごい女。

statement.id: Menurut Digital Daijisen, kijo (鬼女) berarti (1) oni berwujud perempuan, dan (2) perempuan yang hatinya sekejam oni.
statement.en: According to the Digital Daijisen, kijo (鬼女) means (1) an oni in the form of a woman and (2) a woman whose heart is as cruel as an oni.

claims.quote: ① 女の姿をした鬼。 [初出の実例]「山姥とは山に住む鬼女(キジョ)とこそ」(出典：謡曲・山姥（1430頃）)
claims.locator: 精選版 日本国語大辞典

statement.id: Kamus Nihon Kokugo Daijiten menjelaskan kijo sebagai oni berwujud perempuan dan mengutip lakon Noh Yamanba (sekitar 1430): "Yamanba adalah kijo yang tinggal di gunung."
statement.en: The Nihon Kokugo Daijiten defines kijo as an oni in the form of a woman and cites the Noh play Yamanba (c. 1430): "Yamanba is a kijo who lives in the mountains."

claims.quote: いま一つの契機は年を取り過ぎることである。年老いた女は鬼女になるといい(《今昔物語集》)

statement.id: Ensiklopedia lama Heibonsha menyebut satu pemicu lain adalah usia yang terlalu tua, dan perempuan tua dikatakan menjadi kijo, merujuk Konjaku Monogatari-shū.
statement.en: The older Heibonsha encyclopedia names growing too old as another trigger and says an old woman is said to become a kijo, citing the Konjaku Monogatari-shū.

claims.quote: Kijo are female demons. They resemble human women in most ways, although they are hideously ugly to behold. Some have red or yellow eyes, blue skin, sharp horns, long claws, or other supernatural features.

statement.id: Kijo adalah iblis perempuan yang mirip perempuan manusia tetapi sangat buruk rupa; sebagian bermata merah atau kuning, berkulit biru, bertanduk tajam, atau berkuku panjang.
statement.en: Kijo are female demons that resemble human women but are hideously ugly; some have red or yellow eyes, blue skin, sharp horns, or long claws.

claims.quote: Kijo refers chiefly to women who have been transformed from humans into horrible monsters—either out of intense jealousy, wicked crimes, or a terrible grudge that twists the soul into pure hatred. ... These transformed women retreat from common society into more secluded places where they continue to perpetrate their wicked deeds.

statement.id: Kijo terutama adalah perempuan yang berubah menjadi monster akibat cemburu hebat, kejahatan, atau dendam; mereka menyingkir dari masyarakat ke tempat terpencil dan terus melakukan perbuatan jahat.
statement.en: Kijo refers chiefly to women transformed into monsters out of intense jealousy, wicked crimes, or a terrible grudge; they retreat from society to secluded places where they continue their wicked deeds.

claims.quote: Kijo are stronger than most humans, though their strength pales in comparison to oni. These demonesses excel in magic; they accumulate powerful spells over their long lives. Kijo are capable of bestowing hexes and curses, brewing poisons and potions, and weaving complex illusions.

statement.id: Kijo lebih kuat daripada kebanyakan manusia (tetapi kalah dari oni), ahli sihir, dan mampu mengutuk, meracik racun dan ramuan, serta merajut ilusi rumit.
statement.en: Kijo are stronger than most humans (though weaker than oni), excel in magic, and can bestow hexes and curses, brew poisons and potions, and weave complex illusions.

claims.quote: They can be found living in remote mountain caves, abandoned houses, or along mountain roads where they receive a steady supply of victims.

statement.id: Kijo dapat ditemui tinggal di gua gunung terpencil, rumah terbengkalai, atau di jalan pegunungan tempat mereka mendapat korban.
statement.en: Kijo can be found living in remote mountain caves, abandoned houses, or along mountain roads where they receive a steady supply of victims.

claims.quote: Though their name might suggest that kijo are the female counterparts to the male oni, there is nothing to support this. ... It is likely that kijo are entirely separate creatures from oni, other than the fact that both are born from corrupted human souls.

statement.id: Yokai.com menyatakan tidak ada dukungan bahwa kijo adalah padanan perempuan oni; kemungkinan keduanya makhluk terpisah, selain keduanya lahir dari jiwa manusia yang rusak.
statement.en: Yokai.com states nothing supports kijo being the female counterparts of oni; they are likely entirely separate creatures, apart from both being born from corrupted human souls.

claims.quote: Indeed, the name kijo is formed simply by combining the two kanji for oni and woman.

statement.id: Nama kijo terbentuk hanya dengan menggabungkan dua kanji untuk oni dan perempuan.
statement.en: The name kijo is formed simply by combining the two kanji for oni and woman.

statement.en: The Tosa Obake Zōshi (author unknown) states, under the title "Kijo," that an oni woman with hair about 150 centimeters long ate a fetus from a pregnant woman.

summary.en: A kijo is an oni woman (per the encyclopedia article and the dictionary).

short_description.id: Kong koi atau Phi Kong Koi adalah hantu hutan Laos dan Thailand yang sering digambarkan berkaki satu, melompat sambil berteriak koi, dan dipercaya mengisap darah dari jari kaki pengembara yang tertidur.
short_description.en: Kong koi or Phi Kong Koi is a Lao and Thai jungle ghost often described as one-legged, hopping while shouting koi, and believed to suck blood from the toes of sleeping travellers.

long_description.id: Kong koi atau Phi Kong Koi adalah hantu hutan Laos dan Thailand. Wujudnya tidak mudah digambarkan, tetapi sering disebut sebagai hantu berkaki satu yang bergerak melompat dan berteriak koi, koi, koi. Sebagian orang percaya mulutnya berupa tabung seperti lalat, sebagian lagi menggambarkannya mirip monyet atau lutung, dan kebanyakan sepakat bahwa hantu ini buruk rupa dan tidak bisa memanjat pohon.
long_description.en: Kong koi or Phi Kong Koi is a Lao and Thai jungle ghost. Its appearance is hard to pin down, but it is often described as a one-legged phantom that moves by hopping and shouts koi, koi, koi. Some say its mouth is a tube like a fly's, others liken it to a monkey or langur, and most agree it is ugly and cannot climb trees.

long_description.id: Phi Kong Koi dipercaya mengisap darah dari jari kaki pengembara yang tidur di hutan, sehingga para pengembara dianjurkan tidur dengan kaki dirapatkan atau disilangkan. Sebuah artikel jurnal Thailand yang mengutip ringkasan legenda hantu Thai menyebutnya suka mengisap darah dari ibu jari kaki orang yang bermalam di hutan. Hantu ini juga disebut Phi Pong, Phi Pong Kang, atau Phi Teen Diao.
long_description.en: Phi Kong Koi is believed to suck blood from the toes of travellers sleeping in the jungle, so travellers are advised to sleep with their feet together or crossed. A Thai journal article that cites a summary of Thai ghost legends says it likes to suck blood from the big toes of people camping overnight in the forest. The ghost is also called Phi Pong, Phi Pong Kang or Phi Teen Diao.

long_description.id: Kepercayaan tentangnya berbeda-beda: orang Tai Dam di Mukdahan percaya Phi Kong Koi adalah perempuan sangat kecil berambut panjang dengan kaki terbalik yang berbicara kebalikan dari kenyataan, dan ikan atau barang berharga yang ditemukan di jalan hutan tidak boleh diambil karena miliknya. Orang Karen memandangnya sebagai makhluk kecil mirip celurut. Luang Pu Waen Suciṇṇo menceritakan bahwa ia bertarung dengan banyak Phi Kong Koi di hutan Khammouane, Laos; mereka berwujud seperti anak berusia 13-14 tahun dan bersenjata busur kecil, dan meditasi melindungi mereka.
long_description.en: Beliefs vary: the Tai Dam of Mukdahan believe Phi Kong Koi is a very small long-haired woman with backwards feet who says the opposite of reality, and that fish or valuables found on forest paths must not be taken because they are hers. The Karen see it as a small shrew-like creature. Luang Pu Waen Suciṇṇo said he fought many Phi Kong Koi in the forests of Khammouane, Laos; they looked like children of 13-14 armed with small crossbows, and meditation protected them.

long_description.id: Nama ini punya beberapa sumber: phi berarti hantu dalam bahasa Thai, sedangkan kata koi menurut kamus Royal Institute berarti kelompok etnis berkulit hitam dan berambut keriting di Semenanjung Malaya yang juga disebut Sakai. Ada yang berpendapat Phi Kong Koi sebenarnya adalah kelompok etnis Kha Ra Dae.
long_description.en: The name has several sources: phi means ghost in the Thai language, while the word koi is defined by the Royal Institute Dictionary as an ethnic group with black skin and curly hair in the Malay Peninsula, also known as Sakai. Some suggest the Phi Kong Koi are really the Kha Ra Dae, an ethnic group.

long_description.id: Dalam budaya modern, jejak kaki yang diyakini milik Phi Kong Koi dilaporkan di gua di provinsi Loei pada 2016, dan seorang selebritas internet di provinsi Surin mengaku rumahnya diserbu Phi Kong Koi pada Agustus 2024, dengan jejak kaki besar dilaporkan di tangga rumahnya; seorang ilmuwan Universitas Kasetsart menduga jejak seperti itu adalah jejak manusia yang melebar, dan sebuah video tahun 2018 dianggap rekayasa. Kong koi juga dirujuk dalam film Death Whisperer III (2025), dan film Thailand-Laos Wrecked (2026) terinspirasi dari legendanya.
long_description.en: In modern times, footprints believed to be Phi Kong Koi's were reported in a cave in Loei province in 2016, and in August 2024 an internet celebrity in Surin province claimed his home had been invaded by the Phi Kong Koi, with a large footprint reported on his stairs; a Kasetsart University scientist suggested such prints are human ones that have spread, and a 2018 video was dismissed as staged. The Kong koi is also referenced in the film Death Whisperer III (2025), and the Thai-Lao film Wrecked (2026) is inspired by its legend.

short_description.id: Kuafu adalah raksasa mitologi Tiongkok yang ingin menangkap matahari.
short_description.en: Kuafu is a giant in Chinese mythology who seeks to capture the sun.

long_description.id: Kuafu adalah raksasa mitologi Tiongkok yang ingin menangkap matahari. Kuafu disebut cucu Houtu.
long_description.en: Kuafu is a giant in Chinese mythology who seeks to capture the sun. Kuafu is described as Houtu's grandson.

long_description.id: Ia mengejar matahari dari timur ke barat dan meminum Sungai Kuning serta Sungai Wei. Air sungai tidak menghilangkan hausnya dan ia mati akibat kekurangan air. Tongkat kayunya berubah menjadi hutan pohon persik. Versi lain mengisahkan tubuhnya menjadi pegunungan.
long_description.en: He pursues the sun east to west and drinks from the Yellow and Wei rivers. The river water cannot quench his thirst, and he dies from dehydration. His wooden club becomes a forest of peach trees. Another version describes his body becoming a mountain range.

long_description.id: Dalam Shanhaijing, Kuafu dicatat mengenakan dua ular kuning di telinga dan memegang dua ular kuning, dan ia keturunan Houtu melalui Xin. Dahuang Bei Jing menceritakan bahwa ia mengejar bayangan matahari, menyusulnya di Yugu, lalu wafat sebelum mencapai rawa besar. Haiwai Bei Jing menyebutnya mati kehausan setelah minum dari Sungai He dan Sungai Wei, dan tongkatnya menjadi hutan Deng. Dahuang Bei Jing juga menyebut Yinglong membunuh Kuafu.
long_description.en: In the Shanhaijing, Kuafu is recorded wearing two yellow snakes at his ears and holding two yellow snakes, and he descends from Houtu through Xin. The Dahuang Bei Jing says he chased the sun's shadow, overtook it at Yugu, and died before reaching the great marsh. The Haiwai Bei Jing has him die of thirst after drinking from the He and Wei rivers, his staff becoming the Deng forest. The Dahuang Bei Jing also says Yinglong killed Kuafu.

role.id: Raksasa yang mengejar matahari dan mati kehausan
role.en: The giant who chases the sun and dies of thirst

summary.id: Kuafu berlomba lari dengan matahari, minum dari Sungai Kuning dan Sungai Wei, lalu mati kehausan; tongkat yang ia buang menjadi hutan Deng.
summary.en: Kuafu races the sun, drinks from the Yellow and Wei rivers, then dies of thirst; the staff he discarded becomes the Deng forest.

description.id: Hutan persik yang tumbuh dari tongkat Kuafu; Shanhaijing menyebutnya hutan Deng (鄧林).
description.en: The peach forest that grows from Kuafu's staff; the Shanhaijing calls it the Deng forest (鄧林).

note.en: Wikipedia calls Kuafu a grandson of Houtu; the Shanhaijing says Houtu begot Xin and Xin begot Kuafu.

note.en: The Dahuang Bei Jing says Yinglong killed Chiyou and then Kuafu.

statement.en: The Shanhaijing (Great Wilderness, North) records a man named Kuafu in the Great Wilderness who wears two yellow snakes at his ears and holds two yellow snakes; Houtu begot Xin, and Xin begot Kuafu.

claims.quote: 夸父不量力，欲追日景，逮之于禺谷。將飲河而不足也，將走大澤，未至，死于此。應龍已殺蚩尤，又殺夸父，乃去南方處之，故南方多雨。

statement.id: Dalam Dahuang Bei Jing, Kuafu yang tidak menakar kekuatannya hendak mengejar bayangan matahari dan menyusulnya di Yugu; ia hendak minum dari sungai tetapi tidak cukup, menuju rawa besar, dan wafat sebelum sampai. statement.en: In the Dahuang Bei Jing, Kuafu, who overestimated his strength, sought to chase the sun's shadow and overtook it at Yugu; he tried to drink from the river but it was not enough, headed for the great marsh, and died before reaching it. The same text also says Yinglong had killed Chiyou and then Kuafu.

claims.quote: 夸父與日逐走，入日。渴，欲得飲，飲於河、渭，河、渭不足，北飲大澤。未至，道渴而死。棄其杖，化為鄧林。

statement.id: Dalam Haiwai Bei Jing, Kuafu berlomba lari dengan matahari lalu haus; ia minum dari Sungai He dan Sungai Wei yang tidak cukup, hendak minum di rawa besar di utara, tetapi mati kehausan di tengah jalan, dan tongkat yang ia buang menjadi hutan Deng.
statement.en: In the Haiwai Bei Jing, Kuafu races the sun and grows thirsty; he drinks from the He and Wei rivers, which are not enough, heads north to drink at the great marsh, and dies of thirst on the way; the staff he discarded turns into the Deng forest.

summary.id: Dahuang Bei Jing: ia wafat sebelum mencapai rawa besar, dan teks yang sama juga menyebut Yinglong membunuh Kuafu.
summary.en: Dahuang Bei Jing: he dies before reaching the great marsh, and the same text also says Yinglong killed Kuafu.

short_description.id: Kudan adalah yōkai peramal Jepang berkepala manusia dan bertubuh sapi, yang dikatakan meramalkan bencana atau panen dalam beberapa hari setelah lahir, lalu mati.
short_description.en: Kudan is a Japanese prophetic yōkai with a human head and bovine body, said to prophesy disaster or harvest within days of birth and then die.

long_description.id: Kudan adalah yōkai bertipe "binatang peramal" yang beritanya atau legenda kotanya tersebar di Jepang sejak zaman Edo. Ia umumnya digambarkan berkepala manusia dan bertubuh sapi. Namanya ditulis dengan aksara untuk manusia dan sapi. Kamus menggambarkannya sebagai yōkai berkepala manusia dan bertubuh sapi yang meramalkan bencana dan wabah dalam beberapa hari setelah lahir lalu dikatakan mati.
long_description.en: The kudan is a prophecy-beast yōkai whose tales and rumors have circulated in Japan since the Edo period. It is generally depicted with a human head and a bovine body, and its name is written with the characters for person and cow. Dictionaries describe it prophesying disasters and epidemics within days of birth and then, it is said, dying.

long_description.id: Kudan yang konon muncul di Gunung Kurahashi, Provinsi Tango, pada Tenpō 7 (1836) dilaporkan dalam sebuah kawaraban. Ia meramalkan panen melimpah dan menyuruh orang menempel gambarnya di rumah untuk menolak bala. Catatan awal lain terdapat dalam diary tahun 1819 tentang anak sapi berkepala manusia yang berbicara dan menyebut dirinya kudan.
long_description.en: A kudan that allegedly appeared on Mount Kurahashi in Tango Province in Tenpō 7 (1836) was reported in a kawaraban. It predicted a bountiful harvest and told people to paste up its picture at home to ward off evil. Another early attestation is a diary of 1819 about a human-headed speaking calf that named itself kudan.

long_description.id: Kudan tergolong "binatang peramal" yang tidak hanya meramalkan wabah atau panen tetapi juga memberi cara menghindarinya. Menurut Yokai.com, gambar kudan dipakai sebagai jimat. Sosiolog Kenji Sato berteori bahwa kudan mungkin berasal dari makhluk pembawa untung Tiongkok, Bai Ze. Setelah zaman Edo, kudan masih disebut dalam tulisan, dan Lafcadio Hearn mendengar tentang pemain keliling yang memamerkan spesimen kudan yang diawetkan.
long_description.en: The kudan is typical of the prophecy beasts, which not only portend plague or bounty but prescribe how to avoid them. According to Yokai.com, images of kudan were used as talismans. The sociologist Kenji Sato theorizes the kudan may derive from the Chinese luck beast Bai Ze. After the Edo period the kudan was still mentioned in writings, and Lafcadio Hearn heard of travelling showmen displaying a stuffed kudan.

literal_meaning.en: a combination of the characters for "person" (人) and "cow" (牛)

description.id: Dalam beberapa hari setelah lahir, kudan meramalkan bencana, wabah, atau panen, lalu dikatakan mati.
description.en: Within days of birth the kudan prophesies disasters, epidemics or harvests, and is then said to die.

description.id: Kawaraban sezaman melaporkan kudan di Gunung Kurahashi, Provinsi Tango, dan disebut sebagai bahan tertulis folkloris tertua yang masih ada tentang kudan.
description.en: A contemporary kawaraban reported a kudan on Mount Kurahashi in Tango Province and is called the earliest extant written folkloric material on the kudan.

statement.en: The kudan is typical of the so-called prophecy beasts (yogenjū) of Japanese folklore, which not only portend plague or bounty but prescribe how to avoid being stricken.

claims.quote: The kudan may derive from the Chinese luck beast Bai Ze (pronounced "Hakutaku" in Japanese), as has been formally theorized by sociologist Kenji Sato

statement.id: Kudan mungkin berasal dari makhluk pembawa untung Tiongkok Bai Ze (Hakutaku dalam bahasa Jepang), seperti yang diteorikan secara formal oleh sosiolog Kenji Sato.
statement.en: The kudan may derive from the Chinese luck beast Bai Ze (Hakutaku in Japanese), as formally theorized by the sociologist Kenji Sato.

claims.quote: However while the kudan monster dates to the late Edo Period, the idiom is much older, dating to the Heian period, so the relationship between the phrase and the monster has been refuted as an anachronism.

statement.id: Wikipedia menyebut ungkapan "kudan no gotoshi" jauh lebih tua (zaman Heian) daripada makhluknya (akhir zaman Edo), sehingga kaitan antara frasa dan makhluk itu dibantah sebagai anakronisme.
statement.en: Wikipedia says the idiom "kudan no gotoshi" is much older (Heian period) than the monster (late Edo period), so a relationship between phrase and monster has been refuted as an anachronism.

claims.quote: After the shogunate ended and the Meiji era began, the kudan was still mentioned in writings and Lafcadio Hearn heard about travelling showmen displaying an alleged stuffed specimen of a kudan.

statement.id: Setelah zaman keshogunan berakhir dan era Meiji dimulai, kudan masih disebut dalam tulisan, dan Lafcadio Hearn mendengar tentang pemain keliling yang memamerkan spesimen kudan yang diawetkan.
statement.en: After the shogunate ended and the Meiji era began, the kudan was still mentioned in writings, and Lafcadio Hearn heard of travelling showmen displaying an alleged stuffed kudan.

claims.quote: The kutabe or kudabe is considered an equivalent (subclass) of the kudan, though kutabe's legend is set specifically in Tateyama in Etchū Province (Mount Tate, in today's Toyama Prefecture).

statement.id: Kutabe atau kudabe dianggap setara (subkelas) kudan, tetapi legendanya berlatar khusus di Tateyama, Provinsi Etchū (kini Prefektur Toyama).
statement.en: The kutabe or kudabe is considered an equivalent (subclass) of the kudan, though its legend is set specifically at Tateyama in Etchū Province (now Toyama Prefecture).

claims.quote: dated Tenpō 7 (1836) is the earliest extant written folkloric material on the "kudan" proper.

statement.id: Berita tentang kudan dalam kawaraban bertanggal Tenpō 7 (1836) adalah bahan tertulis folkloris tertua yang masih ada tentang kudan.
statement.en: The kudan news in the kawaraban dated Tenpō 7 (1836) is the earliest extant written folkloric material on the kudan proper.

claims.quote: argues that the kudan and the ushi-onna ought to be distinguished, due to a number of differences: the kudan is a calf born from cattle, the ushi-onna is a daughter of human parents

statement.id: Seorang penulis berpendapat kudan dan ushi-onna perlu dibedakan: kudan adalah anak sapi yang lahir dari sapi, sedangkan ushi-onna adalah putri orang tua manusia.
statement.en: A writer argues that the kudan and the ushi-onna ought to be distinguished: the kudan is a calf born from cattle, whereas the ushi-onna is a daughter of human parents.

claims.quote: In the Taisho era, novelist Hyakken Uchida published a short novel entitled Kudan (1921)

statement.id: Pada era Taishō, novelis Hyakken Uchida menerbitkan novel pendek berjudul Kudan (1921).
statement.en: In the Taishō era the novelist Hyakken Uchida published a short novel entitled Kudan (1921).

claims.quote: 日本の妖怪。半人半牛の姿で、生まれて数日の間に災害や疫病の予言をし、言い終えると死んでしまうとされる。

statement.en: The dictionary describes the kudan as a half-human, half-bovine yōkai that in the first few days after birth prophesies disasters and epidemics and is said to die once it has spoken.

claims.quote: 頭が人、体が牛の形をした妖怪。疫病の流行や災害などについて予言するといわれる。

statement.id: Kamus lain memberi definisi kudan sebagai yōkai berkepala manusia dan bertubuh sapi yang dikatakan meramalkan wabah dan bencana.
statement.en: Another dictionary entry defines the kudan as a yōkai with a human head and a bovine body, said to prophesy epidemics and disasters.

claims.quote: Kudan are able to speak human languages from the day they are born. Immediately upon being born, a kudan gives one or more prophecies.

statement.en: According to Yokai.com, kudan can speak human languages from the day they are born and give one or more prophecies immediately after birth.

claims.quote: Because of its reputation for honesty, images of kudan were used as talismans for good luck, prosperity, and protection from sickness and disaster.

claims.quote: During the Edo period, newspapers looking to add credibility to a story would include the words “kudan no gotoshi,” or, “as if a kudan had said it” to their articles.

statement.id: Menurut Yokai.com, pada zaman Edo surat kabar menambahkan kata "kudan no gotoshi" ("seolah kudan yang mengatakannya") agar cerita lebih dipercaya.

claims.quote: Sakyo Komatsu also wrote a piece of fiction entitled Kudan no haha (「くだんのはは」 ; lit. "kudan's mother") (1968)

short_description.id: Kurangaituku adalah makhluk gaib separuh perempuan separuh burung dalam mitologi Māori, yang menawan Hatupatu dan tewas di Whakarewarewa.
short_description.en: Kurangaituku is a supernatural being in Māori mythology, half woman and half bird, who held Hatupatu captive and died at Whakarewarewa.

long_description.id: Kurangaituku adalah makhluk gaib separuh perempuan separuh burung dalam mitologi Māori seperti dikisahkan oleh iwi Te Arawa dan Raukawa. Kamus Tregear mencatatnya sebagai ogress yang bersayap pada lengannya, dapat menombak burung dengan bibirnya, dan hidup dari makanan mentah. Ia juga kadang dikenal sebagai Hine-ingoingo.
long_description.en: Kurangaituku is a half-woman, half-bird supernatural being of Māori mythology, as told by the Te Arawa and Raukawa iwi. Tregear's dictionary describes her as an ogress with wings on her arms who speared birds with her lips and ate raw food. She is also sometimes known as Hine-ingoingo.

long_description.id: Dalam kisah Hatupatu, ia menemukan sang pemuda dan membawanya ke rumahnya; Hatupatu ditawan di gua bersama burung dan kadal peliharaan. Suatu hari ketika Kurangaituku berburu, Hatupatu menggunakan taiaha miliknya untuk menghancurkan kadal dan burung peliharaannya dan mencuri korowai bulunya yang berharga.
long_description.en: In the story of Hatupatu, she finds the youth and takes him to her home; Hatupatu is imprisoned in her cave along with pet birds and lizards. One day while Kurangaituku is out hunting, Hatupatu uses her taiaha to destroy her pet lizards and birds and steals her treasured feather cloaks.

long_description.id: Dalam kumpulan Grey, seekor burung peliharaan yang lolos terbang menjemput Kurangaituku, yang sampai ke guanya hanya dalam tiga langkah. Hatupatu mengucapkan mantra, batu terbuka dan ia bersembunyi di dalamnya, dan Kurangaituku tidak dapat menemukannya. Tregear mencatat bahwa ia terbang mengejar si pelarian, dan di Whakarewarewa ia melewati kolam lumpur mendidih dan tewas terbakar.
long_description.en: In Grey's collection, a pet bird that escaped flew off to fetch Kurangaituku, who reached her cave in only three strides. Hatupatu repeats a charm, the rock opens and he hides in it, and Kurangaituku cannot find him. Tregear records that she flew after her truant, and at Whakarewarewa she went through the boiling mud pools and was burned to death.
