long_description.id: Lady in Red dilaporkan di gedung Weckesser, Wilkes University [lady-in-red-c04], di Charleston sebagai hantu Nettie Dickerson yang tersambar petir [lady-in-red-c05], dan di Drake Hotel Chicago sebagai perempuan cemburu yang melompat [lady-in-red-c06]. Di Mizpah Hotel, Nevada, ia dikenal sebagai "Rose" yang tewas di tangan kekasih cemburu [lady-in-red-c07], meski satu sumber mencatat tidak ada catatan yang menegaskan identitas atau pembunuhan itu [lady-in-red-c08].
long_description.en: Lady in Red sightings are reported at the Weckesser building, Wilkes University [lady-in-red-c04], in Charleston as the ghost of Nettie Dickerson, killed by lightning [lady-in-red-c05], and at Chicago's Drake Hotel as a jealous woman who jumped [lady-in-red-c06]. At the Mizpah Hotel in Nevada she is known as "Rose", who died at the hands of a jealous lover [lady-in-red-c07], though one source notes there are no records confirming her identity or the murder [lady-in-red-c08].

long_description.id: Laporan lain datang dari stasiun Lower Bay Toronto [lady-in-red-c09], di Pluckley Inggris sejak abad ke-12 [lady-in-red-c10], dan di Sungai Bang Pakong Thailand [lady-in-red-c11]. Artikel Historic Hotels of America menyebut pria di Mizpah mendengar suara membisikkan rayuan [lady-in-red-c14] dan tamu menemukan mutiara di bawah bantal [lady-in-red-c15], serta bahwa ia dikatakan baik, ramah, dan murah hati [lady-in-red-c16].
long_description.en: Other reports come from Toronto's Lower Bay station [lady-in-red-c09], at Pluckley in England since the 12th century [lady-in-red-c10], and at the Bang Pakong River in Thailand [lady-in-red-c11]. The Historic Hotels of America article says men at the Mizpah hear a voice whispering sweet nothings [lady-in-red-c14] and guests find a pearl beneath their pillows [lady-in-red-c15], and that she was said to be kind, welcoming and generous [lady-in-red-c16].

who.id: Hantu perempuan bergaun merah, mirip White Lady, yang dikaitkan dengan kekasih dicampakkan atau perempuan sombong [lady-in-red-c01, lady-in-red-c02].
who.en: A red-dressed female ghost like the White Lady, tied to jilted lovers or vain women [lady-in-red-c01, lady-in-red-c02].

origin.id: Kisahnya dilaporkan di banyak tempat, termasuk Toronto, Pluckley, dan Sungai Bang Pakong [lady-in-red-c09, lady-in-red-c10, lady-in-red-c11].
origin.en: Its stories are reported in many places, including Toronto, Pluckley and the Bang Pakong River [lady-in-red-c09, lady-in-red-c10, lady-in-red-c11].

role.en: Typically friendly, attached to historic hotels, theatres or public places [lady-in-red-c03].

famous_for.en: Known as "Rose" at the Mizpah Hotel, a ghost who whispers sweet nothings and leaves pearls [lady-in-red-c07, lady-in-red-c14, lady-in-red-c15].

did_you_know.id: Di Mizpah Hotel, tamu konon menemukan mutiara di bawah bantal, yang disebut berasal dari kalung Lady in Red yang putus [lady-in-red-c15].
did_you_know.en: At the Mizpah Hotel, guests are said to find a pearl beneath their pillows, supposedly from the Lady in Red's broken necklace [lady-in-red-c15].

sources.title: Meet the Lady in Red: Nevada's Most Famous Ghost
sources.publisher: Historic Hotels of America (National Trust for Historic Preservation)

claims.quote: A Lady in Red or Red Lady is a type of female ghost, similar to the White Lady, but according to legend is more specifically attributed to a jilted lover, killed in a fit of passion, or a woman of vanity.

statement.id: Lady in Red adalah jenis hantu perempuan yang mirip White Lady, tetapi menurut legenda lebih khusus dikaitkan dengan kekasih yang dicampakkan, korban pembunuhan karena emosi, atau perempuan yang sombong.
statement.en: The Lady in Red is a type of female ghost like the White Lady, attributed in legend to a jilted lover, a victim of passion, or a vain woman.

claims.quote: In all cases, the Lady in Red is wearing a scarlet or blood red dress.

statement.id: Dalam semua versi, ia bergaun merah tua atau merah darah.
statement.en: In all cases she wears a scarlet or blood-red dress.

claims.quote: She is said to typically be friendly in disposition, with a story attached to historic hotels, theatres or other public places

statement.id: Ia biasanya digambarkan ramah, dan kisahnya melekat pada hotel bersejarah, teater, atau tempat umum lain.
statement.en: She is usually friendly, with stories tied to historic hotels, theatres and other public places.

claims.quote: At Wilkes University in Wilkes-Barre, Pennsylvania, the Weckesser building is reportedly haunted by a Lady in Red that according to one witness appears real until vanishing.

statement.id: Gedung Weckesser di Wilkes University, Wilkes-Barre, Pennsylvania, konon dihantui Lady in Red yang menurut seorang saksi tampak nyata sampai menghilang.
statement.en: The Weckesser building at Wilkes University in Wilkes-Barre, Pennsylvania, is reportedly haunted by a Lady in Red who, according to one witness, appears real until vanishing.

claims.quote: In Charleston, South Carolina, near Dock Street Theatre, a Lady in Red is said to be the ghost of Nettie Dickerson, a prostitute who frequented the Planter's Hotel (now the historic French Quarter building). ... At the age of 25 she was standing in her red dress on the balcony of the hotel during a storm when she was struck by lightning and killed.

statement.id: Di Charleston, South Carolina, dekat Dock Street Theatre, Lady in Red konon hantu Nettie Dickerson, pelacur yang sering mengunjungi Planter's Hotel; pada usia 25 tahun ia berdiri bergaun merah di balkon hotel saat badai dan tersambar petir hingga tewas.
statement.en: In Charleston, South Carolina, near Dock Street Theatre, a Lady in Red is said to be the ghost of Nettie Dickerson, a prostitute who frequented the Planter's Hotel; at 25 she was standing in her red dress on the hotel balcony during a storm when she was struck by lightning and killed.

claims.quote: In Chicago's Drake Hotel, a jealous woman wearing a blood-red dress took her life after jumping from the 10th floor (or the roof, as accounts vary). Guests claim to see her in her last steps from the Gold Coast Room, the Palm Court, and on the 10th floor.

statement.id: Di Drake Hotel Chicago, seorang perempuan cemburu bergaun merah darah mengakhiri hidup dengan melompat dari lantai 10 (atau atap, tergantung versi); tamu mengaku melihat langkah terakhirnya dari Gold Coast Room, Palm Court, dan di lantai 10.
statement.en: At Chicago's Drake Hotel, a jealous woman in a blood-red dress took her life by jumping from the 10th floor (or the roof, as accounts vary); guests claim to see her last steps from the Gold Coast Room, the Palm Court and on the 10th floor.

claims.quote: The fifth floor of the Mizpah Hotel in Nevada is known for a Lady in Red known as "Rose" (her prostitute name) who died at the hands of a jealous lover.

statement.id: Lantai lima Mizpah Hotel di Nevada dikenal karena Lady in Red bernama "Rose" (nama pelacurnya) yang tewas di tangan kekasih yang cemburu.
statement.en: The fifth floor of the Mizpah Hotel in Nevada is known for a Lady in Red called "Rose" (her prostitute name) who died at the hands of a jealous lover.

claims.quote: According to one source, Rose's real name, was Evelyn May Johnston, though there are no records to confirm that a woman by this name existed at that time, nor that a murder similar to the "Red Lady" crime ever took place in the hotel.

statement.id: Menurut satu sumber, nama asli Rose adalah Evelyn May Johnston, tetapi tidak ada catatan yang menegaskan bahwa perempuan bernama itu ada pada masa itu, atau bahwa pembunuhan serupa kasus "Red Lady" pernah terjadi di hotel itu.
statement.en: According to one source, Rose's real name was Evelyn May Johnston, though there are no records confirming that a woman by that name existed at the time, or that a murder like the "Red Lady" crime ever took place in the hotel.

claims.quote: Toronto's Lower Bay transit station has been closed since 1966 but has numerous reports of a Lady in Red. According to witnesses, the ghost appears distraught as it glides without feet or eyes.

statement.id: Stasiun transit Lower Bay di Toronto ditutup sejak 1966 tetapi punya banyak laporan Lady in Red; menurut saksi, hantu itu tampak terpukul dan meluncur tanpa kaki atau mata.
statement.en: Toronto's Lower Bay transit station has been closed since 1966 but has numerous reports of a Lady in Red; according to witnesses the ghost appears distraught and glides without feet or eyes.

claims.quote: A Red Lady is said to walk around the Church of St Nicholas in Pluckley, England since the 12th century.

statement.id: Seorang Red Lady konon berjalan di sekitar Gereja St Nicholas di Pluckley, Inggris, sejak abad ke-12.
statement.en: A Red Lady is said to walk around the Church of St Nicholas in Pluckley, England, since the 12th century.

claims.quote: In Thailand, there is a story of a Lady in Red, believed to be the spirit of a woman who drowned in the Bang Pakong River. Witnesses have reported seeing her while driving across the Bang Pakong River Bridge at night.

statement.id: Di Thailand ada kisah Lady in Red yang dipercaya roh perempuan yang tenggelam di Sungai Bang Pakong; saksi melaporkan melihatnya saat berkendara melintasi Jembatan Sungai Bang Pakong pada malam hari.
statement.en: In Thailand there is a story of a Lady in Red believed to be the spirit of a woman who drowned in the Bang Pakong River; witnesses report seeing her while driving across the Bang Pakong River Bridge at night.

claims.quote: In the film Crimson Peak, Allerdale Hall is haunted by Red Lady ghosts whose red color comes from being buried in red clay vats.

statement.id: Dalam film Crimson Peak, Allerdale Hall dihantui hantu Red Lady yang warna merahnya berasal dari dikubur dalam bak tanah liat merah.
statement.en: In the film Crimson Peak, Allerdale Hall is haunted by Red Lady ghosts whose red color comes from being buried in red clay vats.

claims.quote: Korean drama series The Ghost Detective is named for a Lady in Red that accompanies the main character in solving crimes.

statement.id: Serial drama Korea The Ghost Detective dinamai menurut Lady in Red yang menemani tokoh utama memecahkan kejahatan.
statement.en: The Korean drama series The Ghost Detective is named for a Lady in Red who accompanies the main character in solving crimes.

claims.quote: In spite of her brutal end, many men visiting the Mizpah Hotel have reported hearing an incorporeal voice whispering sweet nothings in their ears—especially in that fancy elevator, which the Lady in Red used to escort her visitors from the lobby to her chambers.

statement.id: Menurut artikel Historic Hotels of America, banyak pria yang menginap di Mizpah Hotel melaporkan mendengar suara tanpa wujud membisikkan rayuan di telinga mereka, terutama di lift mewah yang dulu dipakai Lady in Red mengantar tamunya dari lobi ke kamarnya.
statement.en: According to the Historic Hotels of America article, many men visiting the Mizpah Hotel report hearing an incorporeal voice whispering sweet nothings in their ears, especially in the fancy elevator the Lady in Red used to escort her visitors from the lobby to her chambers.

claims.quote: In addition, hundreds of guests have awakened to discover a pearl beneath their pillows—supposedly from her necklace, which broke and spilled onto the floor in her tragic scuffle.

statement.id: Menurut artikel itu, ratusan tamu terbangun dan menemukan mutiara di bawah bantal mereka, konon dari kalungnya yang putus dan berserakan di lantai saat pergumulan tragisnya.
statement.en: According to the article, hundreds of guests have awakened to find a pearl beneath their pillows, supposedly from her necklace, which broke and spilled onto the floor in her tragic scuffle.

claims.quote: Although the Lady in Red’s origins and true identity are lost to history (many accounts suggest she went, appropriately, by just “Rose”), she was said to be kind, welcoming, and generous—and, evidently, still is.

statement.id: Menurut artikel itu, asal-usul dan identitas aslinya hilang ditelan sejarah (banyak catatan menyebutnya hanya "Rose"), tetapi ia dikatakan baik, ramah, dan murah hati, dan tampaknya masih demikian.
statement.en: According to the article, her origins and true identity are lost to history (many accounts suggest she went by just "Rose"), but she was said to be kind, welcoming and generous, and evidently still is.

claims.quote: At least until an ex-lover, possibly a former patron, stabbed and strangled her in a fit of jealous rage.

statement.id: Menurut artikel itu, kisahnya berakhir ketika mantan kekasih, mungkin bekas pelanggan, menusuk dan mencekiknya dalam amarah cemburu.
statement.en: According to the article, her story ended when an ex-lover, possibly a former patron, stabbed and strangled her in a fit of jealous rage.

summary.en: Rose died at the hands of a jealous lover.

summary.id: Mantan kekasih, mungkin bekas pelanggan, menusuk dan mencekiknya.

summary.id: Tidak ada catatan yang menegaskan nama aslinya atau bahwa pembunuhan itu terjadi; identitasnya hilang ditelan sejarah.
summary.en: No records confirm her real name or that the murder took place; her identity is lost to history.

short_description.id: Lake Tianchi Monster adalah nama kriptid yang dilaporkan menghuni danau di Gunung Baekdu.
short_description.en: Lake Tianchi Monster names a cryptid reportedly inhabiting the lake on Mount Baekdu.

long_description.id: Lake Tianchi Monster adalah nama kriptid yang dilaporkan menghuni danau di Gunung Baekdu. Laporan penampakan awal bertanggal 1903 menyebut makhluk mirip kerbau yang kembali ke air setelah ditembak.
long_description.en: Lake Tianchi Monster names a cryptid reportedly inhabiting the lake on Mount Baekdu. An early sighting report dated 1903 describes a buffalo-like creature retreating into water after being shot.

long_description.id: Laporan awal bertanggal 1903 menyebut makhluk mirip kerbau yang menyerang tiga orang dan kembali ke air setelah ditembak enam kali. Pada 21 sampai 23 Agustus 1962, seseorang yang memakai teleskop dikabarkan melihat dua makhluk saling mengejar di air, dan lebih dari seratus orang melaporkan penampakan. Pada pagi 11 Juli, beberapa kader pemerintah daerah melihat sekawanan makhluk misterius, dan seorang pejabat kehutanan mengatakan makhluk-makhluk itu muncul lima kali dalam sekitar 50 menit.
long_description.en: An early report dated 1903 describes a buffalo-like creature that attacked three people and returned to the water after being shot six times. Over 21 to 23 August 1962, someone looking through a telescope is said to have seen two creatures chasing each other in the water, and over a hundred people reported sightings. On the morning of July 11, several local government cadres saw a school of mysterious creatures, and a forestry official said they appeared five times within about 50 minutes.

long_description.id: Laporan lain menggambarkan kepala mirip manusia pada leher panjang dengan cincin putih dan kulit abu-abu mulus, sedangkan wisatawan melaporkan monster hitam berkepala mirip kuda yang melompat dari air seperti anjing laut. Pada 2007, Zhuo Yongsheng menyatakan merekam enam makhluk yang menurutnya mirip anjing laut dan bersirip, dan dapat berenang secepat kapal pesiar.
long_description.en: Other reports describe a human-like head on a long neck with a white ring and smooth grey skin, while sightseers reported a black monster with a horse-like head that jumped out of the water like a seal. In 2007, Zhuo Yongsheng claimed to have filmed six seal-like, finned creatures that could swim as fast as yachts.

long_description.id: Para ilmuwan menepis laporan-laporan ini. Alasan yang dikemukakan meliputi letusan gunung berapi yang membuat kehidupan berbahaya bagi hewan di danau, dan danau yang dinilai terlalu dingin untuk kehidupan. Kaum skeptis menyebut penampakan itu hanya imajinasi atau batu vulkanik yang mengapung.
long_description.en: Scientists dismiss these reports. The reasons given include volcanic eruptions that would make life hazardous for any animal in the lake, and a lake judged too cold for life. Skeptics say the sightings are only imagination or a floating volcanic rock.

description.id: Zhuo Yongsheng dikutip mengatakan makhluk-makhluk itu dapat berenang secepat kapal pesiar.
description.en: Zhuo Yongsheng was quoted as saying the creatures could swim as fast as yachts.

description.id: Danau di puncak Gunung Baekdu di Pegunungan Baekdu-daegan dan Changbai, mencakup Provinsi Jilin di Tiongkok dan Provinsi Ryanggang di Korea Utara.
description.en: Lake at the peak of Baekdu Mountain within the Baekdu-daegan and Changbai mountain ranges, encompassing Jilin Province of China and Ryanggang Province of North Korea.

description.id: Makhluk mirip kerbau dilaporkan menyerang tiga orang, ditembak enam kali, lalu kembali ke bawah air.
description.en: A buffalo-like creature was reported to attack three people, was shot six times, then retreated under the water.

description.id: Seseorang yang memakai teleskop dilaporkan melihat dua makhluk saling mengejar di air; lebih dari seratus orang melaporkan penampakan.
description.en: A person using a telescope reportedly saw two creatures chasing each other in the water; more than a hundred people reported the sightings.

description.id: Zhuo Yongsheng menyatakan merekam video 20 menit tentang enam makhluk tak dikenal di danau vulkanik.
description.en: Zhuo Yongsheng said he shot a 20-minute video of six unidentified creatures in the volcanic lake.

sources.title: Reporter ‘finds’ China’s own Loch Ness monster
sources.author: Staff Reporter

claims.quote: Lake Tianchi Monster is the name given to what is said to be a cryptid that lives in Heaven Lake (known as Cheonji in Korean) located in the peak of Baekdu Mountain within the Baekdu-daegan and Changbai mountain ranges encompassing Jilin Province of China and Ryanggang Province of North Korea.

statement.id: Lake Tianchi Monster adalah nama untuk kriptid yang konon hidup di Danau Heaven (Cheonji dalam bahasa Korea) di puncak Gunung Baekdu, dalam pegunungan Baekdu-daegan dan Changbai yang mencakup Provinsi Jilin di Tiongkok dan Provinsi Ryanggang di Korea Utara.
statement.en: Lake Tianchi Monster is the name given to a cryptid said to live in Heaven Lake (Cheonji in Korean) at the peak of Baekdu Mountain, within the Baekdu-daegan and Changbai mountain ranges encompassing Jilin Province of China and Ryanggang Province of North Korea.

claims.quote: The first reported sighting was in 1903. It was claimed that a large buffalo-like creature attacked three people, but was shot six times. The monster then retreated under the water.

statement.id: Laporan penampakan awal bertanggal 1903 menyebut makhluk mirip kerbau yang kembali ke air setelah ditembak.
statement.en: An early sighting report dated 1903 describes a buffalo-like creature retreating into water after being shot.

claims.quote: In 21 to 23 August 1962, a person using a telescope reportedly saw two of the monsters chasing each other in water. More than a hundred people reported the sightings.

statement.id: Laporan Agustus 1962 menyebut dua makhluk terlihat saling mengejar dalam air.
statement.en: An August 1962 report describes two creatures chasing each other in the water.

claims.quote: More recent reports describe the monster as having a human-like head attached to a 1.5-meter (5 ft) neck. It is said to have a white ring around the bottom of its neck, and the rest of its skin is grey and smooth.

statement.id: Laporan lain menggambarkan kepala mirip manusia pada leher sepanjang sekitar 1,5 meter.
statement.en: Other reports describe a human-like head on a neck about 1.5 meters long.

claims.quote: In 2007, Zhuo Yongsheng, a Chinese TV reporter said he had shot a 20-minute video of six unidentified creatures in the volcanic lake on 6 September. He later sent still photos to Xinhua's Jilin provincial bureau. According to a news report one of these showed the six "Nessies" swimming in parallel in three pairs.

statement.id: Pada 2007, Zhuo Yongsheng menyatakan merekam enam makhluk tak dikenal di danau.
statement.en: In 2007, Zhuo Yongsheng claimed to film six unidentified creatures in the lake.

claims.quote: On the morning of July 11, several local government cadres caught sight of a school of mysterious creatures swimming through the lake in the Changbai mountains, in north-eastern Jilin province, the Beijing Youth Daily said on Tuesday.

statement.id: Pada pagi 11 Juli, beberapa kader pemerintah daerah melihat sekawanan makhluk misterius berenang di danau di Pegunungan Changbai, Provinsi Jilin, menurut Beijing Youth Daily.
statement.en: On the morning of July 11, several local government cadres saw a school of mysterious creatures swimming through the lake in the Changbai mountains, in Jilin province, according to the Beijing Youth Daily.

claims.quote: "Within about 50 minutes, the monsters appeared five times," it quoted one of the officials, provincial forestry bureau vice-director Zhang Lufeng, as saying. "At times there was one, at times there were several. The last time, there was as many as about 20."

statement.id: Seorang pejabat kehutanan provinsi dikutip mengatakan makhluk-makhluk itu muncul lima kali dalam sekitar 50 menit, kadang satu, kadang beberapa, hingga sekitar 20 pada kali terakhir.
statement.en: A provincial forestry official was quoted as saying the monsters appeared five times within about 50 minutes, at times one, at times several, as many as about 20 the last time.

claims.quote: He said the creatures, two to three kilometres (1.25-2 miles) in the distance, appeared only as white or black spots. But from the ripples in the water, he and others determined the spots were "living beings.

statement.id: Ia mengatakan makhluk-makhluk itu, pada jarak dua sampai tiga kilometer, hanya tampak sebagai bintik putih atau hitam, tetapi dari riak air ia dan yang lain menyimpulkan bahwa bintik itu makhluk hidup.
statement.en: He said the creatures, two to three kilometres in the distance, appeared only as white or black spots, but from the ripples in the water he and others determined the spots were living beings.

claims.quote: Another sighting compared the head of the monster to that of a human, except with big round eyes, a protruding mouth and a neck 1.2 to 1.5 metres long. It also had a white ring separating its neck and torso and smooth, grey skin.

statement.id: Laporan lain membandingkan kepala makhluk itu dengan kepala manusia, tetapi bermata bulat besar dan berbibir menonjol, berleher 1,2 sampai 1,5 meter, bercincin putih di antara leher dan badan, dan berkulit abu-abu mulus.
statement.en: Another sighting compared the monster's head to a human head but with big round eyes and a protruding mouth, a neck 1.2 to 1.5 metres long, a white ring separating neck and torso, and smooth grey skin.

claims.quote: Hundreds of sightseers visiting the area have also reported spotting a black monster with a horse-like head. A Chinese paper quoted local tourism official Meng Fanying as saying that the creature was spotted just 10 metres from the bank, jumping out of the water from time to time like a seal.

statement.id: Ratusan wisatawan melaporkan melihat monster hitam berkepala mirip kuda; seorang pejabat pariwisata setempat dikutip mengatakan makhluk itu terlihat sekitar 10 meter dari tepi dan sesekali melompat keluar dari air seperti anjing laut.
statement.en: Hundreds of sightseers reported a black monster with a horse-like head; a local tourism official was quoted as saying it was spotted about 10 metres from the bank, jumping out of the water from time to time like a seal.

claims.quote: Scientists dismiss the reports, saying volcanic eruptions as recently as 300 years ago would make life hazardous for any animal making the 373-metre deep lake its home.

statement.id: Para ilmuwan menepis laporan itu dengan alasan letusan gunung berapi pada 300 tahun terakhir akan membuat kehidupan berbahaya bagi hewan apa pun di danau sedalam 373 meter itu.
statement.en: Scientists dismiss the reports, saying volcanic eruptions as recently as 300 years ago would make life hazardous for any animal living in the 373-metre deep lake.

claims.quote: Local journalist Zhuo Yongsheng shot footage of six “seal-like” creatures in the north-eastern Tianchi Lake, which local legend has long said is home to Loch Ness-style monsters. “They could swim as fast as yachts and at times they would all disappear in the water,” the Xinhua news agency quoted Zhuo as saying. “Their fins, or maybe wings, were longer than their bodies.”

statement.id: Wartawan setempat Zhuo Yongsheng merekam enam makhluk "mirip anjing laut" di Danau Tianchi; menurut kutipan dari Xinhua, mereka dapat berenang secepat kapal pesiar, sesekali menghilang di air, dan sirip atau sayapnya lebih panjang dari tubuh mereka.
statement.en: Local journalist Zhuo Yongsheng shot footage of six "seal-like" creatures in Tianchi Lake; as quoted by Xinhua, they could swim as fast as yachts, at times all disappeared in the water, and their fins or wings were longer than their bodies.

claims.quote: However, scientists dismissed the reports, saying the lake was too cold for life. Volcanic eruptions would also make life extremely hazardous for any animal making its home there, they said.

statement.id: Para ilmuwan menepis laporan itu dengan alasan danau terlalu dingin untuk kehidupan, dan letusan gunung berapi juga membuat kehidupan sangat berbahaya bagi hewan yang tinggal di sana.
statement.en: Scientists dismissed the reports, saying the lake was too cold for life, and that volcanic eruptions would also make life extremely hazardous for any animal making its home there.

claims.quote: According to Beijing Youth Daily, an estimated 20 monsters were reported; however, "scientists are skeptical that any large creature would be able to survive in the lake given its recent history of volcanic activity", and skeptics say "it's all in the imagination, or just a floating volcanic rock".

statement.id: Menurut Beijing Youth Daily, diperkirakan 20 monster dilaporkan; namun para ilmuwan ragu ada makhluk besar yang dapat bertahan di danau itu mengingat sejarah vulkanisnya yang baru, dan kaum skeptis menyebutnya hanya imajinasi atau batu vulkanik terapung.
statement.en: According to Beijing Youth Daily, an estimated 20 monsters were reported; however scientists are skeptical that any large creature could survive in the lake given its recent volcanic history, and skeptics say it is all imagination or just a floating volcanic rock.

summary.id: Para saksi dan pejabat setempat melaporkan penampakan makhluk di danau.
summary.en: Witnesses and local officials report sightings of creatures in the lake.

summary.id: Para ilmuwan menepis laporan itu, dan kaum skeptis menyebutnya imajinasi atau batu vulkanik yang mengapung.
summary.en: Scientists dismiss the reports, and skeptics call it imagination or a floating volcanic rock.

short_description.id: Leontophone adalah hewan kecil dari tulisan Yunani-Romawi dan bestiari Abad Pertengahan yang begitu beracun sehingga singa yang menggigitnya mati.
short_description.en: The leontophone is a small animal of Greco-Roman writings and Medieval bestiaries so poisonous that a lion biting it dies.

long_description.id: Leontophone, dari bahasa Yunani kuno "pembunuh singa", adalah hewan kecil yang kemungkinan besar legendaris. Ia pertama dicatat penulis Yunani-Romawi lalu masuk bestiari Abad Pertengahan. Singa yang menggigitnya akan mati; dalam ritual yang tepat, dagingnya dibakar dan abunya ditaburkan pada daging umpan di persimpangan jalan untuk meracuni singa.
long_description.en: The leontophone, Ancient Greek for 'lion-killer', is a small and most probably legendary animal. Greco-Roman writers first recorded it, and it later entered Medieval bestiaries. A lion that bites one dies; in the proper ritual its flesh is burned and the ashes scattered on bait meat at a crossroads to poison lions.

long_description.id: Singa membenci leontophone dan mencabiknya dengan cakar alih-alih menggigit. Namun menurut sebagian sumber singa justru lari dan hanya menyerang bila terdesak, karena air seninya pun mematikan. Wujudnya tidak pernah digambarkan pasti: babi hutan kecil, beruang kecil, atau ular.
long_description.en: Lions hate the leontophone and rip it with their claws instead of biting. Yet some sources say the lion runs away and fights only when cornered, because even its urine is deadly. Its look is never fixed: a little boar, a little bear, or a serpent.

who.id: Hewan kecil beracun.
who.en: A small poisonous animal.

origin.id: Tulisan Yunani-Romawi dan bestiari Abad Pertengahan.
origin.en: Greco-Roman writings and Medieval bestiaries.

role.id: Racun bagi singa.
role.en: Poison to lions.

claims.quote: Leontophone (Leontophonus, Leontophonos, Leophontes, from Ancient Greek: λεοντοφόνος, meaning "lion-killer") was a small animal, most probably legendary, that was deadly to lions.

statement.id: Leontophone (Leontophonus, Leontophonos, Leophontes; dari bahasa Yunani Kuno λεοντοφόνος, "pembunuh singa") adalah hewan kecil, kemungkinan besar legendaris, yang mematikan bagi singa.
statement.en: The leontophone (Leontophonus, Leontophonos, Leophontes; from Ancient Greek λεοντοφόνος, 'lion-killer') was a small, most probably legendary animal deadly to lions.

claims.quote: The first written record is from Greco-Roman writers, but it was also known later during the Medieval period, in Medieval bestiaries.

statement.id: Catatan tertulis pertamanya berasal dari penulis Yunani-Romawi, dan kemudian ia juga dikenal dalam bestiari Abad Pertengahan.
statement.en: Its first written record comes from Greco-Roman writers, and it was later known in Medieval bestiaries.

claims.quote: Leontophones are described as fatally poisonous to lions, such that a lion will die if it merely bites a leontophone.

statement.id: Leontophone digambarkan sangat beracun bagi singa: singa akan mati hanya dengan menggigitnya.
statement.en: Leontophones are described as fatally poisonous to lions: a lion dies merely by biting one.

claims.quote: In a proper ritual, the leontophone's flesh is burned and its ashes are sprinkled on a piece of meat, which is placed at a crossroad; if a lion eats even a small amount of the tainted meat, it dies.

statement.id: Dalam ritual yang tepat, daging leontophone dibakar dan abunya ditaburkan pada sepotong daging yang diletakkan di persimpangan jalan; singa yang memakannya sedikit saja akan mati.
statement.en: In the proper ritual its flesh is burned and the ashes sprinkled on meat left at a crossroads; a lion eating even a little of it dies.

claims.quote: However, some sources state that the lion will instead flee from the small creature, only attacking and killing it when left with no option to flee (since attacking the leontophone may cause it to urinate, and the urine of the leontophone is also fatally poisonous to lions).

statement.id: Sebagian sumber menyebut singa justru lari darinya dan hanya menyerang bila terdesak, karena air seni leontophone juga mematikan bagi singa.
statement.en: Some sources say the lion flees instead and attacks only when cornered, since the leontophone's urine is also deadly to lions.

claims.quote: Likewise, due to the danger they pose to lions, lions instinctively hate leontophones. Confronted by a leontophone, they often hunt and kill them, tearing them apart with their claws rather than biting them.

statement.id: Singa membenci leontophone; bila berhadapan, singa sering memburu dan membunuhnya dengan mencabik memakai cakar, bukan menggigit.
statement.en: Lions hate leontophones; confronted with one, they often hunt and kill it, tearing it with their claws rather than biting.

claims.quote: Though no sources give a definite depiction of the leontophone's appearance, some sources speculate that the creature looks like a small boar or a small bear, while others speculate that it is serpentine

statement.id: Tidak ada sumber yang memberi gambaran pasti tentang wujudnya; sebagian menduga mirip babi hutan kecil atau beruang kecil, yang lain menduga mirip ular.
statement.en: No source gives a definite description of its appearance; some guess a small boar or small bear, others that it is serpentine.

claims.quote: Leeuwen haten leontophonen. Ze jagen erop en doden hen, eerder door ze te verscheuren met hun klauwen, dan ze te bijten.

statement.id: Artikel bahasa Belanda juga menyebut singa membenci leontophone dan memburunya, mencabiknya dengan cakar alih-alih menggigit.
statement.en: The Dutch article also says lions hate leontophones and hunt them, tearing them with their claws rather than biting.

short_description.id: Maero atau Mohoao adalah kaum gaib bertubuh liar dari New Zealand yang mendiami pegunungan dan hutan lebat dalam tradisi Māori.
short_description.en: The Maero or Mohoao are supernatural beings from New Zealand inhabiting mountains and forests in Māori tradition.

long_description.id: Dalam tradisi Māori di New Zealand, Maero atau Mohoao digambarkan sebagai entitas iwi-atua liar yang mendiami hutan dan pegunungan, terutama di South Island serta Tararua Range. Makhluk bertubuh besar ini tertutup rambut hitam lebat dan bersenjatakan gada batu, serta memiliki jari-jari kurus berkuku tajam.
long_description.en: In Māori tradition of New Zealand, the Maero or Mohoao are supernatural iwi-atua inhabiting forests and mountains, especially across the South Island and Tararua Range. These beings are covered in dark body hair and armed with stone clubs, possessing long bony fingers with sharp nails.

long_description.id: Mereka memendam amarah terhadap orang Māori yang datang dari Hawaiki karena merasa terusir dari tanah aslinya. Dalam cerita rakyat setempat, seorang manusia bernama Tukoio pernah memotong tubuh maero, namun makhluk gaib tersebut mampu menyatukan kembali bagian tubuhnya dan kembali menghilang ke pedalaman hutan.
long_description.en: They harbor anger towards Māori newcomers from Hawaiki who displaced them from their original homes. In traditional lore, a mortal named Tukoio once dismembered a maero, yet the creature reassembled its body and retreated back into the woods.

long_description.id: Catatan tertulis lama juga menyebut Maero. Taylor menulis bahwa Maero, manusia liar hutan, dikatakan masih ada di pegunungan dan bahwa kepulan asap di sana lazim dianggap perbuatan mereka, tetapi ia memandangnya sebagai bukti keberadaan mereka di masa lalu. Kamus Tregear mendefinisikan maero sebagai ogre atau manusia liar hutan.
long_description.en: Older written records also mention the Maero. Taylor wrote that the Maero, wild men of the woods, are said even yet to exist on mountains and that a curl of smoke there is commonly attributed to them, but he regarded this as evidence of their past rather than present existence. Tregear's dictionary defines maero as an ogre or a wild man of the woods.

who.id: Kaum gaib berambut lebat penghuni rimba bersenjatakan gada batu.
who.en: Hairy supernatural forest beings armed with stone clubs.

origin.id: Tradisi lisan masyarakat Māori di wilayah New Zealand.
origin.en: Oral traditions of the Māori in New Zealand.

role.id: Penghuni liar pegunungan terpencil yang berseteru dengan manusia pendatang.
role.en: Wild alpine dwellers holding hostility against mortal settlers.

famous_for.id: Kemampuannya menyatukan kembali anggota tubuhnya yang terpotong dalam legenda Tukoio.
famous_for.en: Reassembling severed body parts after being struck down in the tale of Tukoio.

did_you_know.id: Dalam kisah tradisi lisan, kepala Maero yang terpenggal masih dapat berbicara dan makhluk itu dapat menyatukan kembali tubuhnya.
did_you_know.en: In traditional lore, a severed Maero head remained alive and called for aid until the creature put itself back together.

learning_questions.id: Mengapa tradisi Māori melukiskan Maero sebagai penghuni pegunungan yang menyimpan amarah terhadap pendatang dari Hawaiki?
learning_questions.en: Why does Māori tradition portray the Maero as alpine dwellers harboring resentment towards migrants from Hawaiki?

sources.title: Te Ika a Maui; or, New Zealand and its inhabitants (second edition)
sources.author: Richard Taylor

claims.quote: In Māori tradition, the Maero (or Mohoao) are an iwi-atua or supernatural people from New Zealand.

statement.id: Dalam tradisi Māori, Maero (atau Mohoao) adalah iwi-atua atau kaum gaib dari New Zealand.
statement.en: In Māori tradition, the Maero (or Mohoao) are an iwi-atua or supernatural people from New Zealand.

claims.quote: They are sometimes described as giants or wild men of the woods, and inhabit mountains and forest, particularly in the South Island and Tararua Range.

statement.id: Mereka digambarkan sebagai raksasa atau manusia liar hutan yang mendiami pegunungan dan hutan di South Island serta Tararua Range.
statement.en: They are described as giants or wild men inhabiting mountains and forests in the South Island and Tararua Range.

claims.quote: Maero are characterised as wild, malevolent and often violent, carrying stone clubs as weapons.

statement.id: Maero memiliki sifat liar, jahat, dan membawa gada batu sebagai senjata.
statement.en: Maero are characterised as wild, malevolent and violent, carrying stone clubs as weapons.

claims.quote: They are covered in dark body hair and have long, bony fingers with sharp fingernails. They kill and eat humans and other animals.

statement.id: Tubuh mereka tertutup rambut hitam dan memiliki jari kurus panjang dengan kuku tajam.
statement.en: They are covered in dark body hair and have long bony fingers with sharp fingernails.

claims.quote: The Maero are said to harbour anger towards the Māori, who arrived from Hawaiki, and are thought to have displaced them and ruined the tapu (sacredness) of their homes, forcing them to dwell in inhospitable alpine regions.

statement.id: Maero menyimpan amarah terhadap suku Māori yang tiba dari Hawaiki karena telah menggusur mereka.
statement.en: The Maero harbor anger towards the Māori from Hawaiki for displacing them.

claims.quote: Tukoio, a mortal man, once found a maero, a mohoao (wild man), and attacked it, cutting off its arms, legs and head.

statement.id: Tukoio pernah menyerang seekor maero dan memotong lengan, kaki, serta kepalanya.
statement.en: Tukoio attacked a maero, cutting off its arms, legs and head.

claims.quote: He brought the head back, but it was still alive and called for help.

statement.id: Kepala maero yang dibawa ternyata masih hidup dan berseru meminta pertolongan.
statement.en: The head brought back was still alive and called for help.

claims.quote: Tukoio did not want to fight a whole clan of maero, so he dropped it and came back later with reinforcements, only to find the maero had put itself back together and returned to the forest.

statement.id: Maero tersebut ternyata mampu menyatukan kembali tubuhnya dan kembali ke hutan.
statement.en: The maero put itself back together and returned to the forest.

claims.quote: as the Maero and Mohocto, or wild man of the woods ; they are said even yet to exist on the Tarama mountains ; if a cnrl of smoke should be seen upon them, it is commonly attributed to the Maero. This, however, is to be regarded as an evidence of their past, rather than present existence.

statement.en: Taylor records that the Maero, wild men of the woods, are said even yet to exist on mountains; a curl of smoke seen there is commonly attributed to the Maero, which he regards as evidence of their past rather than present existence.

claims.quote: MAERO (myth.), an ogre; a wild man of the woods.

statement.id: Kamus Tregear mendefinisikan maero (istilah mitologi) sebagai ogre atau manusia liar hutan.
statement.en: Tregear's dictionary defines maero (mythological) as an ogre or a wild man of the woods.

text.id: Asal-usulnya ditelusuri ke perjumpaan Eropa-Afrika Barat pada abad ke-15; ikonografinya berubah pada pertengahan abad ke-19
text.en: Origins traced to European-West African encounters in the 15th century; iconography changed in the mid-19th century

short_description.id: Mami Wata adalah roh air, putri duyung, dan dewi dalam cerita rakyat berbagai wilayah Afrika, yang dikaitkan dengan kekayaan, kesuburan, dan kecantikan, serta dipuja hingga diaspora Atlantik.
short_description.en: Mami Wata is a water spirit, mermaid and goddess in the folklore of many parts of Africa, tied to wealth, fertility and beauty and honoured as far as the Atlantic diaspora.

long_description.id: Mami Wata, juga disebut Mammy Water, adalah putri duyung, roh air, atau dewi dalam cerita rakyat Afrika Barat, Tengah, Timur, dan Selatan. Namanya berasal dari kata Inggris mother dan water dalam bahasa-bahasa kreol Afrika seperti Krio dan Naijá. Ia dipandang sebagai dewi kekayaan, kesuburan, penyembuhan, kebijaksanaan, dan kecantikan.
long_description.en: Mami Wata, also called Mammy Water, appears as a mermaid, water spirit or goddess in the folklore of Western, Central, Eastern and Southern Africa. Her name comes from the English words mother and water as used in African creoles such as Krio and Naijá. She is seen as a goddess of riches, fertility, healing, wisdom and beauty.

long_description.id: Ia sering digambarkan sebagai perempuan berkulit terang dengan rambut panjang, yang menyukai benda-benda asing persembahan pemujanya. Ia dapat mengendalikan samudra dan sungai serta berubah wujud untuk memikat manusia. Kepercayaan di Liberia menyebut ia tinggal di istana bawah air dan kadang naik ke pantai untuk menyisir rambutnya dengan sisir emas; cermin menjadi lambangnya di tempat-tempat suci.
long_description.en: She is usually pictured as a light-skinned woman with long hair who delights in foreign objects her devotees offer. She commands seas and rivers and changes form to charm people. Liberian belief places her in an underwater mansion from which she now and then comes ashore to comb her hair with a golden comb, and mirrors serve as her emblem in shrines.

long_description.id: Wataknya ambivalen seperti air: ia bisa menyembuhkan dan memberi hidup, tetapi juga merusak. Ia dapat menganugerahkan kekayaan, penglihatan masa depan, atau perjalanan sangat cepat, tetapi lelaki yang tidak setia kepadanya dikatakan kehilangan kekayaan dan jatuh sakit atau gila. Di kalangan Kpelle ia kadang berwujud laki-laki, kadang perempuan, dan beberapa tradisi mengenal pasangan laki-laki bernama Papi Wata.
long_description.en: Her nature is two-sided like water itself, able to heal and give life yet also to destroy. She may bestow riches, foresight or unusually swift travel, but a man who breaks faith with her is said to lose his fortune and fall sick or go mad. Among the Kpelle she is sometimes male and sometimes female, and some traditions know a male counterpart called Papi Wata.

long_description.id: Para sarjana menelusuri asal-usulnya ke perjumpaan orang Eropa dan Afrika Barat pada abad ke-15, ketika gambaran putri duyung Eropa menjadi model awalnya; pada pertengahan abad ke-19 gambar pawang ular Nala Damajanti sangat memengaruhi ikonografinya. Barbara Paxson sebaliknya menempatkan asalnya di Amerika Latin. Di Afrika Tengah dikenal varian Mamba Muntu atau Mami Muntu, yang diidentifikasi sebagai putri duyung, buaya, atau ular.
long_description.en: Scholars link her beginnings to contact between Europeans and West Africans in the 15th century, when European mermaid images served as an early model; in the mid-19th century a picture of the snake charmer Nala Damajanti reshaped her iconography. Barbara Paxson, by contrast, locates her homeland in Latin America. Central Africa knows a variant, Mamba Muntu or Mami Muntu, identified as a mermaid, crocodile or snake.

long_description.id: Mami Wata dipuja di sebagian Afrika dan diaspora Atlantik, misalnya oleh orang Fon dan Ewe serta dalam Voodoo Haiti, tetapi dijadikan setan oleh sebagian komunitas Kristen dan Islam. Sebagian sarjana mengaitkannya dengan roh air di Karibia dan Amerika Selatan seperti Lasirèn, dan sumber kedua mencatat bahwa di Brasil ia diidentikkan dengan Yemanja.
long_description.en: Mami Wata is venerated in parts of Africa and the Atlantic diaspora, for example by the Fon and Ewe and in Haitian Voodoo, but some Christian and Islamic communities have demonized her. Some scholars tie her to water spirits of the Caribbean and South America such as Lasirèn, and the second source notes that in Brazil she was identified with Yemanja.

short_description.id: Mamlambo adalah roh air perempuan dalam mitologi Zulu, biasanya berwujud ular atau perempuan cantik, yang memberi keberuntungan tetapi menuntut korban, kadang berupa nyawa manusia.
short_description.en: Mamlambo is a female water spirit of Zulu mythology, usually appearing as a snake or a beautiful woman, who grants good fortune but demands sacrifice, sometimes a human life.

long_description.id: Dalam mitologi Zulu, Mamlambo adalah roh air perempuan yang biasanya berwujud ular atau perempuan. Ia disebut ibu sungai, ular mitos yang tinggal di bawah air di lubuk sungai dan keluar sebagai perempuan cantik, serta dewi sungai-sungai di Natal yang menampakkan diri kepada orang yang memberinya persembahan.
long_description.en: Zulu mythology knows Mamlambo as a female spirit of the water who most often takes the shape of a snake or a woman. She is called the mother of the river, a mythical serpent dwelling beneath the water in river pools who comes out as a lovely woman, and the goddess of the rivers of Natal who shows herself to those who offer to her.

long_description.id: Mamlambo dikenal pandai berganti wujud: kadang tampak sebagai babun, sigung, atau babi hutan, tetapi bisa pula perempuan cantik, dan ia selalu perempuan. Menurut satu catatan, ia adalah sejenis ular yang membawa keberuntungan bagi pemeliharanya dan dapat diperoleh dari dukun tradisional. Imbalannya berat: ia menuntut korban sebelum memberi kemurahan, berupa kematian salah satu anggota keluarga pemiliknya.
long_description.en: Mamlambo can change shape, showing herself at times as a baboon, a skunk or a wild pig, though she may just as well be a beautiful woman, and she is always female. One account calls her a kind of snake that brings fortune to whoever keeps it and that can be obtained from traditional doctors. The price is heavy: she demands a sacrifice before granting favour, namely the death of someone in the owner's family.

long_description.id: Pada 1997 sejumlah surat kabar melaporkan penampakan monster di Sungai Mzintlava dekat Gunung Ayliff, Afrika Selatan, sehingga mitos ini menarik minat para kriptozoolog. Penduduk menggambarkan makhluk sepanjang sekitar 20 meter berkepala kuda, bertubuh bawah ikan, berkaki pendek, dan berleher ular. Antara Januari dan April 1997 sembilan kematian dikaitkan dengannya; polisi menyebut bagian lunak kepala korban dimakan kepiting, sedangkan penduduk menyalahkan kebiasaan Mamlambo memakan wajah.
long_description.en: In 1997 several newspapers reported a monster in the Mzintlava River near Mount Ayliff, South Africa, which drew cryptozoologists to the myth. Villagers described a creature about 20 meters long with a horse's head, a fish-like lower body, short legs and a snake's neck. Nine deaths between January and April 1997 were blamed on it; police said crabs had eaten the soft parts of the victims' heads, while villagers blamed Mamlambo's habit of eating faces.

cultural_context.id: Felicity Wood menafsirkan mamlambo sebagai sosok yang dikaitkan dengan kemakmuran gaya Barat seperti uang: menggoda dengan kekayaan dan kekuasaan, tetapi dapat mendatangkan kehancuran.
cultural_context.en: Felicity Wood reads the mamlambo as a figure tied to Western forms of prosperity such as money: seductive with wealth and power, yet able to bring ruin.

learning_questions.id: Mengapa kisah makhluk pemberi kekayaan sering disertai tuntutan korban yang berat?
learning_questions.en: Why are tales of wealth-giving beings often paired with demands for heavy sacrifice?

sources.title: Mamlambo, n.

claims.quote: In Zulu mythology: a female water spirit, usually in the form of a snake or a woman requiring sacrifice, sometimes of human life, in return for her favour.

statement.id: Dalam mitologi Zulu, Mamlambo adalah roh air perempuan (female water spirit), biasanya berwujud ular atau perempuan, yang menuntut korban, kadang nyawa manusia, sebagai imbalan kemurahannya.
statement.en: In Zulu mythology Mamlambo is a female water spirit, usually in the form of a snake or a woman, requiring sacrifice, sometimes of human life, in return for her favour.

claims.quote: The Mamlambo demands a sacrifice before she bestows her favours on a man, and this penalty or sacrifice takes the form of someone dying in his family.

statement.id: Mamlambo menuntut korban (sacrifice) sebelum memberi kemurahan kepada seorang pria, berupa kematian salah satu anggota keluarganya.
statement.en: Mamlambo demands a sacrifice before granting her favours to a man, taking the form of someone in his family dying.

claims.quote: it is well known to assume different shapes; at times it appears as a baboon, or a skunk, or a wild pig, but it is just as likely to be a lovely woman. It is always female.

statement.id: Mamlambo dikenal berganti wujud: kadang tampak sebagai babun, sigung, atau babi hutan (baboon, skunk, wild pig), tetapi bisa juga perempuan cantik; ia selalu perempuan.
statement.en: It is known to assume different shapes, appearing at times as a baboon, a skunk or a wild pig, but just as likely as a lovely woman; it is always female.

claims.quote: Mamlambo the mother of the river is a mythical snake that lives under the water in river pools. She escapes from the river as a beautiful woman.

statement.id: Mamlambo, ibu sungai (mother of the river), adalah ular mitos yang tinggal di bawah air di lubuk sungai dan keluar dari sungai sebagai perempuan cantik.
statement.en: Mamlambo, the mother of the river, is a mythical snake living under the water in river pools, who leaves the river as a beautiful woman.

claims.quote: Mamlambo is a kind of snake that brings fortune to anyone who accommodates it.

statement.id: Mamlambo adalah sejenis ular yang membawa keberuntungan (fortune) bagi siapa pun yang memeliharanya.
statement.en: Mamlambo is a kind of snake that brings fortune to anyone who keeps it.

claims.quote: This snake is available from traditional doctors

statement.id: Ular ini bisa diperoleh dari dukun tradisional (traditional doctors).
statement.en: This snake can be obtained from traditional doctors.

claims.quote: she is the goddess of the rivers of Natal and will appear to those who sacrifice to her.

statement.id: Ia adalah dewi sungai-sungai di Natal (goddess of the rivers) dan menampakkan diri kepada orang yang memberinya persembahan.
statement.en: She is the goddess of the rivers of Natal and appears to those who sacrifice to her.

claims.quote: Villagers in the area claimed that the creature was about 20 meters

statement.id: Penduduk desa di daerah itu mengaku makhluk tersebut panjangnya sekitar 20 meter (20 meters).
statement.en: Villagers in the area claimed the creature was about 20 meters long.

claims.quote: During the period between January and April 1997, as many as nine deaths had been attributed to the Mamlambo.

statement.id: Antara Januari dan April 1997, sebanyak sembilan kematian (nine deaths) dikaitkan dengan Mamlambo.
statement.en: Between January and April 1997, as many as nine deaths were attributed to the Mamlambo.

claims.quote: According to police, the victims had been in the water a while and had the soft parts of their heads and neck eaten by crabs

statement.id: Menurut polisi (police), para korban sudah lama berada di air dan bagian lunak kepala serta leher mereka dimakan kepiting (crabs).
statement.en: According to police, the victims had been in the water a while and crabs had eaten the soft parts of their heads and necks.

claims.quote: the mamlambo tends to be associated with Western forms of prosperity, like money

statement.id: Menurut Felicity Wood, mamlambo cenderung dikaitkan dengan bentuk kemakmuran gaya Barat (Western forms of prosperity), seperti uang.
statement.en: According to Felicity Wood, the mamlambo tends to be associated with Western forms of prosperity, such as money.

claims.quote: Like the Mami Wata, she is a dangerous, seductive figure, offering wealth and power but able to bring about terrifying ruin

statement.id: Seperti Mami Wata, ia sosok yang berbahaya dan memikat (dangerous, seductive), menawarkan kekayaan dan kekuasaan tetapi bisa mendatangkan kehancuran mengerikan.
statement.en: Like Mami Wata, she is a dangerous, seductive figure, offering wealth and power but able to bring terrifying ruin.

claims.quote: El mito de Mamlambo se volvió de interés para los cryptozoologos en 1997, cuando algunos periódicos sudafricanos

statement.id: Mitos Mamlambo menarik minat para kriptozoolog (cryptozoologos) pada 1997, ketika sejumlah surat kabar (periódicos) melaporkan penampakannya.
statement.en: The Mamlambo myth drew the interest of cryptozoologists (cryptozoologos) in 1997, when some newspapers (periódicos) reported sightings.

claims.quote: en el Río Mzintlava cerca del Monte Ayliff; Sudáfrica.

statement.id: Penampakan dilaporkan di Sungai Mzintlava dekat Gunung Ayliff (Monte Ayliff), Afrika Selatan (Sudáfrica).
statement.en: The sightings were reported in the Mzintlava River near Mount Ayliff (Monte Ayliff), South Africa (Sudáfrica).

claims.quote: tenía cabeza de caballo, la parte inferior de un pez, piernas cortas, y el cuello de serpiente,

statement.id: Menurut penduduk, monster itu berkepala kuda (caballo), bertubuh bawah ikan (pez), berkaki pendek, dan berleher ular (serpiente).
statement.en: According to villagers the monster had a horse's head (caballo), the lower body of a fish (pez), short legs and a snake's neck (serpiente).

claims.quote: También se reportó que el monstruo había matado a 9 personas.

statement.id: Dilaporkan pula bahwa monster itu telah membunuh 9 orang (9 personas).
statement.en: It was also reported that the monster had killed 9 people (9 personas).

claims.quote: los pobladores, por otro lado, aclamaban que estas mutilaciones habían sido causadas por el hábito de Mamlambo de comer caras

statement.id: Sebaliknya, penduduk (pobladores) menyatakan luka-luka itu disebabkan kebiasaan Mamlambo memakan wajah (comer caras).
statement.en: The villagers (pobladores), on the other hand, claimed these mutilations were caused by Mamlambo's habit of eating faces (comer caras).

summary.id: Polisi: bagian lunak kepala korban dimakan kepiting setelah lama di air.
summary.en: Police: crabs ate the soft parts of the victims' heads after a long time in the water.

summary.id: Penduduk: luka disebabkan kebiasaan Mamlambo memakan wajah.
summary.en: Villagers: the wounds came from Mamlambo's habit of eating faces.

summary.id: Tradisi: ular atau perempuan, dapat berganti wujud.
summary.en: Tradition: a snake or a woman, able to change shape.

summary.id: Laporan 1997: monster berkepala kuda, bertubuh bawah ikan, berleher ular.
summary.en: 1997 reports: a monster with a horse's head, fish body and snake neck.

short_description.id: Māui adalah pahlawan budaya dan tokoh penipu cerdik dalam mitologi Polinesia, yang dikenal lewat perbuatan seperti memancing pulau, mencuri api, dan memperlambat Matahari.
short_description.en: Māui is the great culture hero and trickster of Polynesian mythology, known for exploits such as fishing up islands, stealing fire and slowing the Sun.

long_description.id: Māui adalah pahlawan budaya sekaligus tokoh penipu dalam mitologi Polinesia. Ia sangat jarang disembah; ia lebih dipandang sebagai pahlawan rakyat daripada dewa. Westervelt menyebutnya salah satu demigod Polinesia yang orang tuanya termasuk makhluk gaib, dengan kekuatan supernatural dan mantra.
long_description.en: Māui is the culture hero and trickster of Polynesian mythology. He was very rarely worshipped and is regarded more as a folk hero than a deity. Westervelt calls him one of the Polynesian demi-gods, whose parents belonged to the family of supernatural beings and who had supernatural powers and enchantments.

long_description.id: Kisah petualangan Māui diceritakan di sebagian besar Polinesia dan dapat dilacak sampai ke pulau-pulau di dekat New Guinea. Perbuatan yang umum di kebanyakan tradisi adalah mencuri api dari dunia bawah, memancing pulau dengan kail sakti, dan menangkap Matahari untuk memperpanjang hari. Meski dikatakan sangat nakal, banyak perbuatannya bertujuan memperbaiki hidup sesamanya.
long_description.en: Tales of Māui's adventures are told throughout most of Polynesia and can be traced as far west as islands off New Guinea. Exploits common to most traditions are stealing fire from the underworld, fishing up islands with a magic hook and capturing the Sun to lengthen the days. Though said to be very rascally, many of his deeds improved the lives of others.

long_description.id: Asal-usul Māui berbeda dari satu budaya ke budaya lain, termasuk orang tuanya, status ilahinya, dan bentuk beberapa mitos utama. Menurut Westervelt, ia kadang disebut Maui-Tiki-Tiki atau Maui-po-tiki. Dalam tradisi Hawaii ia dikreditkan dengan menarik gugusan pulau dari dasar samudra, sedangkan kisah Māori menjadikan ikan raksasa tangkapannya Pulau Utara Selandia Baru.
long_description.en: Māui's origins vary from culture to culture, including his parentage, divine status and the form of several major myths. According to Westervelt he is sometimes called Maui-Tiki-Tiki or Maui-po-tiki. In Hawaiian tradition he is credited with pulling island groups up from the ocean depths, while the Māori account makes the giant fish he caught the North Island of New Zealand.

long_description.id: Dalam salah satu versi, tipu daya terakhir Māui berujung pada kematiannya dan melibatkan Hine-nui-te-pō, dewi kematian dan dunia bawah.
long_description.en: In one version his final trick ended in his death and brought him into contact with Hine-nui-te-pō, goddess of death and the underworld.

cultural_context.id: Meski dikenal nakal, banyak perbuatan Māui bertujuan memperbaiki kehidupan sesama manusia.
cultural_context.en: Although known as rascally, many of Māui's deeds were to better the lives of his fellow people.

who.id: Pahlawan budaya dan tokoh penipu dalam mitologi Polinesia.
who.en: A culture hero and trickster of Polynesian mythology.

origin.id: Tradisi Polinesia; kisahnya diceritakan di sebagian besar Polinesia dan dapat dilacak sampai pulau-pulau di dekat New Guinea.
origin.en: Polynesian tradition; his tales are told across most of Polynesia and can be traced as far as islands off New Guinea.

role.id: Menurut Westervelt, ia adalah demigod yang memakai mantra dan kekuatan supernatural; dalam banyak kisah perbuatannya bermanfaat bagi manusia.
role.en: According to Westervelt, a demi-god who used enchantments and supernatural powers; in many tales his deeds benefit people.

famous_for.id: Dikenal karena memancing pulau, mencuri api, dan menangkap Matahari untuk memperpanjang hari.
famous_for.en: Known for fishing up islands, stealing fire and capturing the Sun to lengthen the days.

did_you_know.id: Westervelt mencatat bahwa orang Samoa menceritakan kisah menjerat matahari tanpa menyebut nama Maui; mereka mengatakan jerat itu dilemparkan oleh anak matahari sendiri.
did_you_know.en: Westervelt records that the Samoans tell the story of snaring the sun without mentioning Maui; they say the snare was cast by a child of the sun itself.

description.id: Menurut Westervelt, Maui memiliki kekuatan supernatural dan dianggap memakai segala macam mantra; dalam salah satu versi ia memberi kekuatan pada tali pancingnya dengan karakia.
description.en: According to Westervelt, Maui had supernatural powers and was supposed to use all manner of enchantments; in one version he gave his fishing line strength with a karakia.

description.id: Dalam kisah Hawaii, Māui dikreditkan menarik berbagai gugusan pulau dari dasar samudra dengan kail ajaib.
description.en: In the Hawaiian account, Māui is credited with pulling various island groups up from the ocean depths with a magic hook.

description.id: Dalam salah satu versi, ikan raksasa yang ditarik Māui menjadi Pulau Utara Selandia Baru, Te Ika-a-Māui.
description.en: In one version, the giant fish Māui pulled up became the North Island of New Zealand, Te Ika-a-Māui.

description.id: Orang Samoa menceritakan kisah yang sama tanpa menyebut nama Maui; jerat itu dilemparkan oleh anak matahari sendiri.
description.en: The Samoans tell the same story without Maui's name; the snare was cast by a child of the sun itself.

role.id: Memancing pulau dengan kail ajaib.
role.en: Fishes up islands with a magic hook.

summary.id: Dalam salah satu versi, Māui menganyam tali pancing, memberinya kekuatan dengan karakia, dan memasang kail ajaib dari tulang rahang pemberian neneknya; ikan raksasa yang ia tarik menjadi Pulau Utara. Dalam kisah Hawaii, ia menarik berbagai gugusan pulau dari dasar samudra.
summary.en: In one version Māui wove a fishing line, strengthened it with a karakia and attached a magic hook made from the jawbone his grandmother gave him; the giant fish he pulled up became the North Island. In the Hawaiian account he pulled various island groups up from the ocean depths.

role.id: Mencari api dari Mahuika.
role.en: Seeks fire from Mahuika.

summary.id: Māui, cucu Mahuika, pergi mencari Mahuika di gua dalam gunung yang menyala. Mahuika memberinya kuku jari yang menyala, tetapi Māui memadamkannya satu demi satu sampai Mahuika marah dan mengirim api mengejarnya. Māui kemudian membawa pulang ranting kering dan menunjukkan cara menggosokkannya untuk membuat api.
summary.en: Māui, a grandson of Mahuika, went to find Mahuika in a cave in a burning mountain. She gave him burning fingernails, but he put them out one by one until she became angry and sent fire to pursue him. Māui then brought dry sticks home and showed how to rub them together to make fire.

role.id: Menjerat dewa matahari.
role.en: Snares the sun-god.

summary.id: Dalam salah satu versi, Tama-nui-te-rā terjerat dan Māui memukulnya dengan tulang rahang sampai ia menyerah dan setuju bergerak pelan melintasi langit.
summary.en: In one version Tama-nui-te-rā, trapped in the noose, was beaten with the jawbone by Māui until he yielded and promised to cross the sky slowly.

role.id: Tipu daya terakhirnya melibatkan Hine-nui-te-pō.
role.en: His last trick involves Hine-nui-te-pō.

summary.id: Tipu daya terakhir Māui berujung pada kematiannya dan melibatkan Hine-nui-te-pō, dewi kematian dan dunia bawah.
summary.en: His final trick ended in his death and brought him into contact with Hine-nui-te-pō, goddess of death and the underworld.

description.id: Menurut Westervelt, Haleakala ("Rumah Matahari") adalah gunung tempat Maui menjerat matahari.
description.en: According to Westervelt, Haleakala ("the House of the Sun") is the mountain from which Maui snared the sun.

note.id: Dalam salah satu versi, Māui adalah cucu Mahuika, dewi api.
note.en: In one version Māui is a grandson of Mahuika, the fire goddess.

note.id: Māui menjerat dewa matahari Tama-nui-te-rā dan memukulnya sampai ia setuju bergerak lebih lambat.
note.en: Māui snares the sun-god Tama-nui-te-rā and strikes him until he agrees to move more slowly.

note.id: Tipu daya terakhir Māui melibatkan Hine-nui-te-pō dan berujung pada kematiannya.
note.en: Māui's last trick involved Hine-nui-te-pō and led to his death.

learning_questions.id: Mengapa status ilahi Māui bisa berbeda antarbudaya Polinesia?
learning_questions.en: Why might Māui's divine status differ between Polynesian cultures?

claims.quote: Māui or Maui is the great culture hero and trickster in Polynesian mythology.

statement.id: Māui adalah pahlawan budaya dan penipu ulung dalam mitologi Polinesia.
statement.en: Māui is the great culture hero and trickster in Polynesian mythology.

claims.quote: Tales of Māui's exploits and adventures are told throughout most of Polynesia; they can be traced back as far west as islands off New Guinea.

statement.id: Kisah petualangan Māui diceritakan di seantero Polinesia hingga pulau-pulau di lepas New Guinea.
statement.en: Tales of Māui's exploits are told across Polynesia and as far west as islands off New Guinea.

claims.quote: Very rarely was Māui actually worshipped, being less of a deity (demigod) and more of a folk hero.

statement.id: Māui sangat jarang disembah, lebih berposisi sebagai pahlawan rakyat daripada dewa.
statement.en: Māui was rarely worshipped, being viewed as a folk hero rather than a deity.

claims.quote: Some exploits common to most Polynesian traditions are stealing fire for humans from the underworld, fishing up islands with his magical hook, and capturing the Sun to lengthen the days.

statement.id: Beberapa perbuatan yang umum dalam kebanyakan tradisi Polinesia adalah mencuri api untuk manusia dari dunia bawah, memancing pulau-pulau dengan kail saktinya, dan menangkap Matahari untuk memperpanjang hari.
statement.en: Some exploits common to most Polynesian traditions are stealing fire for humans from the underworld, fishing up islands with his magical hook, and capturing the Sun to lengthen the days.

claims.quote: Although Māui was said to be very rascally or "kolohe", many of his deeds were to better the lives of his fellow people.

statement.id: Meskipun Māui dikatakan sangat nakal atau "kolohe", banyak perbuatannya bertujuan memperbaiki kehidupan sesama manusia.
statement.en: Although Māui was said to be very rascally, or "kolohe", many of his deeds were to better the lives of his fellow people.

claims.quote: His origins vary from culture to culture, with variation in his parentage, divine status, and the specific form of several major myths, but many of his main exploits remain relatively similar.

statement.id: Asal-usul Māui berbeda dari satu budaya ke budaya lain, termasuk orang tuanya, status ilahinya, dan bentuk beberapa mitos utama, tetapi banyak perbuatan pokoknya relatif serupa.
statement.en: Māui's origins vary from culture to culture, including his parentage, divine status and the specific form of several major myths, but many of his main exploits remain relatively similar.

claims.quote: The noted greenstone god of the Maoris of New Zealand, Potiki, may well be considered a representation of Maui-Tiki-Tiki, who was sometimes called Maui-po-tiki.

statement.id: Menurut Westervelt, dewa batu hijau (greenstone) Māori yang terkenal, Potiki, dapat dianggap sebagai perwujudan Maui-Tiki-Tiki, yang kadang disebut Maui-po-tiki.
statement.en: According to Westervelt, the noted greenstone god of the Maoris, Potiki, may well be considered a representation of Maui-Tiki-Tiki, who was sometimes called Maui-po-tiki.

claims.quote: Māui's last trick led to his death and involved Hine-nui-te-pō, the goddess of death and the underworld.
claims.locator: Māori mythology — The death of Māui

statement.id: Tipu daya terakhir Māui berujung pada kematiannya dan melibatkan Hine-nui-te-pō, dewi kematian dan dunia bawah.
statement.en: Māui's last trick led to his death and involved Hine-nui-te-pō, the goddess of death and the underworld.

claims.quote: Māui also is credited with the creation of the Hawaiian islands, when he went on a fishing expedition with his friends, and, using a magic fish hook, pulled up various island groups from the oceanic depths.

statement.id: Māui juga dipercaya menciptakan kepulauan Hawaii: dalam ekspedisi memancing bersama teman-temannya ia memakai kail ajaib untuk menarik berbagai gugusan pulau dari dasar samudra.
statement.en: Māui is also credited with creating the Hawaiian islands: on a fishing expedition with his friends he used a magic fish hook to pull up various island groups from the ocean depths.

claims.quote: One night, he wove for himself a flax fishing line and enchanted it with a karakia to give it strength; to this he attached the magic fish-hook made from the jawbone that his grandmother Murirangawhenua had given him.
claims.locator: Māori mythology — Islands of New Zealand

statement.id: Pada suatu malam ia menganyam tali pancing dari rami dan memberinya kekuatan dengan karakia (mantra); padanya ia mengikatkan kail ajaib dari tulang rahang yang diberikan neneknya, Murirangawhenua.
statement.en: One night he wove a flax fishing line and enchanted it with a karakia (incantation) to give it strength; to it he attached the magic fish-hook made from the jawbone his grandmother Murirangawhenua had given him.

claims.quote: He pulled up a giant fish which would become the North Island of New Zealand, known as Te Ika-a-Māui; the valleys and mountains of the island were made by his brothers chopping up the fish for themselves.
claims.locator: Māori mythology — Islands of New Zealand

statement.id: Ia menarik seekor ikan raksasa yang kelak menjadi Pulau Utara Selandia Baru, yang dikenal sebagai Te Ika-a-Māui; lembah dan gunung di pulau itu terbentuk ketika saudara-saudaranya mencincang ikan itu untuk diri mereka sendiri.
statement.en: He pulled up a giant fish that would become the North Island of New Zealand, known as Te Ika-a-Māui; the island's valleys and mountains were made by his brothers chopping up the fish for themselves.

claims.quote: So Māui (a grandson of Mahuika) offered to go and find her. Mahuika lived in a cave in a burning mountain at the end of the earth. She gave Māui one of her burning fingernails to relight the fires, but Māui extinguished fingernail after fingernail until Mahuika became angry and sent fire to pursue Māui
claims.locator: Māori mythology — Māui brings fire to the world

statement.id: Māui (cucu Mahuika) menawarkan diri mencari Mahuika, yang tinggal di gua dalam gunung yang menyala di ujung bumi. Mahuika memberinya satu kuku jarinya yang menyala untuk menyalakan kembali api, tetapi Māui memadamkan kuku demi kuku sampai Mahuika marah dan mengirim api untuk mengejarnya.
statement.en: Māui (a grandson of Mahuika) offered to find her; Mahuika lived in a cave in a burning mountain at the end of the earth. She gave him one of her burning fingernails to relight the fires, but Māui put out fingernail after fingernail until Mahuika became angry and sent fire to pursue him.

claims.quote: Māui brought back dry sticks of these trees to his village and showed his people how to rub the sticks together and make fire.
claims.locator: Māori mythology — Māui brings fire to the world

statement.id: Māui membawa pulang ranting kering dari pohon-pohon itu ke desanya dan menunjukkan kepada rakyatnya cara menggosokkan ranting untuk membuat api.
statement.en: Māui brought dry sticks of these trees back to his village and showed his people how to rub the sticks together to make fire.

claims.quote: Tama-nui-te-rā was caught in the noose and Māui struck him with the jawbone until he surrendered and agreed to travel slowly across the sky.
claims.locator: Māori mythology — Māui slows the sun

statement.id: Tama-nui-te-rā terjerat dalam jerat itu dan Māui memukulnya dengan tulang rahang sampai ia menyerah dan setuju bergerak pelan melintasi langit.
statement.en: Tama-nui-te-rā was caught in the noose and Māui struck him with the jawbone until he surrendered and agreed to travel slowly across the sky.

claims.quote: Maui was one of the Polynesian demi-gods. His parents belonged to the family of supernatural beings. He himself was possessed of supernatural powers and was supposed to make use of all manner of enchantments.

statement.id: Menurut Westervelt, Maui adalah salah satu demigod Polinesia; orang tuanya termasuk keluarga makhluk gaib, dan ia sendiri memiliki kekuatan supernatural serta dianggap memakai segala macam mantra.
statement.en: According to Westervelt, Maui was one of the Polynesian demi-gods; his parents belonged to the family of supernatural beings, and he himself possessed supernatural powers and was supposed to use all manner of enchantments.

claims.quote: The legends of Hawaii, Tonga, Tahiti, New Zealand and the Hervey group make this youngest Maui "the discoverer of fire" or "the ensnarer of the sun" or "the fisherman who pulls up islands" or "the man endowed with magic," or "Maui with spirit power."

statement.id: Menurut Westervelt, legenda dari Hawaii, Tonga, Tahiti, Selandia Baru, dan kelompok Hervey menjadikan Maui yang paling muda ini "penemu api", "penjerat matahari", "nelayan yang menarik pulau", "orang yang dianugerahi sihir", atau "Maui dengan kekuatan roh".
statement.en: According to Westervelt, the legends of Hawaii, Tonga, Tahiti, New Zealand and the Hervey group make this youngest Maui "the discoverer of fire", "the ensnarer of the sun", "the fisherman who pulls up islands", "the man endowed with magic" or "Maui with spirit power".

claims.quote: The New Zealanders claim Maui as an ancestor of their most ancient tribes and sometimes class him among the most ancient of their gods, calling him "creator of land" and "creator of man."

statement.id: Menurut Westervelt, orang Selandia Baru menganggap Maui sebagai leluhur suku-suku tertua mereka dan kadang menggolongkannya di antara dewa-dewa tertua mereka, menyebutnya "pencipta daratan" dan "pencipta manusia".
statement.en: According to Westervelt, the New Zealanders claim Maui as an ancestor of their most ancient tribes and sometimes class him among their most ancient gods, calling him "creator of land" and "creator of man".

claims.quote: The Samoans tell the same story without mentioning the name of Maui. They say that the snare was cast by a child of the sun itself.
claims.locator: Chapter IV, Maui Snaring the Sun

statement.id: Menurut Westervelt, orang Samoa menceritakan kisah yang sama tanpa menyebut nama Maui; mereka mengatakan jerat itu dilemparkan oleh anak matahari sendiri.
statement.en: According to Westervelt, the Samoans tell the same story without mentioning Maui's name; they say the snare was cast by a child of the sun itself.

claims.quote: Haleakala (the House of the Sun), the mountain from which Maui the demi-god snared the sun, looks down ten thousand feet upon the Kauiki headland.

statement.id: Menurut Westervelt, Haleakala ("Rumah Matahari") adalah gunung tempat Maui sang demigod menjerat matahari.
statement.en: According to Westervelt, Haleakala ("the House of the Sun") is the mountain from which Maui the demi-god snared the sun.

short_description.id: Mbielu-mbielu-mbielu adalah kriptid air dari wilayah Likouala yang konon memiliki 'papan' hijau di punggungnya, sehingga sebagian kriptozoolog menganggapnya stegosaurus yang masih hidup.
short_description.en: Mbielu-mbielu-mbielu is a water cryptid of the Likouala area said to bear green 'planks' on its back, which has led some cryptozoologists to see it as a surviving stegosaur.

long_description.id: Mbielu-mbielu-mbielu, yang namanya berarti 'hewan dengan papan yang tumbuh dari punggungnya', adalah kriptid yang konon terlihat di Sungai Likouala. Sumber berbeda soal negaranya: artikel pertama menyebut Republik Demokratik Kongo, sedangkan artikel kedua menyebut Republik Kongo. Informasi tentangnya hampir seluruhnya berasal dari sedikit laporan warga yang dicatat Roy Mackal.
long_description.en: Reported from the Likouala River, the cryptid Mbielu-mbielu-mbielu takes its name from a phrase meaning 'the animal with planks growing out of its back'. The sources disagree on the country: the first article names the Democratic Republic of the Congo, while the second names the Republic of the Congo. Nearly all that is known comes from a handful of local reports recorded by Roy Mackal.

long_description.id: Para kriptozoolog tidak pernah sepakat tentang wujudnya. Ia biasanya disebut terbenam di sungai dan danau dengan hanya punggungnya yang tampak, ditumbuhi ganggang hijau, dan paling aktif pada sore hari. Karena 'papan' di punggungnya, sebagian menganggapnya stegosaurid; ada pula yang membandingkannya dengan nguma-monene atau melukiskannya mirip buaya raksasa berpunggung bergerigi.
long_description.en: Cryptozoologists have never settled on what it looks like. It is usually said to lie submerged in rivers and lakes with only its algae-covered back above water, and to be most active in the afternoon. Because of the 'planks' on its back some think of it as a stegosaurid; others compare it to the nguma-monene or describe it as a giant crocodile with a serrated back.

long_description.id: Roy Mackal berpendapat makhluk ini biawak raksasa, sedangkan Dale A. Drinnon menduga buaya raksasa berpunggung bergerigi. Pada 1980, Odette Gesonget dari Bouanila memilih gambar Stegosaurus dari buku Mackal untuk menggambarkannya, tetapi mengaku tidak pernah melihatnya sendiri dan hanya mengandalkan cerita orang tua serta kakek-neneknya.
long_description.en: Roy Mackal believed it was a giant monitor lizard, while Dale A. Drinnon suggested a giant crocodilian with a serrated back. In 1980 Odette Gesonget of Bouanila chose a Stegosaurus picture from Mackal's books to describe it, but admitted she had never seen it and relied only on what her parents and grandparents had told her.
