text.en: A document from 1816 and reports from 1847; last recorded sighting in 2005

short_description.id: Memphré adalah monster danau dalam cerita rakyat Kanada yang konon hidup di Danau Memphremagog, antara Vermont dan Quebec. Tercatat lebih dari 225 penampakan dalam dua abad terakhir.
short_description.en: Memphré is a lake monster of Canadian folklore said to live in Lake Memphremagog, between Vermont and Quebec. More than 225 sightings have been recorded over the past two centuries.

long_description.id: Memphré adalah monster yang konon hidup di Danau Memphremagog, danau glasial air tawar antara Newport, Vermont, dan Magog, Quebec. Sebelum orang Eropa tiba, kawasan itu dihuni bangsa Abenaki, yang memberi danau itu namanya. Salah satu legenda menyebut makhluk itu mendiami kedalaman di bawah Gunung Owl's Head. Memphré sering digambarkan mirip Loch Ness Monster.
long_description.en: Memphré is a monster said to live in Lake Memphremagog, a freshwater glacial lake between Newport, Vermont, and Magog, Quebec. Before Europeans arrived, the area was occupied by the Abenakis, who gave the lake its name. One legend says the creature inhabits the depths beneath Owl's Head Mountain. Memphré is often described much like the Loch Ness Monster.

long_description.id: Menurut dokumen tahun 1816, penduduk pribumi mengatakan kepada para pemukim pertama dari New England bahwa mereka takut mandi atau berenang di danau karena dihuni ular laut. Dalam dua abad terakhir tercatat lebih dari 225 penampakan, dan salah satu laporan paling awal berasal dari 1847. Pada masa lalu makhluk ini dikenal sebagai "Sea Serpent", "the Anaconda", atau "Lake Memphremagog Monster", dan belakangan dijuluki "Memphré".
long_description.en: According to a document from 1816, the Indigenous people told the first settlers from New England that they feared bathing or swimming in the lake because it was inhabited by a sea serpent. More than 225 sightings have been recorded over the past two centuries, one of the earliest reports dating to 1847. In the past the creature was known as the "Sea Serpent", "the Anaconda" or the "Lake Memphremagog Monster", and in recent years it has been dubbed "Memphré".

long_description.id: Komunitas ilmiah menanggapi keberadaan Memphré dan sebagian besar monster danau lain secara skeptis, tetapi laporan penampakan tetap ada, yang terakhir pada 2005. Pada Agustus 2011, gambar Memphré tampil pada koin seperempat dolar Kanada berwarna.
long_description.en: The scientific community treats the existence of Memphré and most other lake monsters skeptically, yet reports of sightings persist, the last in 2005. In August 2011 a coloured Canadian quarter carried an artist's impression of Memphré.

who.id: Monster danau dalam cerita rakyat Kanada.
who.en: A lake monster of Canadian folklore.

origin.id: Berasal dari legenda di sekitar Danau Memphremagog, kawasan bangsa Abenaki sebelum kedatangan orang Eropa.
origin.en: From legends around Lake Memphremagog, an area occupied by the Abenakis before Europeans arrived.

role.id: Konon menghuni danau itu dan membuat penduduk pribumi takut berenang di dalamnya.
role.en: Said to inhabit the lake and to have made Indigenous people afraid to swim in it.

famous_for.en: Known for more than 225 recorded sightings and often compared with the Loch Ness Monster.

description.en: Freshwater glacial lake between Newport, Vermont, and Magog, Quebec, where Memphré is said to live.

description.id: Menurut satu legenda, makhluk itu mendiami kedalaman di bawah gunung ini.
description.en: According to one legend the creature inhabits the depths beneath this mountain.

description.en: A document from 1816 says Indigenous people told the first settlers they feared swimming in the lake because a sea serpent lived in it.

description.en: One of the earliest reports: The Stanstead Journal proclaimed that a strange animal, something of a sea serpent, exists in the lake.

sources.author: Matthew Farfan

claims.quote: In Canadian folklore, Memphré is a lake monster said to live in Lake Memphremagog, a fresh water glacial lake located between Newport, Vermont, United States and Magog, Quebec, Canada.

statement.id: Dalam cerita rakyat Kanada, Memphré adalah monster danau yang konon hidup di Danau Memphremagog, antara Newport, Vermont, dan Magog, Quebec.
statement.en: In Canadian folklore, Memphré is a lake monster said to live in Lake Memphremagog between Newport, Vermont, and Magog, Quebec.

claims.quote: Memphré is often described much like the Loch Ness Monster.

statement.id: Memphré sering digambarkan mirip Loch Ness Monster.
statement.en: Memphré is often described much like the Loch Ness Monster.

claims.quote: In August 2011, an artistic impression of Memphré was featured on a coloured Canadian quarter.

statement.id: Pada Agustus 2011, gambar Memphré tampil pada koin seperempat dolar Kanada berwarna.
statement.en: In August 2011 an image of Memphré appeared on a coloured Canadian quarter.

claims.quote: While the existence of Memphré and most other lake monsters is treated skeptically by the scientific community, reports of sightings persist, with the last in 2005.

statement.id: Keberadaan Memphré dan sebagian besar monster danau lain ditanggapi skeptis oleh komunitas ilmiah, tetapi laporan penampakan tetap ada, yang terakhir pada 2005.
statement.en: The existence of Memphré and most other lake monsters is treated skeptically by the scientific community, yet reports of sightings persist, the last in 2005.

claims.quote: Lake Memphremagog is located partly in Canada and partly in the United States. Europeans have been living around the lake for only the last two centuries; before their arrival, the area was occupied by the Abenakis, the indigenous people who gave the lake its name, which roughly translates as "beautiful waters."

statement.id: Danau Memphremagog terletak sebagian di Kanada dan sebagian di Amerika Serikat. Sebelum orang Eropa tiba, kawasan itu dihuni bangsa Abenaki, penduduk asli yang memberi danau itu namanya, yang kira-kira berarti "perairan indah".
statement.en: Lake Memphremagog lies partly in Canada and partly in the United States. Before Europeans arrived, the area was occupied by the Abenakis, the indigenous people who gave the lake its name, which roughly translates as "beautiful waters".

claims.quote: One such legend pertains to a creature that is said to inhabit the depths beneath Owl's Head Mountain.

statement.id: Salah satu legenda danau itu menyangkut makhluk yang konon mendiami kedalaman di bawah Gunung Owl's Head.
statement.en: One legend of the lake concerns a creature said to inhabit the depths beneath Owl's Head Mountain.

claims.quote: According to a document from 1816, when the first settlers arrived from New England, the Indigenous people told them that they were afraid to bathe or swim in the lake because it was inhabited by a sea serpent.

statement.id: Menurut dokumen tahun 1816, ketika para pemukim pertama tiba dari New England, penduduk pribumi mengatakan takut mandi atau berenang di danau itu karena dihuni ular laut.
statement.en: According to a document from 1816, when the first settlers arrived from New England, the Indigenous people told them they were afraid to bathe or swim in the lake because it was inhabited by a sea serpent.

claims.quote: Over the past two centuries, more than 225 sightings of the monster have been recorded. One of the earliest reports dates to 1847 when The Stanstead Journal proclaimed that "a strange animal, something of a sea serpent... exists in Lake Memphremagog."

statement.id: Dalam dua abad terakhir tercatat lebih dari 225 penampakan monster itu; salah satu laporan paling awal berasal dari 1847, ketika The Stanstead Journal menyatakan bahwa "hewan aneh, semacam ular laut... ada di Danau Memphremagog".
statement.en: Over the past two centuries more than 225 sightings have been recorded; one of the earliest reports dates to 1847, when The Stanstead Journal proclaimed that "a strange animal, something of a sea serpent... exists in Lake Memphremagog".

claims.quote: Known in the past by such names as the "Sea Serpent," "the Anaconda," or "the Lake Memphremagog Monster," in recent years, the creature has been affectionately dubbed "Memphré."

statement.id: Pada masa lalu makhluk ini dikenal dengan nama seperti "Sea Serpent", "the Anaconda", atau "Lake Memphremagog Monster"; belakangan ia dijuluki dengan akrab "Memphré".
statement.en: In the past the creature was known by names such as "Sea Serpent", "the Anaconda" or "the Lake Memphremagog Monster"; in recent years it has been affectionately dubbed "Memphré".

summary.id: Komunitas ilmiah menanggapi keberadaannya secara skeptis.
summary.en: The scientific community treats its existence skeptically.

summary.id: Lebih dari 225 penampakan tercatat dalam dua abad terakhir.
summary.en: More than 225 sightings have been recorded over two centuries.

gaps.searched: Tidak ada gambar Commons yang terbukti menggambarkan makhluk ini; artikel Wikipedia-nya tidak memuat ilustrasi makhluk tersebut.

short_description.id: Menehune adalah bangsa mirip kurcaci dalam tradisi Hawaii yang konon tinggal di hutan lebat dan lembah tersembunyi, dan terkenal sebagai pembangun yang cekatan.
short_description.en: The Menehune are a dwarf-like people of Hawaiian tradition said to live in deep forests and hidden valleys, famed as skilled builders.

long_description.id: Menehune adalah ras mitologis berpostur mirip kurcaci dalam tradisi Hawaii yang dikatakan tinggal di hutan lebat dan lembah tersembunyi di Kepulauan Hawaii, jauh dari permukiman manusia. Mereka digambarkan sebagai pengrajin ulung yang membangun kuil (heiau), kolam ikan, jalan, perahu, dan rumah, dan sebagian bangunan yang oleh cerita rakyat Hawaii dikaitkan dengan mereka masih ada. Mereka dikatakan telah tinggal di Hawaiʻi sebelum para pemukim tiba dari Polinesia.
long_description.en: In Hawaiian tradition the Menehune are a legendary people of small, dwarf-like stature, said to dwell in the deep forests and hidden valleys of the islands, away from human settlements. They are portrayed as superb craftspeople who raised temples (heiau), fishponds, roads, canoes and houses, and some structures Hawaiian folklore credits to them still stand. They are reputed to predate the settlers who reached Hawaiʻi from Polynesia many centuries ago.

long_description.id: Menurut legenda, Menehune hanya muncul pada malam hari untuk membangun, dan bila gagal menyelesaikan pekerjaan dalam semalam mereka meninggalkannya. Thrum mencatat bahwa aturan mereka adalah menyelesaikan setiap pekerjaan dalam satu malam, bahwa mereka selalu bersatu dalam setiap pekerjaan, dan bahwa mereka tidak terlihat oleh siapa pun kecuali keturunan atau kerabat mereka, meskipun banyak orang dapat mendengar dengung suara mereka. Menurut kisah, mereka bersedia memenuhi perintah keturunan mereka. Makanan kesukaan mereka adalah pisang, dan mereka juga menyukai ikan.
long_description.en: According to legend, the Menehune appear only at night to build, and leave a work if they cannot finish it within the night. Thrum records that their rule was to complete any work in a single night, that they were always united in their tasks, and that they were invisible to all but their descendants or kin, though many could hear the hum of their voices. In the tales they were willing to do the bidding of their descendants. Their favorite food is banana, and they also like fish.

long_description.id: Kisah-kisah yang dihimpun Thrum mengaitkan Menehune dengan bendungan dan saluran air di Kikiaola, dinding kolam ikan di tikungan Sungai Huleia yang dibiarkan tak selesai, dan perahu yang diangkat dengan tangan. Mereka juga dikreditkan membangun banyak heiau, antara lain dengan berbaris dari Pololu ke Honoipu untuk mengoper batu, dan sebuah heiau di tebing Waikolu dekat Kalaupapa, Molokai.
long_description.en: The tales collected by Thrum link the Menehune with a dam and watercourse at Kikiaola, a fish-pond wall at the bend of the Huleia River that was left unfinished, and a canoe lifted by hand. They are also credited with many heiaus, including by standing in a line from Pololu to Honoipu to pass stones along, and a heiau on the pali of Waikolu near Kalaupapa, Molokai.

long_description.id: Asal Menehune diperdebatkan. Sebagian orang Hawaii yang dicatat Thrum percaya mereka penghuni asli pulau-pulau itu, sedangkan yang lebih terpelajar memandangnya golongan mitos gnome atau kurcaci. Sebagian sarjana awal mengusulkan bahwa Menehune berasal dari "rakyat jelata" (manahune dalam bahasa Tahiti) yang melarikan diri ke pegunungan, sedangkan Katharine Luomala berpendapat legenda itu mitologi pasca-kontak dengan Eropa.
long_description.en: The origin of the Menehune is debated. Some Hawaiians recorded by Thrum believed they were the original inhabitants of the islands, while the more educated regarded them as a mythical class of gnomes or dwarfs. Some early scholars proposed that the Menehune descend from the "commoners" (manahune in Tahitian) who fled to the mountains, while Katharine Luomala argues the legends are a post-European-contact mythology.

who.id: Bangsa mirip kurcaci dalam tradisi Hawaii yang dikenal sebagai pembangun ulung.
who.en: A dwarf-like people of Hawaiian tradition known as superb builders.

origin.id: Tradisi Hawaii; mereka dikatakan tinggal di hutan dan lembah tersembunyi Kepulauan Hawaii.
origin.en: Hawaiian tradition; said to live in the forests and hidden valleys of the Hawaiian Islands.

role.id: Membangun kuil, kolam ikan, jalan, perahu, dan rumah, biasanya dalam satu malam.
role.en: Build temples, fishponds, roads, canoes and houses, usually within a single night.

famous_for.id: Dikenal karena mengerjakan bangunan besar dalam semalam dan tak terlihat kecuali oleh kerabat mereka.
famous_for.en: Known for completing great works overnight and for being unseen except by their kin.

did_you_know.id: Menurut Thrum, ada pepatah Hawaii "He po hookahi, a ao ua pau" ("dalam satu malam, dan saat fajar sudah selesai") yang berasal dari aturan kerja Menehune.
did_you_know.en: Thrum links a Hawaiian proverb, "He po hookahi, a ao ua pau", meaning a single night and done by dawn, to the Menehune's working rule.

description.id: Menurut kisah, Menehune membangun mahakarya pada malam hari dan menyelesaikannya sebelum fajar.
description.en: In the tales the Menehune build masterpieces at night and finish them before dawn.

description.id: Menurut Thrum, mereka tidak terlihat oleh siapa pun kecuali keturunan atau kerabat mereka, meskipun suara mereka dapat didengar.
description.en: According to Thrum they were invisible to everyone but their descendants or kin, although their voices could be heard.

title.id: Bendungan dan saluran air di Kikiaola
title.en: The dam and watercourse at Kikiaola

role.id: Membangun bendungan dan saluran batu dalam semalam.
role.en: Build a dam and stone watercourse in one night.

summary.id: Pada tengah malam para Menehune, masing-masing membawa sebuah batu, menuju Kikiaola, membangun bendungan dan memasang saluran air batu sebelum fajar.
summary.en: At dead of night the Menehunes, each carrying a stone, went to Kikiaola and built a dam and laid a stone watercourse before dawn.

role.id: Membangun dinding kolam ikan hingga fajar.
role.en: Build the walls of a fish-pond until dawn.

summary.id: Menehune diperintah membuat dinding kolam ikan di tikungan Sungai Huleia; saat fajar dinding belum cukup rampung, sehingga dibiarkan tak selesai hingga kini.
summary.en: The Menehunes were ordered to build the walls of a fish-pond at a bend of the Huleia River; by dawn the walls were still too short to meet, so the work was left incomplete to this day.

role.id: Mengangkat perahu dengan tangan pada tengah malam.
role.en: Lift a canoe by hand at dead of night.

summary.id: Menehune memberi tahu Laka bahwa perahu akan dibawa ke halau malam itu; pada tengah malam terdengar dengung suara mereka dan perahu diangkat dengan tangan, tidak diseret.
summary.en: The Menehunes told Laka the canoe would be brought to the halau that night; at dead of night their voices were heard and the canoe was held up by hand, not dragged.

description.id: Lokasi bendungan dan saluran air batu yang dalam kisah dibangun Menehune dalam semalam.
description.en: Site of a dam and stone watercourse that the tales say the Menehunes built in one night.

description.id: Heiau yang dalam tradisi dibangun Menehune dengan batu dari Pololu yang dioper dari tangan ke tangan sampai Honoipu.
description.en: A heiau that tradition says the Menehunes built, with stones from Pololu passed hand to hand as far as Honoipu.

description.id: Tebing dekat Kalaupapa, Molokai, tempat berdiri heiau yang diyakini orang Hawaii dibangun Menehune.
description.en: A cliff near Kalaupapa, Molokai, where stands a heiau Hawaiians believe the Menehunes built.

learning_questions.id: Bagaimana kita menimbang tradisi lisan terhadap hipotesis sarjana ketika menjelaskan asal sebuah makhluk legenda?
learning_questions.en: How should we weigh oral tradition against scholarly hypotheses when explaining the origin of a legendary being?

sources.title: Hawaiian Folk Tales: Stories of the Menehunes (Hawaii the Original Home of the Brownies)
sources.author: Thomas G. Thrum (ed.)

claims.quote: Menehune are a mythological race of dwarf-like people in Hawaiian tradition who are said to live in the deep forests and hidden valleys of the Hawaiian Islands, hidden and far away from human settlements.

statement.id: Menehune adalah ras manusia kerdil mitologis di Hawaii yang hidup di hutan lebat.
statement.en: Menehune are a mythological dwarf-like race in Hawaiian lore living in deep forests.

claims.quote: The Menehune are described as superb craftspeople. They built temples (heiau), fishponds, roads, canoes, and houses.

statement.id: Menehune digambarkan sebagai perajin ulung yang membangun kuil heiau, kolam ikan, dan jalan.
statement.en: Menehune are superb craftspeople credited with building heiau, fishponds, roads, and canoes.

claims.quote: Some of these structures that Hawaiian folklore attributed to the Menehune still exist.

statement.id: Beberapa bangunan yang dikaitkan dengan Menehune masih berdiri hingga kini.
statement.en: Some structures attributed to the Menehune still exist today.

claims.quote: Legend has it that the Menehune appear only during the night hours to build masterpieces, and if they fail to complete their work in the length of the night, they will leave it unoccupied.

statement.id: Menurut legenda, Menehune hanya muncul pada malam hari untuk membangun mahakarya, dan bila gagal menyelesaikan pekerjaan dalam semalam, mereka akan meninggalkannya tanpa dihuni.
statement.en: According to legend, the Menehune appear only at night to build masterpieces, and if they cannot finish a work within the night they leave it unoccupied.

claims.quote: No one but their children and humans connected to them can see the Menehune.

statement.id: Tidak ada yang dapat melihat Menehune kecuali anak-anak mereka dan manusia yang berhubungan dengan mereka.
statement.en: No one but their children and humans connected to them can see the Menehune.

claims.quote: Their favorite food is the maiʻa (banana), and they also like fish.

statement.id: Makanan kesukaan mereka adalah maiʻa (pisang), dan mereka juga menyukai ikan.
statement.en: Their favorite food is the maiʻa (banana), and they also like fish.

claims.quote: They are said to have lived in Hawaiʻi before settlers arrived from Polynesia many centuries ago.

statement.id: Mereka dikatakan telah tinggal di Hawaiʻi sebelum para pemukim tiba dari Polinesia berabad-abad lalu.
statement.en: They are said to have lived in Hawaiʻi before settlers arrived from Polynesia many centuries ago.

claims.quote: Folklorist Katharine Luomala believes that the legends of the Menehune are a post-European contact mythology created by adaptation of the term manahune (which by the time of the colonization of the Hawaiian Islands by Europeans had acquired a meaning of "lowly people" or "low social status" and not diminutive in stature) to European legends of brownies.

statement.id: Folkloris Katharine Luomala berpendapat bahwa legenda Menehune adalah mitologi pasca-kontak dengan Eropa, yang tercipta dengan menyesuaikan istilah manahune (yang pada masa kolonisasi Eropa bermakna "orang rendahan" atau "berstatus sosial rendah", bukan bertubuh kecil) dengan legenda Eropa tentang brownies.
statement.en: Folklorist Katharine Luomala believes the Menehune legends are a post-European-contact mythology created by adapting the term manahune (which by the time of European colonization meant "lowly people" or "low social status", not small stature) to European legends of brownies.

claims.quote: Some early scholars hypothesized that there was a first settlement of Hawaiʻi, by settlers from the Marquesas Islands, and a second, from Tahiti. The Tahitian settlers oppressed the "commoners", the manahune in the Tahitian language, who fled to the mountains and were called Menahune.

statement.id: Sebagian sarjana awal berhipotesis bahwa Hawaiʻi dimukimi dua kali: pertama oleh pendatang dari Kepulauan Marquesas, kedua dari Tahiti. Pendatang Tahiti menindas "rakyat jelata", yaitu manahune dalam bahasa Tahiti, yang lari ke pegunungan dan disebut Menahune.
statement.en: Some early scholars hypothesized a first settlement of Hawaiʻi from the Marquesas Islands and a second from Tahiti. The Tahitian settlers oppressed the "commoners" (manahune in Tahitian), who fled to the mountains and were called Menahune.

claims.quote: The Menehunes were supposed to have been a wonderful people, small of stature and of great activity. They were always united in doing any service required of them.

statement.id: Menurut catatan Thrum, Menehune dianggap bangsa yang menakjubkan, bertubuh kecil dan sangat aktif, dan mereka selalu bersatu dalam melakukan setiap pekerjaan yang diminta.
statement.en: According to Thrum's account, the Menehunes were supposed to be a wonderful people, small of stature and very active, always united in doing any service required of them.

claims.quote: It was their rule that any work undertaken must be completed in one night, otherwise it would be left unfinished, as they did not labor twice on the same work; hence the origin of the saying: “He po hookahi, a ao ua pau,”—in one night, and by dawn it is finished.

statement.id: Menurut catatan Thrum, aturan mereka adalah bahwa setiap pekerjaan yang dimulai harus selesai dalam satu malam; kalau tidak, pekerjaan itu dibiarkan belum selesai karena mereka tidak mengerjakan hal yang sama dua kali.
statement.en: According to Thrum's account, their rule was that any work undertaken must be finished in one night, otherwise it was left unfinished, as they did not labor twice on the same work.

claims.quote: and were invisible to every one but their own descendants, or those connected with them in some way. Many persons could hear the noise and hum of their voices, but the gift of seeing them with the naked eye was denied to those not akin to them.

statement.id: Menurut catatan Thrum, mereka tidak terlihat oleh siapa pun kecuali keturunan mereka atau orang yang berhubungan dengan mereka; banyak orang dapat mendengar deru dan dengung suara mereka, tetapi kemampuan melihat mereka dengan mata telanjang tidak diberikan kepada yang bukan kerabat.
statement.en: According to Thrum's account, they were invisible to everyone but their own descendants or those connected with them; many could hear the noise and hum of their voices, but the gift of seeing them with the naked eye was denied to those not akin to them.

claims.quote: They were always willing to do the bidding of their descendants, and their supernatural powers enabled them to perform some wonderful works.

statement.id: Menurut catatan Thrum, mereka selalu bersedia memenuhi perintah keturunan mereka, dan kekuatan supernatural mereka memungkinkan mereka melakukan beberapa pekerjaan menakjubkan.
statement.en: According to Thrum's account, they were always willing to do their descendants' bidding, and their supernatural powers enabled them to perform some wonderful works.

claims.quote: Some treat the subject with gravity and respect, and express the belief that they were the original inhabitants of these islands, but gradually gave way to the heavier-bodied ancestors of the present race; ... the more intelligent and better educated look upon the Menehunes as a mythical class of gnomes or dwarfs

statement.id: Menurut Thrum, pendapat orang Hawaii tentang Menehune berbeda: sebagian memperlakukannya dengan serius dan percaya bahwa mereka penghuni asli pulau-pulau itu yang perlahan tersisih oleh leluhur yang bertubuh lebih besar, sedangkan yang lebih terpelajar memandang Menehune sebagai golongan mitos gnome atau kurcaci.
statement.en: According to Thrum, Hawaiians differ about the Menehunes: some treat them with gravity and believe they were the original inhabitants who gradually gave way to heavier-bodied ancestors, while the more educated regard them as a mythical class of gnomes or dwarfs.

claims.quote: At the dead of night he heard the noise and hum of the voices of the Menehunes on their way to Kikiaola, each of whom was carrying a stone. The dam was duly constructed, every stone fitting in its proper place, and the stone auwai, or watercourse, also laid around the bend of Kikiaola. Before the break of day the work was completed

statement.id: Dalam kisah yang dicatat Thrum, pada tengah malam terdengar deru dan dengung suara para Menehune dalam perjalanan ke Kikiaola, masing-masing membawa sebuah batu. Bendungan dibangun dengan setiap batu pas pada tempatnya, dan auwai (saluran air) batu dipasang mengitari tikungan Kikiaola; sebelum fajar pekerjaan itu selesai.
statement.en: In a story recorded by Thrum, at dead of night the hum of the Menehunes' voices was heard on their way to Kikiaola, each carrying a stone. The dam was built with every stone fitting in place, and the stone auwai (watercourse) was laid around the bend of Kikiaola; before daybreak the work was complete.

claims.quote: At one time Pi also told the Menehunes to wall in a fish-pond at the bend of the Huleia River. They commenced work toward midnight, but at dawn the walls of the pond were not sufficiently finished to meet, so it was left incomplete, and has remained so to this day.

statement.id: Dalam kisah yang dicatat Thrum, Pi pernah menyuruh Menehune membuat dinding kolam ikan di tikungan Sungai Huleia. Mereka mulai bekerja menjelang tengah malam, tetapi saat fajar dinding kolam belum cukup rampung untuk bertemu, sehingga dibiarkan tak selesai hingga kini.
statement.en: In a story recorded by Thrum, Pi once told the Menehunes to wall in a fish-pond at the bend of the Huleia River. They began toward midnight, but at dawn the walls were not finished enough to meet, so it was left incomplete and remains so to this day.

claims.quote: The Menehunes told Laka that it would be brought to the halau that night. At the dead of night the hum of the voices of the Menehunes was heard; this was the commencement of the lifting of the canoe. It was not dragged, but held up by hand.

statement.id: Dalam kisah Laka yang dicatat Thrum, Menehune berkata bahwa perahu akan dibawa ke halau malam itu; pada tengah malam terdengar dengung suara mereka, dimulainya pengangkatan perahu, yang tidak diseret melainkan diangkat dengan tangan.
statement.en: In the story of Laka recorded by Thrum, the Menehunes said the canoe would be brought to the halau that night; at dead of night the hum of their voices was heard, the lifting of the canoe began, and it was held up by hand rather than dragged.

claims.quote: The Menehunes are credited with the construction of numerous heiaus (ancient temples) in various parts of the islands.

statement.id: Menurut Thrum, Menehune dikreditkan membangun banyak heiau (kuil kuno) di berbagai bagian kepulauan.
statement.en: According to Thrum, the Menehunes are credited with building numerous heiaus (ancient temples) in various parts of the islands.

claims.quote: The heiau of Mookini, near Honoipu, Kohala, is pointed out as an instance of their marvellous work. ... Tradition says the Menehunes were placed in a line covering the entire distance from Pololu to Honoipu, whereby the stones were passed from hand to hand for the entire work.

statement.id: Menurut Thrum, heiau Mookini, dekat Honoipu, Kohala, ditunjuk sebagai contoh karya menakjubkan mereka; tradisi mengatakan para Menehune ditempatkan berbaris sepanjang seluruh jarak dari Pololu ke Honoipu sehingga batu-batu dioper dari tangan ke tangan selama seluruh pekerjaan.
statement.en: According to Thrum, the heiau of Mookini, near Honoipu, Kohala, is pointed out as an instance of their marvellous work; tradition says the Menehunes were placed in a line covering the whole distance from Pololu to Honoipu, so that the stones were passed from hand to hand throughout the work.

claims.quote: There stands on the pali of Waikolu, near Kalaupapa, Molokai, a heiau that Hawaiians believe to have been constructed by no one else than the Menehunes.

statement.id: Menurut Thrum, di tebing (pali) Waikolu, dekat Kalaupapa, Molokai, berdiri sebuah heiau yang diyakini orang Hawaii dibangun oleh tidak lain daripada Menehune.
statement.en: According to Thrum, on the pali of Waikolu, near Kalaupapa, Molokai, stands a heiau that Hawaiians believe was built by none other than the Menehunes.

topic.en: Origin and nature of the Menehune

summary.id: Tradisi: bangsa mirip kurcaci yang tinggal di Hawaiʻi sebelum pemukim dari Polinesia tiba.
summary.en: Tradition: a dwarf-like people who lived in Hawaiʻi before settlers from Polynesia arrived.

summary.id: Sebagian orang Hawaii (menurut Thrum): penghuni asli yang tersisih; yang lebih terpelajar: golongan mitos gnome atau kurcaci.
summary.en: Some Hawaiians (per Thrum): the original inhabitants who gave way; the more educated: a mythical class of gnomes or dwarfs.

summary.id: Sarjana awal: "rakyat jelata" (manahune) yang ditindas pendatang Tahiti lalu lari ke pegunungan.
summary.en: Early scholars: the "commoners" (manahune) oppressed by Tahitian settlers who fled to the mountains.

summary.id: Katharine Luomala: mitologi pasca-kontak dengan Eropa yang menyesuaikan istilah manahune dengan legenda brownies Eropa.
summary.en: Katharine Luomala: a post-European-contact mythology adapting the term manahune to European brownie legends.

short_description.id: Miage-nyūdō adalah yōkai yang dikisahkan di Pulau Sado. Ia tergolong jenis mikoshi-nyūdō: sosok mirip biksu kecil yang menjulang ketika dipandang ke atas.
short_description.en: The miage-nyūdō is a yōkai told of on Sado Island. It is a type of mikoshi-nyūdō: a small monk-like figure that grows taller when looked up at.

long_description.id: Miage-nyūdō adalah yōkai yang dikisahkan di Pulau Sado (Niigata), dan tergolong jenis mikoshi-nyūdō. Yokai.com mencantumkan miage nyūdō sebagai salah satu nama lain mikoshi nyūdō ("pendeta yang mengantisipasi").
long_description.en: The miage-nyūdō is a yōkai told of on Sado Island (Niigata), and is a type of mikoshi-nyūdō. Yokai.com lists miage nyūdō among the alternate names of the mikoshi nyūdō ("anticipating priest").

long_description.id: Saat mendaki tanjakan kecil di malam hari, sosok seperti biksu kecil muncul di depan. Bila orang menengadah, ia menjadi lebih tinggi dan orang itu jatuh terlentang. Yokai.com menggambarkan mikoshi nyūdō tumbuh setinggi pandangan pengamat dan secepat itu pula.
long_description.en: When climbing a small slope at night, something in the form of a little monk appears ahead. If one looks up, it grows taller and the person falls over backwards. Yokai.com describes the mikoshi nyūdō as growing as tall as the observer can raise his eyes, and just as fast.

long_description.id: Dikatakan bahwa mengucapkan rumus bahwa tipunya sudah terbaca sambil berbaring tengkurap membuatnya lenyap; seorang pelancong juga memukulnya dengan tongkat. Menurut Yokai.com, memandang dari kepala ke kaki melemahkan kemampuannya bertambah tinggi. Versi daerah berbeda: di Hamochi ia mencuri makanan dan uang pelancong, di Utami sebuah batu besar berubah menjadi nyūdō, di Akadomari ia meremukkan pelancong sebelum jatuh ke jurang, dan di Hatano tantangan membuatnya jatuh.
long_description.en: It is said that chanting that its trick has been seen through while lying down forwards makes it disappear; one traveler also struck it with a rod. According to Yokai.com, looking from head to feet saps its power to grow. Regional versions differ: in Hamochi it steals travelers' food and money, in Utami a large stone has become a nyūdō, in Akadomari it crushed travelers before falling into a ravine, and in Hatano a challenge makes it fall down.

long_description.id: Menurut Yokai.com, hewan pengubah wujud seperti itachi dan tanuki disebut berubah menjadi raksasa mikoshi nyūdō untuk memburu manusia.
long_description.en: According to Yokai.com, shape-shifting animals such as itachi and tanuki are said to turn into mikoshi nyūdō giants to hunt humans.

description.id: Sosok kecil seperti biksu muncul di depan pelancong malam dan menjadi lebih tinggi ketika dipandang ke atas, sehingga orang itu jatuh terlentang.
description.en: A small monk-like figure appears before night travelers and grows taller when looked up at, so that the person falls over backwards.

description.id: Di Hamochi, miage-nyūdō yang muncul di tempat bernama Tsujidō dikatakan mencuri makanan dan uang pelancong.
description.en: In Hamochi, the miage-nyūdō that appears at a place called Tsujidō is said to steal food and money from travelers.

description.id: Dikatakan bahwa dengan mengucapkan rumus itu dan berbaring tengkurap, sosok itu lenyap; seorang pelancong juga memukulnya dengan tongkat sambil mengucapkannya.
description.en: It is said that chanting the formula and lying down forwards makes it disappear; one traveler also struck it with a rod while chanting.

description.id: Menurut Yokai.com, memandang dari kepala ke kaki melemahkan kemampuannya bertambah tinggi, dan menyatakan bahwa tipunya sudah terbaca membuatnya lenyap.
description.en: According to Yokai.com, looking from head to feet saps its power to grow, and declaring that its trick was anticipated makes it vanish.

description.id: Di Hatano, menantangnya dengan mengatakan yang dulu terlihat jauh lebih besar membuat kakinya mengecil dan ia jatuh.
description.en: In Hatano, challenging it by saying the earlier one was much larger makes its feet thin and it falls.

description.id: Di Utami, setelah sebuah jizō dipuja di atas batu itu, nyūdō tersebut tidak muncul lagi.
description.en: In Utami, after a jizō was deified above the rock, the nyūdō no longer appeared.

description.id: Miage-nyūdō yang muncul di tempat bernama Tsujidō mencuri makanan dan uang pelancong.
description.en: The miage-nyūdō appearing at a place called Tsujidō steals travelers' food and money.

description.id: Batu besar bernama "miage-ishi" (batu "menengadah") berubah wujud menjadi nyūdō di tempat yang rimbun dan redup bahkan siang hari.
description.en: A large stone called the "miage-ishi" ("look up stone") shapeshifted into a nyūdō in a thickly wooded place dim even at noon.

description.id: Miage-nyūdō yang membunuh pelancong malam jatuh ke jurang, berjanji tidak menyerang lagi, dan jurang itu kemudian disebut "rawa nyūdō".
description.en: A miage-nyūdō that killed night travelers fell into a ravine and no longer appeared; the ravine began to be called the "nyūdō marsh".

description.id: Menantang miage-nyūdō dengan mengatakan yang dulu jauh lebih besar membuat kakinya mengecil sehingga ia jatuh.
description.en: Challenging the miage-nyūdō by saying the earlier one was much larger makes its feet thin and it falls down.

role.id: Sosok kecil menjulang ketika dipandang ke atas.
role.en: A small figure that grows taller when looked up at.

summary.id: Saat mendaki tanjakan kecil di malam hari, sosok seperti biksu kecil muncul di depan; bila orang menengadah, ia menjadi lebih tinggi dan orang itu jatuh terlentang.
summary.en: When climbing a small slope at night, something in the form of a little monk appears ahead; if one looks up it grows taller and the person falls over backwards.

title.en: The nyūdō of the Akadomari ravine

role.id: Pembunuh pelancong malam yang akhirnya berhenti muncul.
role.en: A killer of night travelers that eventually stopped appearing.

summary.id: Miage-nyūdō yang meremukkan pelancong jatuh ke dasar jurang dan ditolong dengan syarat tidak menyerang lagi dan menjauhi tempat itu; jurang itu lalu disebut "rawa nyūdō".
summary.en: A miage-nyūdō that crushed travelers fell to the bottom of a ravine and was helped on condition that it stop attacking and stay away; the ravine began to be called the "nyūdō marsh".

description.id: Miage-nyūdō dikisahkan di Pulau Sado (Sado, Niigata).
description.en: The miage-nyūdō is told of on Sado Island (Sado, Niigata).

note.id: Miage-nyūdō tergolong jenis mikoshi-nyūdō.
note.en: The miage-nyūdō is a type of mikoshi-nyūdō.

claims.quote: Miage-nyūdō is a type of yōkai told about on Sado Island (Sado, Niigata Prefecture).

statement.id: Miage-nyūdō adalah yōkai dari Pulau Sado.
statement.en: Miage-nyūdō is a yōkai of Sado Island.

claims.quote: They are a type of mikoshi-nyūdō.

statement.id: Ia digolongkan sebagai jenis mikoshi-nyūdō.
statement.en: It is classified as a kind of mikoshi-nyūdō.

claims.quote: When climbing a small slope at night, something taking on the appearance of a little bōzu would appear in front, and by looking up, it would become taller, and the person looking at it would fall down backwards.

statement.id: Sosok itu bertambah tinggi ketika pelancong mendongak melihatnya.
statement.en: The figure grows taller when a traveler looks up at it.

claims.quote: It is said that by chanting "miage-nyūdō, I've seen past you (見上入道、見越した )" and lying down forwards, it would disappear.

statement.id: Ucapan bahwa tipuannya telah diketahui konon mengusirnya.
statement.en: A formula declaring that its trick has been seen through is said to dispel it.

claims.quote: In Hamochi, Sado District (now a part of Sado), it is said that the miage-nyūdō that appears at a place called Tsujidō would steal food and money from travelers.

statement.id: Versi Hamochi mencuri makanan dan uang pelancong.
statement.en: A Hamochi version steals travelers’ food and money.

claims.quote: In Utami, Ryōtsu (now a part of Sado), it is said that they are in places where trees grow thickly and is dim even at noon, and that a large stone called the "miage-ishi (見上石, look up stone)" has shapeshifted into a nyūdō.

statement.id: Kisah Utami mengaitkannya dengan batu yang berubah wujud.
statement.en: An Utami account associates it with a stone that changes form.

claims.quote: Once, a traveler met this, and by chanting "miage-nyūdō, I've seen past you" and striking it with a rod, the nyūdō disappeared. It is said that afterwards, when a jizō was deified above the rock, the nyūdō no longer appeared.

statement.id: Menurut satu kisah, seorang pelancong mengucapkan rumus "sudah kulihat tipumu" sambil memukul sosok itu dengan tongkat sehingga ia lenyap; setelah sebuah jizō dipuja di atas batu itu, nyūdō tersebut tidak muncul lagi.
statement.en: In one account a traveler chanted the "I've seen past you" formula and struck the figure with a rod, and it vanished; after a jizō was deified above the rock, the nyūdō no longer appeared.

claims.quote: Also, in a legend of Akadomari (now a part of Sado), Sado District, there was a miage-nyūdō that squashed and killed night travelers, but it once accidentally fell to the bottom of a ravine, and since it was helped by someone under the condition that it would "no longer attack people" and to "stay away from that place," it no longer appeared there

statement.id: Dalam legenda Akadomari, miage-nyūdō yang meremukkan dan membunuh pelancong malam jatuh ke dasar jurang, ditolong dengan syarat tidak menyerang orang lagi dan menjauhi tempat itu, lalu tidak muncul lagi di sana.
statement.en: In a legend from Akadomari, a miage-nyūdō that crushed and killed night travelers fell to the bottom of a ravine, was helped on condition that it no longer attack people and stay away from that place, and no longer appeared there.

claims.quote: In Hatano, Sado District (now a part of Sado), it is said that when those who meet a miage-nyūdō say, "the miage-nyūdō I saw before was much larger" and thus challenge it, and since its feet would thus become thinner, a violent sound would result, and the miage-nyūdō would fall down.

statement.id: Di Hatano dikatakan bahwa orang yang bertemu miage-nyūdō dan menantangnya dengan mengatakan bahwa yang dulu dilihatnya jauh lebih besar membuat kakinya mengecil, terdengar bunyi keras, lalu miage-nyūdō itu jatuh.
statement.en: In Hatano it is said that when someone meeting a miage-nyūdō challenges it by saying the one seen before was much larger, its feet thin out, a violent sound results, and the miage-nyūdō falls down.

claims.quote: Mikoshi nyūdō 見越入道 みこしにゅうどう Translation: anticipating priest Alternate names: mikoshi, miage nyūdō, taka bōzu

statement.id: Yokai.com mencantumkan miage nyūdō di antara nama lain mikoshi nyūdō, "pendeta yang mengantisipasi".
statement.en: Yokai.com lists miage nyūdō among the alternate names of the mikoshi nyūdō, "anticipating priest".

claims.quote: As soon as a person raises his eyes to look upon a mikoshi nyūdō, the giant grows to an immense height—as tall the observer is able to raise his eyes, and just as fast.

statement.id: Menurut Yokai.com, begitu orang menengadah pada mikoshi nyūdō, raksasa itu tumbuh setinggi pandangan si pengamat dan secepat itu pula.
statement.en: According to Yokai.com, as soon as a person looks up at a mikoshi nyūdō, the giant grows as tall as the observer can raise his eyes, and just as fast.

claims.quote: Then, look from its head down to its feet, rather than starting at the feet and looking up. If done properly, the giant’s power to grow will be sapped.

statement.id: Menurut Yokai.com, jika orang memandang mikoshi nyūdō dari kepala ke kaki alih-alih dari kaki ke atas, kemampuan raksasa itu untuk bertambah tinggi akan melemah.
statement.en: According to Yokai.com, looking at a mikoshi nyūdō from its head down to its feet instead of from the feet up saps the giant's power to grow.

claims.quote: Telling the giant, “You lost! I anticipated your trick!” causes it to vanish in anger, leaving the traveler to pass safely along.

statement.id: Menurut Yokai.com, mengatakan kepada raksasa itu bahwa ia kalah dan tipunya sudah diantisipasi membuatnya lenyap dengan marah sehingga pelancong dapat lewat dengan selamat.
statement.en: According to Yokai.com, telling the giant that it lost and its trick was anticipated makes it vanish in anger, leaving the traveler to pass safely.

claims.quote: Mikoshi nyūdō is a popular form of some shape-shifting animals. In particular, itachi and tanuki transform into these giants in order to hunt humans.

statement.id: Menurut Yokai.com, wujud mikoshi nyūdō populer bagi hewan pengubah wujud; itachi dan tanuki disebut berubah menjadi raksasa ini untuk memburu manusia.
statement.en: According to Yokai.com, the mikoshi nyūdō form is popular with shape-shifting animals; itachi and tanuki are said to turn into these giants to hunt humans.

short_description.id: Mixtecatl adalah salah satu dari enam raksasa putra Iztac-Mixcoatl dan Tlaltecuhtli dalam mitologi Aztek, pendiri Mixtlan [mixtecatl-c01, mixtecatl-c02].
short_description.en: Mixtecatl is one of the six giant sons of Iztac-Mixcoatl and Tlaltecuhtli in Aztec mythology, founder of Mixtlan [mixtecatl-c01, mixtecatl-c02].

long_description.id: Mixtecatl adalah salah satu dari enam raksasa putra Iztac-Mixcoatl dan Tlaltecuhtli yang menghuni Bumi setelah Air Bah [mixtecatl-c01]. Sebagai putra kelima, ia mendirikan Mixtlan, asal penduduk wilayah Mixteca [mixtecatl-c02].
long_description.en: Mixtecatl is one of the six giant sons of Iztac-Mixcoatl and Tlaltecuhtli who populated the Earth after the Great Flood [mixtecatl-c01]. The fifth son, he founded Mixtlan, origin of the people of the Mixteca region [mixtecatl-c02].

long_description.id: Sebuah puisi kosmogoni Nahoa berbait kosong, lengkap dengan catatan kaki, menyebut sosok yang mengambil nama Ilancuéye [mixtecatl-c03]. "Ular awan putih" bersatu dengannya, dan enam tlacámes (laki-laki) lahir sebagai saudara yang menjadi sumber banyak bangsa [mixtecatl-c04]. Dalam puisi itu Mixtécatl yang gagah berani berlindung dari Mixtecápan di perbukitan tandus, tempat yang kini disebut sederhana Mixteca [mixtecatl-c05]. Nama Iztamixcóhuatl, menurut catatan kaki, tersusun dari iztac (putih), mixtli (awan), dan cohuatl (ular) [mixtecatl-c06]. Catatan kaki lain menyebut orang Indian percaya bumi mula-mula dihuni raksasa, yang dalam catatan itu disebut quinametzin [mixtecatl-c08].
long_description.en: A Nahoa cosmogony poem in blank verse, with footnotes, names a being who takes the name Ilancuéye [mixtecatl-c03]. The "serpent of white cloud" is joined with her, and six tlacámes (men) are engendered as brothers who become the source of many races [mixtecatl-c04]. In the poem the valiant Mixtécatl guards himself from Mixtecápan in the barren hills, a place today called simply Mixteca [mixtecatl-c05]. According to a footnote, the name Iztamixcóhuatl is composed of iztac (white), mixtli (cloud) and cohuatl (serpent) [mixtecatl-c06]. Another footnote says the Indians believed the earth was first inhabited by giants, whom that note calls quinametzin [mixtecatl-c08].

long_description.id: Nama ibu para raksasa berbeda antar sumber: satu sumber menyebut Tlaltecuhtli atau Ilancueitl [mixtecatl-c01], sedangkan puisi tersebut memakai Ilancuéye dan catatannya menyebut Orozco y Berra, mengikuti Torquemada, keliru memakai Ilancueitl [mixtecatl-c07].
long_description.en: Sources differ on the giants' mother: one names Tlaltecuhtli or Ilancueitl [mixtecatl-c01], while the poem uses Ilancuéye and its note says Orozco y Berra, following Torquemada, erred in using Ilancueitl [mixtecatl-c07].

literal_meaning.en: Inhabitant of the land of clouds

claims.quote: Mixtecatl (From Nahuatl, 'Inhabitant of the land of clouds') is one of the six giants sons of Iztac-Mixcoatl and Tlaltecuhtli or Ilancueitl that populated the Earth after the Great Flood during the Fifth Sun in Aztec mythology.

statement.id: Mixtecatl adalah salah satu dari enam raksasa putra Iztac-Mixcoatl dan Tlaltecuhtli (atau Ilancueitl) yang menghuni Bumi setelah Air Bah pada masa Matahari Kelima dalam mitologi Aztek.
statement.en: Mixtecatl is one of the six giant sons of Iztac-Mixcoatl and Tlaltecuhtli (or Ilancueitl) who populated the Earth after the Great Flood in the Fifth Sun of Aztec mythology.

claims.quote: The fifth son who founded Mixtlan from where the natives of the region known today as Mixteca come from.

statement.id: Ia putra kelima yang mendirikan Mixtlan, asal penduduk wilayah yang kini disebut Mixteca.
statement.en: He was the fifth son, founder of Mixtlan, origin of the people of the region now called Mixteca.

claims.quote: With many jaws and bloody tongues; By such a metamorphosis is sanctified, And takes the rare name of Ilancuéye:

statement.id: Dalam puisi kosmogoni Nahoa ini, sosok berahang banyak dan berlidah berdarah, lewat suatu metamorfosis, disucikan dan mengambil nama langka Ilancuéye.
statement.en: In this Nahoa cosmogony poem, a being of many jaws and bloody tongues, by a metamorphosis, is sanctified and takes the rare name of Ilancuéye.

claims.quote: the «ferocious serpent Of white cloud» which lives in Citlálco, (24) With her is joined in sweet union, Of love, which six tlacámes engender; (25) These brothers dwell on the earth And become the source of many races:

statement.id: Dalam puisi itu, "ular ganas dari awan putih" yang tinggal di Citlálco bersatu dengannya, dan persatuan itu melahirkan enam tlacámes (laki-laki); saudara-saudara ini hidup di bumi dan menjadi sumber banyak bangsa.
statement.en: In the poem, the "ferocious serpent of white cloud" who lives in Citlálco is joined with her, six tlacámes (men) are engendered, and these brothers dwell on the earth and become the source of many races.

claims.quote: The valiant Mixtécatl guards himself From Mixtecápan in the barren hills; (32) ... (32) Today is called simply Mixteca.

statement.id: Dalam puisi itu, Mixtécatl yang gagah berani berlindung dari Mixtecápan di perbukitan tandus; catatan kaki 32 menyatakan bahwa kini ia disebut sederhana Mixteca.
statement.en: In the poem, the valiant Mixtécatl guards himself from Mixtecápan in the barren hills; footnote 32 states that it is today called simply Mixteca.

claims.quote: Iztamixcóhuatl is composed of iztac, white, mixtli, cloud, and cohuatl, serpent;

statement.id: Catatan kaki dalam buku yang sama menjelaskan bahwa nama Iztamixcóhuatl tersusun dari iztac (putih), mixtli (awan), dan cohuatl (ular).
statement.en: A footnote in the same book explains that the name Iztamixcóhuatl is composed of iztac (white), mixtli (cloud) and cohuatl (serpent).

claims.quote: Ilancueye is composed of ilamatl or ilantli, old, and of cueye, corruption of cueyatl, "frog; old frog." Mr. Orozco y Berra, following Torquemada, fell into the error of calling this goddess Ilancueitl

statement.id: Catatan kaki menjelaskan bahwa Ilancueye berarti "katak tua" dan menyebut Orozco y Berra, mengikuti Torquemada, keliru menyebut sang dewi Ilancueitl.
statement.en: A footnote explains that Ilancueye means "old frog" and says Mr. Orozco y Berra, following Torquemada, fell into the error of calling this goddess Ilancueitl.

claims.quote: The Indians believed that the earth was first inhabited by giants, and the large pachyderm bones that were found in a fossilized state in excavations, were their remains. They called them quinametzin,

statement.en: A footnote in the same book says the Indians believed the earth was first inhabited by giants, and that the large fossilized bones found in excavations were their remains; they called them quinametzin.

short_description.id: Mizuchi adalah sejenis naga atau makhluk mirip ular dalam legenda Jepang yang berhubungan dengan air; sebagian pengamat menganggapnya dewa air. Ia tercatat dalam Nihon Shoki dan sebuah puisi Man'yōshū.
short_description.en: The mizuchi is a Japanese dragon or serpent-like creature tied to water; some commentators saw a water deity in it. The Nihon Shoki and one Man'yōshū poem record it.

long_description.id: Mizuchi (大虬, 蛟龙, 蛟, 美都知) adalah sejenis naga Jepang atau makhluk legendaris mirip ular yang hidup di perairan atau berhubungan dengan air. Sebagian pengamat menganggapnya dewa air. Menurut artikel bahasa Jepang, ia dianggap berkaitan dengan air dalam mitos dan legenda, dan 『和名抄』 menyamakan 「蛟」 dengan 「大虬」 dalam 日本書紀.
long_description.en: Mizuchi (大虬, 蛟龙, 蛟, 美都知) names a dragon-like or serpent-like creature of Japanese legend that lives in water or is tied to it. Certain commentators took it to be a water god. According to the Japanese article it is regarded as connected with water in myth and legend, and 『和名抄』 equates 「蛟」 with 「大虬」 in the 日本書紀.

long_description.id: Kronik Nihongi mencatat seekor ular atau naga air besar di Provinsi Kibi yang menyemburkan racun dan membunuh banyak orang yang lewat. Seorang pria bernama Agatamori melempar tiga labu ke kolam dan menantang makhluk itu menenggelamkannya; makhluk itu berubah menjadi rusa, gagal, lalu dibunuh.
long_description.en: The Nihongi chronicle records a great water serpent or dragon in Kibi Province that spewed venom and killed many passersby. A man named Agatamori cast three calabashes into the pool and challenged the creature to sink them; it turned into a deer, failed, and was slain.

long_description.id: Namanya dalam bahasa kuno dilafalkan mi-tsu-chi dan dapat diuraikan menjadi mi "air", tsu partikel "dari", dan chi "roh". Kunio Yanagita menekankan bahwa mizuchi menandakan "roh air", sedangkan 南方熊楠 menyatakan ular-ular yang ditakuti di tepi air disebut ミヅチ dalam arti "penguasa air". Minakata juga menduga bahwa di sebagian daerah mizuchi kemudian dianggap makhluk sejenis kappa.
long_description.en: In olden times the name was pronounced mi-tsu-chi and can be broken down into mi "water", tsu a particle meaning "of", and chi "spirit". Kunio Yanagita stressed that the mizuchi signifies a "water spirit", while 南方熊楠 stated that the feared snakes living by the water were called ミヅチ in the sense of "master of the water". Minakata also conjectured that in some regions the mizuchi later came to be regarded as creatures of the kappa kind.

description.en: The beast could not sink the three floating calabashes and was slain by the man.

statement.en: The ancient chronicle Nihongi contains references to mizuchi: in central Kibi Province, at a fork of the Kawashima River (川嶋河, old name of the Takahashi River in Okayama Prefecture), a great water serpent or dragon (大虬) dwelt and spewed venom that poisoned and killed many passersby.

statement.id: Menurut artikel bahasa Jepang, 蛟 (みずち; bacaan lama 「みつち」) adalah jenis naga, ular legendaris, atau dewa air yang dianggap berkaitan dengan air dalam mitos dan legenda Jepang.
statement.en: According to the Japanese article, 蛟 (みずち; old reading 「みつち」) is a kind of dragon, legendary serpent or water deity regarded as connected with water in Japanese myth and legend.

claims.quote: 南方熊楠は、『十二支考・蛇』の冒頭で、「わが邦でも水辺に住んで人に怖れらるる諸蛇を水の主というほどの意〔こころ〕でミヅチと呼んだらしい」としている。

statement.id: 南方熊楠 menulis bahwa di Jepang pun berbagai ular yang tinggal di tepi air dan ditakuti orang tampaknya disebut ミヅチ dengan arti "penguasa air".
statement.en: 南方熊楠 wrote that in Japan too the various snakes living by the water and feared by people seem to have been called ミヅチ in the sense of "master of the water".

claims.quote: 『和名抄』は、「虬龍」、「螭龍」、「蛟」のいずれの項もあるが、このうち「蛟（こう）」を和名の「美豆知」とし、日本書紀の「大虬（みづち）」に相当すると注釈されている。

short_description.id: Muki adalah makhluk kerdil mirip goblin dalam mitologi Andes Tengah yang hidup di dalam tambang [muki-mythology-c01, muki-mythology-c02, muki-mythology-c03].
short_description.en: The muki is a dwarfish, goblin-like creature of Central Andean mythology that lives inside the mines [muki-mythology-c01, muki-mythology-c02, muki-mythology-c03].

long_description.id: Muki adalah makhluk mirip goblin dalam mitologi Andes Tengah [muki-mythology-c01] yang hidup di dalam tambang [muki-mythology-c02]. Tingginya tidak lebih dari 2 kaki [muki-mythology-c03], dan dalam beberapa tradisi ia bertanduk dua untuk memecah batu dan menunjuk urat mineral [muki-mythology-c04]. Ia bisa menyamar sebagai hewan atau lelaki berambut pirang untuk menipu penambang [muki-mythology-c05]; para tetua menyarankan melawannya dengan ikat pinggang [muki-mythology-c06].
long_description.en: The muki is a goblin-like creature of Central Andean mythology [muki-mythology-c01] that lives inside the mines [muki-mythology-c02]. He is no taller than 2 feet [muki-mythology-c03], and in some traditions has two horns to break rocks and point out veins [muki-mythology-c04]. He may disguise himself as an animal or a blond man to deceive miners [muki-mythology-c05]; elders advise fighting him with a belt [muki-mythology-c06].

long_description.id: Menurut sebuah artikel majalah pertambangan, legenda Muki dituturkan di kamp tambang terpencil dari Kolombia hingga Bolivia, dengan nama yang berbeda antardaerah seperti chinchiliku dan jusshi [muki-mythology-c07]. Menurut tradisi lisan, ia berotot tidak proporsional, bersuara dalam, berkulit pucat, berambut pirang panjang, dan bermata yang memantulkan cahaya seperti logam [muki-mythology-c14]. Tema umum adalah kesepakatan dengan penambang: ia menukar pengetahuan atau bantuan dengan alkohol atau koka [muki-mythology-c09], tetapi sebagai penipu atau iblis ia bisa membuat kesepakatan itu berbalik buruk bagi penambang yang serakah [muki-mythology-c10]. Sebagian cerita menggambarkannya sebagai penolong yang menuntun penambang ke bijih atau memperingatkan bahaya [muki-mythology-c12], sementara yang lain sebagai goblin pemangsa [muki-mythology-c13].
long_description.en: According to a mining-industry magazine article, Muki legends are shared in isolated mining camps from Colombia to Bolivia, under names that differ by region such as chinchiliku and jusshi [muki-mythology-c07]. In oral tradition he is disproportionately muscular, deep-voiced, ghostly pale, with long blond hair and eyes that reflect the light like metals [muki-mythology-c14]. A common theme is deals with miners: he trades knowledge or help for alcohol or coca [muki-mythology-c09], but as a trickster or demon he can make those deals backfire for greedy miners [muki-mythology-c10]. Some stories paint him as a helpful figure who leads miners to ore or warns of dangers [muki-mythology-c12], while others paint a predatory goblin [muki-mythology-c13].

long_description.id: Artikel yang sama menyebut kata muki berasal dari kata Quechua murik, "mencekik" atau "menyesakkan", merujuk pada debu dan silika yang memenuhi paru-paru penambang [muki-mythology-c08], dan menilai penjelasan paling masuk akal bagi legendanya adalah bahwa Muki mempersonifikasikan bahaya dan risiko pekerjaan penambang [muki-mythology-c11].
long_description.en: The same article says the word muki comes from the Quechua word murik, "to smother" or "to strangle", a reference to the dust and silica that fill miners' lungs [muki-mythology-c08], and judges the most plausible explanation for the legends to be that the Muki personifies the dangers and risks of the miners' work [muki-mythology-c11].

sources.publisher: CIM Magazine (Canadian Institute of Mining, Metallurgy and Petroleum)

claims.quote: is a goblin-like creature in the mythology of the Central Andes in Bolivia, Peru, Ecuador and Colombia.

statement.id: Muki adalah makhluk mirip goblin dalam mitologi Andes Tengah di Bolivia, Peru, Ekuador, dan Kolombia.
statement.en: The muki is a goblin-like creature of Central Andean mythology in Bolivia, Peru, Ecuador and Colombia.

claims.quote: He is known to be a miner and his existence is constrained to underground spaces: The muki lives inside the mines.

statement.id: Ia dikenal sebagai penambang yang hanya hidup di ruang bawah tanah, yaitu di dalam tambang.
statement.en: He is a miner whose existence is confined underground: the muki lives inside the mines.

claims.quote: The muki is considered to be a dwarf due to its height, since it is no taller than 2 feet (0.61 meters).

statement.id: Muki dianggap kurcaci karena tingginya tidak lebih dari 2 kaki.
statement.en: The muki is considered a dwarf, no taller than 2 feet.

claims.quote: In some mining traditions, he has two horns that are used to break the rocks and point at the mineral veins.

statement.id: Dalam beberapa tradisi tambang, ia bertanduk dua untuk memecah batu dan menunjuk urat mineral.
statement.en: In some mining traditions he has two horns to break rocks and point to mineral veins.

claims.quote: Sometimes he shape-shifts into an animal or a blonde white man to appear to the miners and deceive them.

statement.id: Kadang ia berubah menjadi hewan atau lelaki kulit putih berambut pirang untuk menipu para penambang.
statement.en: Sometimes he turns into an animal or a blond white man to deceive the miners.

claims.quote: Elders advise that, when dealing with the muki, one should use his/her belt to battle him without succumbing to fear.

statement.id: Para tetua menasihati agar melawan muki dengan ikat pinggang tanpa takut.
statement.en: Elders advise fighting the muki with one's belt without giving in to fear.

claims.quote: Legends of the Muki have been consistently shared over the years in isolated mining camps as far north as Colombia, as far south as Bolivia, and in the Peruvian Andes in between. However, its name differs from region to region – people in the Moquegua region in the south of Peru speak of a chinchiliku, and those in the northern Cajamarca region call it the jusshi.

statement.id: Legenda Muki dituturkan di kamp-kamp tambang terpencil dari Kolombia di utara hingga Bolivia di selatan dan di Andes Peru di antaranya; namanya berbeda antardaerah, misalnya chinchiliku di wilayah Moquegua dan jusshi di wilayah Cajamarca.
statement.en: Legends of the Muki are shared in isolated mining camps from Colombia in the north to Bolivia in the south, and in the Peruvian Andes between; its name differs by region, for example chinchiliku in the Moquegua region and jusshi in the Cajamarca region.

claims.quote: The word muki comes from the Quechua word murik, which means “to smother” or “to strangle,” a reference to the often lethal dust and silica that would fill miners’ lungs.

statement.id: Menurut artikel ini, kata muki berasal dari kata Quechua murik yang berarti "mencekik" atau "menyesakkan", merujuk pada debu dan silika yang sering mematikan dan memenuhi paru-paru penambang.
statement.en: According to this article, the word muki comes from the Quechua word murik, meaning "to smother" or "to strangle", a reference to the often lethal dust and silica that would fill miners' lungs.

claims.quote: One common theme in Muki lore is the tendency for the creature to make deals with miners. The Muki is said to trade valuable mining knowledge or help in exchange for luxuries such as alcohol or coca.

statement.id: Satu tema umum dalam cerita Muki adalah kecenderungannya membuat kesepakatan dengan penambang; ia konon menukar pengetahuan atau bantuan penambangan yang berharga dengan barang mewah seperti alkohol atau koka.
statement.en: One common theme in Muki lore is its tendency to make deals with miners; it is said to trade valuable mining knowledge or help for luxuries such as alcohol or coca.

claims.quote: However, the Muki plays the part of a trickster or demon, and these deals can backfire badly for miners who are greedy and indiscreet about their luck.

statement.id: Namun Muki berperan sebagai penipu atau iblis, dan kesepakatan itu bisa berbalik buruk bagi penambang yang serakah dan ceroboh membicarakan keberuntungannya.
statement.en: However, the Muki plays the part of a trickster or demon, and these deals can backfire badly for miners who are greedy and indiscreet about their luck.

claims.quote: The most plausible – and unfortunate – explanation for the rise and spread of Muki legends involve the creature as a personification of the dangers and risks miners accept in their line of work.

statement.id: Artikel ini menyebut penjelasan paling masuk akal bagi munculnya legenda Muki adalah bahwa makhluk itu mempersonifikasikan bahaya dan risiko yang diterima penambang dalam pekerjaan mereka.
statement.en: The article calls the most plausible explanation for the rise and spread of Muki legends that the creature personifies the dangers and risks miners accept in their line of work.

claims.quote: Some stories paint the creature in a more positive light, as a mysterious but helpful figure who can lead miners to productive ore deposits or warn them of dangers underground.

statement.id: Sebagian cerita menggambarkannya secara lebih positif, sebagai tokoh misterius tetapi suka menolong yang dapat menuntun penambang ke endapan bijih yang produktif atau memperingatkan mereka akan bahaya di bawah tanah.
statement.en: Some stories paint the creature in a more positive light, as a mysterious but helpful figure who can lead miners to productive ore deposits or warn them of dangers underground.

claims.quote: while some legends paint him as something of a predatory goblin searching for unsuspecting children or isolated miners to attack, in general the existence of the Muki has become a sort of catch-all for the mysterious goings-on underground.

statement.id: Sebagian legenda menggambarkannya sebagai goblin pemangsa yang mencari anak-anak atau penambang terpencil untuk diserang, tetapi pada umumnya keberadaan Muki menjadi penjelasan serba guna untuk kejadian misterius di bawah tanah.
statement.en: Some legends paint him as a predatory goblin searching for unsuspecting children or isolated miners to attack, but in general the Muki has become a catch-all for the mysterious goings-on underground.

claims.quote: According to oral tradition, the Muki is no more than two feet in height, yet is disproportionately muscular, with a deep voice. His skin is described as ghostly pale, with long blond hair framing dazzling eyes that reflect the light, like the metals in the mines he inhabits.

statement.id: Menurut tradisi lisan, Muki tidak lebih tinggi dari dua kaki namun berotot tidak proporsional dan bersuara dalam; kulitnya digambarkan pucat seperti hantu, dengan rambut pirang panjang dan mata berkilau yang memantulkan cahaya seperti logam di tambang.
statement.en: According to oral tradition, the Muki is no more than two feet tall yet disproportionately muscular, with a deep voice; his skin is described as ghostly pale, with long blond hair and dazzling eyes that reflect the light like the metals in the mines.

summary.id: Penolong misterius yang menuntun penambang ke bijih atau memperingatkan bahaya.
summary.en: A mysterious helper who leads miners to ore or warns of dangers.

summary.id: Goblin pemangsa yang mencari anak-anak atau penambang terpencil untuk diserang.
summary.en: A predatory goblin seeking children or isolated miners to attack.

gaps.searched: Tidak ada gambar Commons yang terbukti menggambarkan makhluk ini; artikel Wikipedia-nya tidak memuat ilustrasi makhluk tersebut.

short_description.id: Murkatta adalah hantu tanpa kepala dalam tradisi Nepal, bermata dan bermulut di dada.
short_description.en: Murkatta is a headless ghost in Nepalese tradition with eyes and a mouth in the chest.

long_description.id: Murkatta adalah hantu tanpa kepala dalam tradisi Nepal, bermata dan bermulut di dada. Ia digambarkan membawa kepalanya di bawah lengan.
long_description.en: Murkatta is a headless ghost in Nepalese tradition with eyes and a mouth in the chest. It is portrayed carrying its head under its arm.

long_description.id: Sumber menganggap mereka sebagai roh orang mati. Murkatta juga ditafsirkan sebagai simbol kekalahan atau hilangnya kecerdasan.
long_description.en: The source regards them as spirits of the dead. Murkatta is also interpreted as symbolising defeat or loss of intellect.

long_description.id: Di Kathmandu, festival pada hari Ghode Jatra dirayakan untuk menakut-nakuti Murkatta dan mencegah mata jahatnya mengenai anak-anak. Seorang penulis menyebut murkatta sebagai kata dalam bahasa Nepal untuk hantu tanpa kepala, dan nama sebuah dusun di dataran rendah Nepal tempat, kata orang, hantu yang membawa kepalanya di bawah lengan pernah berkeliaran.
long_description.en: In Kathmandu, a festival on the day of Ghode Jatra is celebrated to scare away the Murkatta and keep its evil eyes from children. One author notes murkatta as the Nepali word for a headless ghost, and as the name of a hamlet in the lowlands of Nepal where, people say, ghosts carrying their heads under their arms roamed.

short_description.id: Ningyo adalah makhluk dalam sastra Jepang dengan ciri manusia dan ikan.
short_description.en: Ningyo is a being in Japanese literature with human and fish traits.

long_description.id: Ningyo adalah makhluk dalam sastra Jepang dengan ciri manusia dan ikan. Terjemahan putri duyung tidak mencakup semua ningyo karena istilahnya tidak khusus perempuan. Nihon Shoki mencatat kisah penangkapan makhluk air tawar pada abad ketujuh.
long_description.en: Ningyo is a being in Japanese literature with human and fish traits. The translation mermaid is incomplete because the word is not limited to females. The Nihon Shoki records alleged captures of freshwater beings in the seventh century.

long_description.id: Contoh berikutnya umumnya menempatkan ningyo di air laut. Pada abad pertengahan, kemunculannya di pantai dianggap pertanda buruk. Pada zaman Edo, ada spesimen ningyo rakitan dari bagian ikan.
long_description.en: Later examples generally place ningyo in the sea. In medieval accounts, a ningyo stranded on shore was seen as an ill omen. In the Edo period, preserved ningyo specimens were made from fish parts.

long_description.id: Dalam penuturan lain, ningyo dari Samudra Pasifik dan Laut Jepang digambarkan mengerikan, berbeda dari putri duyung Atlantik dan Laut Tengah. Mereka lebih menyerupai ikan daripada manusia, dengan wajah mirip ikan yang cacat hingga torso manusia berjari panjang kurus dan bercakar tajam, dan ukurannya dari seukuran anak manusia hingga anjing laut besar.
long_description.en: In another account, ningyo from the Pacific Ocean and the Sea of Japan are described as hideous, unlike the mermaids of the Atlantic and Mediterranean. They are more fish than human, with faces that are deformed and fish-like or torsos with long bony fingers and sharp claws, and they range from the size of a human child to a large seal.

long_description.id: Daging ningyo dipercaya memberi umur panjang abadi dan kemudaan bagi yang memakannya, sehingga menjadi pokok banyak cerita rakyat. Namun ningyo dapat mengutuk manusia yang mencoba melukai atau menangkapnya, dan sebagian legenda menuturkan kota-kota tertelan gempa atau gelombang pasang setelah seorang nelayan membawa pulang ningyo. Sejak akhir zaman Edo, ningyo menyerupai putri duyung ala Barat menjadi populer di Jepang.
long_description.en: Eating ningyo flesh is believed to confer everlasting life and youth, which makes it a frequent theme in folk tales. Yet a ningyo can curse humans who try to wound or capture it, and some legends tell of towns swallowed by earthquakes or tidal waves after a fisherman brought one home. Since the end of the Edo period, ningyo resembling Western-style mermaids have become popular in Japan.

description.id: Dapat menjatuhkan kutukan kuat pada manusia yang mencoba melukai atau menangkapnya.
description.en: Can place a powerful curse on humans who try to wound or capture it.

claims.quote: Ningyo (人魚; "human fish"), is a creature with both human and fish-like features, described in various pieces of Japanese literature.

statement.id: Ningyo adalah makhluk dalam sastra Jepang dengan ciri manusia dan ikan.
statement.en: Ningyo is a being in Japanese literature with human and fish traits.

claims.quote: Though often translated as "mermaid", the term is technically not gender-specific and may include the "mermen".

statement.id: Terjemahan putri duyung tidak mencakup semua ningyo karena istilahnya tidak khusus perempuan.
statement.en: The translation mermaid is incomplete because the word is not limited to females.

claims.quote: The earliest records of the ningyo attested in written Japanese sources are freshwater beings allegedly captured in the 7th century (§Asuka period), documented later in the Nihon Shoki.

statement.id: Nihon Shoki mencatat kisah penangkapan makhluk air tawar pada abad ketujuh.
statement.en: The Nihon Shoki records alleged captures of freshwater beings in the seventh century.

claims.quote: But subsequent examples are usually seawater beings.

statement.id: Contoh berikutnya umumnya menempatkan ningyo di air laut.
statement.en: Later examples generally place ningyo in the sea.

claims.quote: In later medieval times (§Kamakura and Muromachi periods)), it was held to be a sign of ill omen, and its beaching (§Omens in Michinoku) was blamed for subsequent bloody battles or calamity.

statement.id: Pada abad pertengahan, kemunculannya di pantai dianggap pertanda buruk.
statement.en: In medieval accounts, a ningyo stranded on shore was seen as an ill omen.

claims.quote: There were also preserved ningyo being manufactured using fish parts (§Mummies or Feejee mermaids), and illustrated by some scholars of the period (e.g. §Baien gyofu); some such mummies are held by certain temples that have ningyo legend attached to them (cf. §Prince Shōtoku).

statement.id: Pada zaman Edo, ada spesimen ningyo rakitan dari bagian ikan.
statement.en: In the Edo period, preserved ningyo specimens were made from fish parts.

claims.quote: Unlike the mermaids of the Atlantic Ocean and Mediterranean Sea, ningyo from the Pacific Ocean and the Sea of Japan are hideous to behold.

statement.id: Berbeda dari putri duyung Samudra Atlantik dan Laut Tengah, ningyo dari Samudra Pasifik dan Laut Jepang digambarkan mengerikan untuk dilihat.
statement.en: Unlike the mermaids of the Atlantic Ocean and the Mediterranean Sea, ningyo from the Pacific Ocean and the Sea of Japan are described as hideous to behold.

claims.quote: Ningyo are more fish than human. They can have anything from ugly, deformed fish-like faces, to entire human torsos with long, bony fingers and sharp claws. Ningyo range in size from a human child to a large seal.

statement.id: Ningyo lebih menyerupai ikan daripada manusia: dari wajah mirip ikan yang buruk dan cacat hingga seluruh torso manusia dengan jari panjang kurus dan cakar tajam; ukurannya dari seukuran anak manusia hingga anjing laut besar.
statement.en: Ningyo are more fish than human, ranging from ugly, deformed fish-like faces to entire human torsos with long bony fingers and sharp claws, and in size from a human child to a large seal.

claims.quote: The flesh of a ningyo is believed to grant eternal life and youth to those who eat it, and thus it is the subject of many folk tales.

statement.id: Daging ningyo dipercaya memberi umur panjang abadi dan kemudaan bagi yang memakannya, sehingga menjadi pokok banyak cerita rakyat.
statement.en: The flesh of a ningyo is believed to grant eternal life and youth to those who eat it, and so features in many folk tales.

claims.quote: ningyo can place a powerful curse on humans who try to wound or capture them. Some legends tell of entire towns that were swallowed by earthquakes or tidal waves after a foolish fisherman brought home a ningyo in one of his catches.

statement.id: Ningyo dapat menjatuhkan kutukan kuat pada manusia yang mencoba melukai atau menangkapnya; sebagian legenda menuturkan seluruh kota tertelan gempa atau gelombang pasang setelah seorang nelayan membawa pulang ningyo hasil tangkapannya.
statement.en: Ningyo can lay a powerful curse on humans who try to wound or capture them; some legends tell of whole towns swallowed by earthquakes or tidal waves after a fisherman brought home a ningyo in his catch.

claims.quote: Since the end of the Edo period and the opening of Japan to the West, ningyo that resemble Western-style Atlantic mermaids have become popular in Japan.

statement.id: Sejak akhir zaman Edo dan pembukaan Jepang kepada Barat, ningyo yang menyerupai putri duyung ala Atlantik dari Barat menjadi populer di Jepang.
statement.en: Since the end of the Edo period and the opening of Japan to the West, ningyo resembling Western-style Atlantic mermaids have become popular in Japan.

short_description.id: Nittaewo adalah humanoid bertubuh kecil dalam mitologi Veddha dan cerita rakyat Sri Lanka.
short_description.en: Nittaewo are small humanoids of Veddha mythology and Sri Lankan folklore.

long_description.id: Nittaewo adalah humanoid bertubuh kecil dalam mitologi Veddha dan cerita rakyat Sri Lanka. Belum ditemukan bukti arkeologis yang memastikan keberadaan mereka. Menurut sebuah buku, mereka adalah ras kerdil yang dahulu tinggal di daerah Kattra-gam di Lenama.
long_description.en: Nittaewo are small humanoids of Veddha mythology and Sri Lankan folklore. No archaeological evidence has established their existence. According to one book they were a pigmy race that lived at one time in the Kattra-gam country of Lenama.

long_description.id: Mereka digambarkan berbulu dan memiliki tangan bercakar panjang. Mereka dikatakan selalu berjalan tegak dan tidak berekor. Cerita menempatkan mereka dalam kelompok kecil yang tidur di gua atau sarang daun di pohon. Veddha dikatakan menjadi musuh mereka, dengan busur dan panah yang tak mampu mereka lawan.
long_description.en: They are described as hairy with long-clawed hands. They are said to walk upright and lack tails. Tales place them in small groups sleeping in caves or leaf nests in trees. Veddha are said to be their enemies, armed with bows and arrows they cannot resist.

long_description.id: Mereka dikatakan tidak memakai perkakas dan membelah perut mangsa dengan cakar atau kuku melengkung, dan membelah perut Veddah yang sedang tidur. Menurut sebuah buku, mereka kanibal berbulu yang menyerang berkelompok dan hanya takut pada kerbau dan anjing. Nittaewo terakhir dikatakan dimusnahkan orang Veddah di Leanama pada akhir abad ke-18 dengan menggiring mereka ke sebuah gua yang pintunya ditutup semak kering lalu dibakar.
long_description.en: They are said to have used no tools and to have disembowelled prey with long claws or hooked nails, and to have disembowelled sleeping Veddahs. According to one book they were hairy cannibals that attacked in companies and were afraid only of the buffalo and the dog. Tradition holds that Veddahs at Leanama wiped out the last nittaewo late in the 18th century by driving them into a cave and setting brushwood alight at its mouth.

description.id: Nittaewo dikatakan menyerang berkelompok dan membelah perut mangsanya dengan cakar atau kuku panjang tanpa perkakas; dikatakan pula bahwa ketika menjumpai Veddah yang tidur, ia akan membelah perutnya.
description.en: The nittaewo were said to attack in companies and disembowel prey with long claws or nails without tools; it was also said that on finding a sleeping Veddah one would disembowel him.

summary.en: Late in the 18th century, it was said, Veddahs at Leanama wiped out the last nittaewo, driving them into a cave sealed with burning brushwood. Another source says the Veddas herded the last of them into a cave and destroyed them.

claims.quote: Nittaewo (or Nittevo) were said to be a small tribe of short-statured bigfoot or Yeti-like hominid cryptids native to Sri Lanka. No archeological evidence has been found to prove the existence of these humanoids, but they are ubiquitous in Veddha mythology and Sri Lankan folklore.

statement.en: No archaeological evidence has established their existence.

claims.quote: They were covered in hair, which was often said to be reddish in colour, and were said to have very short, powerful arms with short, long-clawed hands.
